sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: A passenger vehicle must have both a foot brake and a parking brake.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: How must the driver-side window operate on a Massachusetts passenger vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: The driver-side window must work and move upward and downward.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: Which three categories of exterior lights must every passenger vehicle carry?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: A passenger vehicle needs headlights, brake lights and directional signals.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: How many approved front lights and rear lights — and in what colors — are required for night driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: Night-driving equipment includes two approved white front headlights and two approved red rear lights.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: How many red rear brake lights and what license-plate light must a passenger vehicle have?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: A passenger vehicle needs three red rear brake lights and a small white light above the rear license plate.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: When directional signals or brake lights fail, how soon must you fix them — and how do you communicate meanwhile?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: Failed directional signals or brake lights must be repaired immediately, with hand signals used for turns or slowing until repair.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: How often must every Massachusetts vehicle pass a combined safety and emissions inspection?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: Every vehicle must pass a safety and emissions inspection each year.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: For which two narrow purposes may a passenger-vehicle spotlight be switched on?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: A passenger-vehicle spotlight may be used only to read signs or as an emergency light when the headlights fail.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: At thirty feet ahead of your car, how high above the pavement may a spotlight beam rise?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: A spotlight’s beam may be no higher than two feet above the roadway at a distance of thirty feet from the vehicle.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: What authorization is required before mounting flashing, rotating, oscillating, or strobe emergency lights?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: Flashing, rotating, oscillating or strobe emergency lights require an RMV permit.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: How dark may side and rear windows be tinted in Massachusetts, and what is the rule on windshield tinting?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: The manual allows side and rear window darkening up to thirty-five percent but prohibits windshield tinting.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: Which five visibility, medical, escape, and signaling items does the manual recommend packing in a vehicle safety kit?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: Recommended vehicle safety-kit items include a reflective vest, warning triangles or LED flares, first-aid supplies, a glass breaker and white and red breakdown cloths.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: Which four seasonal items does the manual recommend adding for cold and icy Massachusetts driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: The manual recommends winter tires, an ice scraper, jumper cables and extra warm clothing for cold and icy conditions.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: Where should you store your vehicle safety kit instead of burying it beneath heavy trunk cargo?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: A vehicle safety kit should be stored inside where the driver or passengers can reach it quickly.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: Who must wear a belt or child restraint in Massachusetts — including inside vans and small trucks under what weight?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: Massachusetts requires every occupant of a passenger vehicle, including a van or small truck under eighteen thousand pounds, to use a safety belt or child restraint unless exempt.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: What dollar fine can an unbelted driver receive in Massachusetts?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: An unbelted driver can receive a twenty-five-dollar fine.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: Starting at what age does an unbelted passenger personally face their own twenty-five-dollar fine?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: An unbelted passenger age sixteen or older can receive a twenty-five-dollar fine.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: For which passenger age bracket does the DRIVER get fined twenty-five dollars per unbelted rider?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: The driver can be fined twenty-five dollars for each unbelted passenger from age twelve through fifteen.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: When may Massachusetts police issue a safety-belt fine?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: A safety-belt fine may be issued only when the vehicle has been stopped for a traffic violation.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: Vehicles built before which month and year are exempt from this Massachusetts safety-belt requirement?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: Occupants of vehicles manufactured before July nineteen sixty-six are exempt from the safety-belt requirement described here.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.front: Which five commercial or heavy-vehicle driver categories appear on the belt-exemption list — and at what truck weight?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.expected_back: The listed belt exceptions include drivers of taxis, liveries, tractors, buses and trucks weighing at least eighteen thousand pounds, although some commercial drivers must still wear belts.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.front: Which emergency-vehicle occupants and drivers appear on Massachusetts's seat-belt exemption list?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.expected_back: The listed belt exceptions include emergency-vehicle passengers and police-vehicle and fire-vehicle drivers.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.front: When is a postal employee exempt from the Massachusetts safety-belt rule?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.expected_back: A postal employee driving while working is exempt from the safety-belt requirement described here.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.front: What documentation must a person carry if a disability makes wearing a safety belt physically impossible?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.expected_back: A person physically unable to wear a belt because of a disability needs physician certification for the disability exemption.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.front: Until reaching EITHER what age OR what height in inches must a child ride in a federally approved child restraint?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.expected_back: An infant or small child must use a federally approved child restraint until reaching either eight years of age or fifty-seven inches in height.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.front: What is required once a child reaches age eight or fifty-seven inches tall?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.expected_back: Correct belt use is required once a child reaches eight years of age or a height of fifty-seven inches.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.front: What fine applies for violating the Massachusetts child-restraint law?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.expected_back: A violation of the child-restraint law can result in a twenty-five-dollar fine.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.front: What proof of safety testing must appear directly on any legal child restraint?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.expected_back: A child restraint must bear a sticker showing compliance with the federal child-restraint standard.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.front: How must a child restraint be anchored inside the vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.expected_back: A child restraint must be permanently secured to the vehicle or attached using a safety belt or attachment system.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.front: Where must you NEVER install a rear-facing child seat?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.expected_back: A rear-facing child seat must never be placed in the front passenger position when that position has an air bag.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.front: Which row is safest for children, and which specific seating spot in that row is best?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.expected_back: The manual identifies the rear seat as the safest place for a child and the rear center seat as best.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.front: Which direction must an infant car seat always face?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.expected_back: An infant seat must face toward the rear of the vehicle.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.front: Which two measurements of the child — paired with what product specs — govern child-seat selection?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.expected_back: Child-seat selection should use the child’s height and weight and the seat manufacturer’s exact limits.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: What three pound bands appear in the manual's illustrative seat guide — and what rule overrides rough examples?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: The manual’s illustrative seat guide lists infant seats up to twenty pounds, toddler convertible seats from twenty to forty pounds and boosters from forty to eighty pounds, alongside its instruction to follow each seat’s actual manufacturer limits.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: Which two deadly crash motions do safety belts prevent?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: Safety belts help prevent occupants from being thrown around inside the vehicle or ejected during a crash.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: How should you wear a two-part lap-and-shoulder safety belt?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: The manual recommends wearing both the lap belt and shoulder belt.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: Which cabin surfaces — and who else inside — does a seat belt keep your body from striking?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: A belt restrains the body during a crash so it is less likely to strike the windshield, dashboard, steering wheel, another hard surface or another occupant.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: How does wearing a safety belt help the driver steer or brake through a swerve or glancing hit?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: A safety belt helps the driver stay seated behind the steering wheel and retain control rather than being pushed across the seat.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: Where on your body — and in what condition — does the lap belt belong?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: The lap belt belongs low and snug across the hips without twists.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: Across which two body parts must the shoulder belt lie — and which three placements are wrong?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: The shoulder belt belongs across the chest and shoulder rather than under the arm or over the face or neck.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: Why does wearing a seat belt actually IMPROVE your odds of escaping a burning or sinking car?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: A safety belt can help prevent a head injury and loss of consciousness that would make escape from a burning or sinking vehicle harder.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.front: Does having airbags replace the need to buckle your safety belt?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.expected_back: An air bag is designed to work with safety belts and does not replace them.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.front: For which crash direction are front airbags built — and which two impact types leave you relying on belts?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.expected_back: Front air bags are designed for frontal crashes and do not protect occupants in side or rear impacts.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.front: What specific danger does an unbelted adult pose to children or small pets during a crash?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.expected_back: Children and small pets can be crushed by an unbelted adult during a crash.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.front: What two factors determine the right child seat for an infant or young child?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.expected_back: Infants and young children need child seats suited to their age and size.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.front: How should the driver and front passenger position their seats relative to the dashboard?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.expected_back: The driver and front passenger should move their seats as far back from the dashboard as they can.

sec05-card-sec05-R14.front: Which three core driving tasks must items inside your car never interfere with?
sec05-card-sec05-R14.expected_back: Objects inside the vehicle must not interfere with seeing, reacting or driving.

sec05-card-sec05-R15.front: Where must dashboard items, windshield mounts, or hanging mirror objects never block your sightline?
sec05-card-sec05-R15.expected_back: Items on the dashboard, windshield or mirror must not block the forward road view or the view through the mirrors.

sec05-card-sec05-R16.front: Why must loose floor items be secured away from the driver's footwell?
sec05-card-sec05-R16.expected_back: Loose objects must be kept from rolling beneath the driver’s feet and interfering with the pedals.

sec05-card-sec05-R17.front: What is Massachusetts's rule on wearing headphones, a headset, or attention-limiting wired or wireless gear while driving?
sec05-card-sec05-R17.expected_back: A headset, headphones or another wired or wireless device that limits attention to the surroundings is illegal while driving.

sec05-card-sec05-R18.front: Who may legally wear ONE earplug with a cell phone while driving in Massachusetts?
sec05-card-sec05-R18.expected_back: A driver age eighteen or older may use one earplug with a cell phone.

sec05-card-sec05-R19.front: What practical benchmark sets the maximum safe stereo volume inside your vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-R19.expected_back: Keep in-vehicle sound low enough to hear emergency-vehicle sirens.

sec05-card-sec05-R20.front: Where must any television screen installed inside a vehicle sit?
sec05-card-sec05-R20.expected_back: A vehicle television must be behind the front seat and out of the driver’s view.

sec05-card-sec05-R21.front: Does the ban on television distraction apply even to a screen visible through another car's window?
sec05-card-sec05-R21.expected_back: A driver must not be distracted by a television screen, including a screen viewed through a side window.

sec05-card-sec05-R22.front: Under what age are children barred from pickup beds — and what speed ceiling caps the rare statutory exceptions?
sec05-card-sec05-R22.expected_back: Children younger than twelve generally cannot ride in a pickup bed, and the very limited exceptions never allow speeds above five miles per hour.

sec05-card-sec05-R23.front: What blanket rule applies to handheld mobile electronic devices while driving in Massachusetts?
sec05-card-sec05-R23.expected_back: Massachusetts prohibits handheld mobile-electronic-device use while driving.

sec05-card-sec05-R24.front: Starting at what age may a Massachusetts driver use a mobile electronic device — and in what mode only?
sec05-card-sec05-R24.expected_back: Drivers age eighteen and older may use a mobile electronic device while driving only in hands-free mode.

sec05-card-sec05-R25.front: When may an adult touch a phone while driving, and how must the phone be positioned?
sec05-card-sec05-R25.expected_back: A driver may touch a device only to activate hands-free operation, and the device must be mounted without interfering with driving.

sec05-card-sec05-R26.front: May you pick up your phone while stopped at a red light or stop sign — or where must you be?
sec05-card-sec05-R26.expected_back: Handheld device use is allowed only while stationary outside a public travel lane, not while stopped at a red light or stop sign.

sec05-card-sec05-R27.front: Should you pull onto the shoulder of a busy road or highway just to check your phone?
sec05-card-sec05-R27.expected_back: A driver should not stop on the shoulder of a busy road or highway to use a mobile device.

sec05-card-sec05-R28.front: Which four text and web actions on a mobile device are banned while driving?
sec05-card-sec05-R28.expected_back: A driver may not use a mobile electronic device to compose, send or read messages or access the internet while driving.

sec05-card-sec05-R29.front: What installation rule lets you use a GPS unit or phone map app for navigation while driving?
sec05-card-sec05-R29.expected_back: A navigation device or navigation-enabled phone may be used when temporarily or permanently affixed in the vehicle for navigation assistance.

sec05-card-sec05-R30.front: What is the ONLY situation in which a driver under eighteen may use ANY mobile electronic device while driving?
sec05-card-sec05-R30.expected_back: A driver younger than eighteen may use a mobile electronic device while driving only to report an emergency.

sec05-card-sec05-R31.front: Which five portable gadget types count as mobile devices — and which four installed or audio systems are excluded?
sec05-card-sec05-R31.expected_back: The mobile-device definition includes portable communications, gaming, video, photography and television-receiving equipment, while excluding audio equipment and installed navigation, emergency-assistance or rear-seat video equipment as specified.

sec05-card-sec05-R32.front: What penalty hits a driver for a FIRST Massachusetts handheld-device offense?
sec05-card-sec05-R32.expected_back: A first handheld-device driving offense carries a one-hundred-dollar fine.

sec05-card-sec05-R33.front: What dollar fine AND mandatory requirement hit on a SECOND handheld-device offense?
sec05-card-sec05-R33.expected_back: A second handheld-device driving offense carries a two-hundred-fifty-dollar fine and a mandatory distracted-driving education program.

sec05-card-sec05-R34.front: Which three penalties stack on a THIRD or subsequent handheld-device offense?
sec05-card-sec05-R34.expected_back: A third or later handheld-device driving offense carries a five-hundred-dollar fine, an insurance surcharge and a mandatory distracted-driving program.

sec05-card-sec05-R35.front: When does negligent phone-distracted driving become a crime — and what two severe consequences can follow a crash?
sec05-card-sec05-R35.expected_back: Negligent driving that injures a person or damages property is a crime, and a mobile-device-related crash can bring criminal charges and loss of license.

sec05-card-sec05-R36.front: Which three pre-drive steps does the manual suggest to kill phone temptation completely?
sec05-card-sec05-R36.expected_back: Turning off notifications, silencing the phone and placing it in the rear seat can help prevent phone use while driving.

sec05-card-sec05-R37.front: When a call or text genuinely cannot wait, where should you pull over — and what spot should you avoid?
sec05-card-sec05-R37.expected_back: If phone use is necessary, pull into a safe place rather than stopping beside a busy road or highway.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: What kind of windshield-washer fluid should you keep topped off for Massachusetts winter driving?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: Keep windshield-washer fluid filled with a type that will not freeze.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: Which three emergency items does Massachusetts recommend keeping in your trunk for winter trips?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: Carry a blanket, flashlight and small shovel in the trunk for winter travel.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: What license plate type is required on a truck used to plow snow for pay?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: A truck used to plow for compensation must have commercial plates.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: Alongside pedestrians, bicyclists, and roadside workers, which animal-related travelers count as Massachusetts vulnerable road users?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: Massachusetts vulnerable road users include pedestrians, roadside workers, bicyclists and people riding horses or horse-drawn carriages.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: Which small wheeled or mobility devices fall inside Massachusetts's vulnerable-road-user definition?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: The vulnerable-road-user definition includes people using wheelchairs, personal mobility devices, motorized bicycles, motorized or nonmotorized scooters, skateboards and roller skates.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: At least how many feet of clearance must you leave when passing any vulnerable road user in Massachusetts?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: Leave at least four feet of safe clearance when passing a vulnerable road user.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: May you cross the center line or use an adjacent lane to give a vulnerable user passing room, and what speed rule still applies?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: When safe, a driver passing a vulnerable road user may use the adjacent lane and cross the center line if needed, while still obeying the speed limit.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: What common personal tech habits require extra scanning for pedestrians near the street?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: Look carefully for pedestrians who may be distracted by a phone or headphones.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: Why must you use heightened caution around schools, parks, bus stops, and playgrounds?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: Be especially cautious of children near schools, parks, bus stops and playgrounds because they can be unpredictable and hard to see.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: What assumption should you avoid making when joggers or skaters approach a crosswalk or signal?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: Do not assume joggers or skaters will obey traffic signals or crosswalk rules.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: What should you check before getting into your vehicle to back up?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: Before entering the vehicle to back up, look behind it for children or animals.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: Instead of trusting mirrors or backup sensors alone, how should you look while reversing?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: When reversing, turn your head and look through the window rather than relying only on mirrors or sensors.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: What must you do when a blind pedestrian is crossing the street ahead of you?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: Stop completely for a blind pedestrian crossing the street and remain stopped until the person is safely across.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: Which three actions are forbidden when you encounter a blind pedestrian or a car stopped for one?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: Do not honk at a blind pedestrian, wave the person across or pass a vehicle stopped for that crossing.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: Which two mobility aids identify a blind pedestrian at a street crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: A blind pedestrian may use a white cane or a guide dog.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: Why must you never assume a pedestrian or cyclist hears your vehicle approaching and will step aside?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: A person’s deafness or hearing loss cannot be recognized just by looking, so never assume a road user hears your vehicle and will move.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: When claiming your technical right of way would create a dangerous situation, what should you do?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: Yielding is safer than insisting on right of way when that would create a dangerous condition.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: Why should you scan with extra focus around train stations and bus stops?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: Watch closely near train and bus stops because they may have more pedestrian traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: Why do streets near senior centers and older-adult residences call for extra patience and care?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: Use extra care near senior centers and residences because older pedestrians may have reduced vision, hearing, mobility or reaction speed.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: Where might pedestrians walking in the roadway be hidden from your view as you approach?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: Slow and stop when needed for someone walking in the street, and look for people concealed by curves, hilltops or parked vehicles.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.front: On which Massachusetts roadways are bicycles and mopeds barred from riding?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.expected_back: Bicycles and mopeds have a right to use public roadways except limited-access or express state highways where signs prohibit them.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.front: Do traffic-control devices and right-of-way laws apply to bicycle and moped riders?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.expected_back: Bicycle and moped riders must obey traffic-control and right-of-way rules.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.front: Which three everyday driver slip-ups can badly hurt a passing bicycle or moped rider?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.expected_back: Distraction, lane drift or opening a door without looking can seriously injure a bicycle or moped rider.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.front: Why should you ease off the gas when passing a bicycle or moped even if you have clearance?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.expected_back: Slow when passing a bicycle or moped because vehicle-generated wind can upset the rider’s balance.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.front: What must you do when oncoming traffic or a narrow lane prevents passing a bicycle or moped with safe room?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.expected_back: If a bicycle or moped cannot be passed with enough room, wait until oncoming traffic clears or the lane widens.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.front: What headlight adjustment must you make for an oncoming bicyclist after dark?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.expected_back: Dim headlights for an approaching bicyclist at night.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.front: What sudden movement should you always anticipate when trailing or passing a bicycle or moped?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.expected_back: Be prepared for a bicycle or moped rider to swerve unexpectedly.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.front: What check is essential before swinging open a parked vehicle's street-side door?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.expected_back: Check for bicycles and mopeds before opening a vehicle door beside the road.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.front: How do a motorcycle's roadway rights compare with those of a car or truck?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.expected_back: A motorcycle is a motor vehicle with the same roadway rights as a car or truck.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.front: During which two common maneuvers must drivers look especially carefully for approaching motorcycles?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.expected_back: Watch for motorcycles when entering traffic or turning left across traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.front: What three-part routine should you follow before merging or changing lanes near motorcycles?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.expected_back: Before changing lanes or merging, signal early and check mirrors and blind spots twice for motorcycles.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.front: How many seconds of following distance should you keep behind a motorcycle instead of the usual three-second gap?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.expected_back: Use a four-second following interval behind a motorcycle rather than the three-second interval used for other motor vehicles.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.front: May a car squeeze alongside a motorcycle within the same traffic lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.expected_back: A motorcycle is entitled to the entire lane, and another vehicle must not share its lane space.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.front: Why might a motorcyclist move from one side of their lane to the other without changing lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.expected_back: A motorcycle rider may need to shift within the lane to avoid debris, potholes or oil.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.front: When is a motorcycle allowed to weave between lanes of traffic in Massachusetts?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.expected_back: Motorcycle weaving between lanes is illegal at any time.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: If a lane is extra wide and a motorcyclist rides near one edge, may you pull up into the open half?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: Do not crowd a motorcycle’s lane even when the lane is wide and the rider is using only one side.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: When turning left with a motorcycle approaching from the opposite direction, when should you make your turn?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: Let an approaching motorcycle clear an intersection before turning left across its path.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: How does a motorcycle's compact profile affect what other drivers see in traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: A motorcycle’s small size can hide it behind other vehicles and make its speed or location difficult to judge.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: How can loose gravel, potholes, or slick pavement affect a motorcycle ahead of you?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: Gravel, potholes and slippery pavement may cause a motorcycle to change direction or speed suddenly.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: How should you adjust your space behind a motorcycle during rain or bad weather?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: Give motorcycles additional stopping room in bad weather in case they must stop abruptly.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: What transmission, maximum engine size, and top speed capability define a moped in Massachusetts?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: A moped may be a pedal bicycle with an assisting motor or a nonpedal bicycle with a motor, and must have an automatic transmission, engine capacity no greater than fifty cubic centimeters and maximum capability no greater than thirty miles per hour.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: What credential must you hold to legally ride a moped on Massachusetts roads?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: Operating a moped requires a valid driver license of any class or a learner permit.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: Even if a moped's design cap is thirty miles per hour, what is the fastest speed you may legally drive one?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: A moped may not be driven faster than twenty-five miles per hour.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.front: Which high-speed highways are off-limits to moped operators?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.expected_back: Mopeds are prohibited on limited-access or express state highways posted against bicycles.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.front: What signaling methods must a moped operator use before turning or stopping?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.expected_back: A moped operator must use the correct electronic and hand signals before stopping or turning.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.front: How does Massachusetts treat mopeds on roadside bike lanes compared with off-street recreational paths?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.expected_back: Mopeds may use roadside bicycle lanes but not off-street recreational paths.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.front: Who on a moped must wear a helmet, and what safety standard must it meet?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.expected_back: Moped operators and passengers must wear helmets meeting or exceeding the United States Department of Transportation standard.

sec07-card-sec07-R13.front: May a moped rider who holds only a learner permit carry a passenger?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.expected_back: A moped operator using a learner permit may not carry a passenger.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.front: Up to how much can a rider be fined for breaking Massachusetts's listed moped operating rules?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.expected_back: Violating the listed moped rules can bring a fine of up to one hundred dollars.

sec07-card-sec07-R15.front: How many wheels, what steering setup, and what power or riding posture define a Massachusetts motorized scooter?
sec07-card-sec07-R15.expected_back: A motorized scooter has two or three wheels, handlebars and an electric or gasoline motor, and may be designed for a standing or seated operator.

sec07-card-sec07-R16.front: Does the Massachusetts RMV register motorized scooters?
sec07-card-sec07-R16.expected_back: The RMV does not register motorized scooters.

sec07-card-sec07-R17.front: What credential do you need before riding a motorized scooter on public roads?
sec07-card-sec07-R17.expected_back: A motorized-scooter operator needs a valid driver license of any class or a learner permit.

sec07-card-sec07-R18.front: What is the top legal speed for a motorized scooter, and which highways can it never use?
sec07-card-sec07-R18.expected_back: Motorized scooters may not exceed twenty miles per hour or travel on limited-access or express state highways.

sec07-card-sec07-R19.front: What helmet requirement applies when operating a motorized scooter?
sec07-card-sec07-R19.expected_back: A motorized-scooter rider must wear a helmet meeting or exceeding the federal transportation standard.

sec07-card-sec07-R20.front: Where on the roadway must a motorized-scooter rider stay, even while passing another vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-R20.expected_back: A motorized-scooter operator must stay on the road’s right side even when passing another vehicle.

sec07-card-sec07-R21.front: How must a motorized-scooter operator signal before slowing to stop or turning?
sec07-card-sec07-R21.expected_back: A motorized-scooter operator must use the correct electronic and hand signals before stopping or turning.

sec07-card-sec07-R22.front: During what hours of the day is operating a motorized scooter illegal?
sec07-card-sec07-R22.expected_back: A motorized scooter may not be operated before sunrise or after sunset.

sec07-card-sec07-R23.front: When may a motorized scooter carry a passenger in Massachusetts?
sec07-card-sec07-R23.expected_back: A motorized scooter may not carry passengers.

sec07-card-sec07-R24.front: How do fines escalate across first, second, and later motorized-scooter rule violations?
sec07-card-sec07-R24.expected_back: The listed scooter-rule fines are up to twenty-five dollars for a first offense, twenty-five to fifty dollars for a second and fifty to one hundred dollars for later offenses.

sec07-card-sec07-R25.front: What top-speed bracket defines a limited-use vehicle, and what decides whether it counts as a motorcycle or passenger car?
sec07-card-sec07-R25.expected_back: A limited-use vehicle can exceed thirty miles per hour but cannot exceed forty, and its wheel count determines whether it is classed as a motorcycle or passenger vehicle.

sec07-card-sec07-R26.front: Which license class is needed for a passenger-type limited-use vehicle versus a motorcycle-type one?
sec07-card-sec07-R26.memory_hook: Class D passenger, Class M bike
sec07-card-sec07-R26.expected_back: A passenger-type limited-use vehicle requires a Class D license or permit, while a motorcycle-type limited-use vehicle requires Class M.

sec07-card-sec07-R27.front: Which highways and speed-limit zones are off-limits to a limited-use vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-R27.expected_back: A limited-use vehicle cannot travel on limited-access or express state highways or roads with a speed limit above forty miles per hour.

sec07-card-sec07-R28.front: What wheel count, weight rating, and speed range define a Massachusetts low-speed vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-R28.expected_back: A low-speed vehicle has four wheels, a gross weight rating below three thousand pounds and a speed capability between twenty and twenty-five miles per hour.

sec07-card-sec07-R29.front: What license or permit is required to drive a four-wheeled low-speed vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-R29.expected_back: A low-speed vehicle operator needs a valid Class D license or learner permit.

sec07-card-sec07-R30.front: Which highways and posted speed limits ban low-speed vehicles?
sec07-card-sec07-R30.expected_back: A low-speed vehicle cannot use limited-access or express state highways or roads with limits above thirty miles per hour.

sec07-card-sec07-R31.front: Beyond thirty-mile-per-hour caps, where else can low-speed vehicles be barred, and how do traffic laws apply?
sec07-card-sec07-R31.expected_back: Low-speed vehicles may also be prohibited in heavily trafficked areas and must obey traffic laws.

sec07-card-sec07-R32.front: If police cite a bicyclist for a traffic violation, how does that fine affect the rider's Massachusetts driving record?
sec07-card-sec07-R32.expected_back: A police officer may cite a bicyclist for a traffic violation, but the fine does not affect the bicyclist’s driving record.

sec07-card-sec07-R33.front: What must a stopped bicyclist tell police when asked, and what happens for lying versus refusing a name?
sec07-card-sec07-R33.expected_back: A bicyclist must give an officer their true name and address when asked, can be fined for failing to do so and can be arrested for refusing to give a name.

sec07-card-sec07-R34.front: What safety gear must a bicycle-rental business offer to customers?
sec07-card-sec07-R34.expected_back: A bicycle-rental company must offer renters helmets that meet safety requirements.

sec07-card-sec07-R35.front: What consequence can a motorist face for breaking passing or safety rules around bicyclists?
sec07-card-sec07-R35.expected_back: A motorist may receive a traffic citation for prohibited behavior around bicycles.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: Which three categories of driving events get logged onto your Massachusetts RMV driving record?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: The RMV driving record tracks civil motor-vehicle infractions, criminal violations and crashes with more than fifty percent fault.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: How long do a Massachusetts license suspension or revocation take away your right to drive?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: A suspension or revocation removes driving privileges for a fixed period or indefinitely.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: Which unpaid bills or court matters block you from renewing an expired Massachusetts driver license?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: An expired license cannot be renewed while listed unpaid parking, excise-tax or toll obligations or outstanding court warrants remain.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: What four outcomes can result from receiving a Massachusetts motor-vehicle citation?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: A motor-vehicle citation may lead to a fine, loss of driving privileges, a court appearance or imprisonment.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: Which two serious driving violations does the manual highlight as criminal motor-vehicle offenses?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: Driving under the influence and leaving a crash scene are examples of criminal motor-vehicle offenses.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: What can happen to your license if you rack up repeated violations like speeding or running traffic signals?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: Repeated violations such as speeding or disobeying traffic signals can cause loss of a license.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: Which three driver factors make penalties steeper across many Massachusetts traffic violations?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: Junior status, age below twenty-one and repeat offenses can increase penalties for many violations.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: Can one motor-vehicle offense trigger only one type of punishment, or several at once?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: A single motor-vehicle offense can carry multiple penalties, including a fine, license loss and imprisonment.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: How is a civil motor-vehicle infraction classified legally, and how is it usually settled?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: A civil motor-vehicle infraction is noncriminal and can usually be resolved by paying its fine.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: How many days do you have after getting a civil citation to either pay it or request a court hearing?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: A driver receiving a civil citation has twenty days to pay or request a hearing to contest it.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: What extra surcharge gets tacked onto civil fines under Massachusetts General Laws chapters eighty-nine or ninety?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: Civil fines under Massachusetts General Laws chapters eighty-nine or ninety receive an additional five-dollar public-safety surcharge.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: What filing fee does the RMV charge when you request a hearing to fight a civil citation?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: Requesting a civil-citation hearing requires a twenty-five-dollar RMV filing fee.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: Under what exact outcome is your twenty-five-dollar civil-hearing filing fee refunded?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: The hearing filing fee is refunded when the court finds the driver not responsible for every violation on the civil citation.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: What happens if you neither pay nor contest a civil citation within twenty days?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: Failure to respond to a civil citation within twenty days results in responsibility and a substantial late fee.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: What happens to your license if you still fail to pay a civil citation and its added late fee?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: Failure to pay a civil citation and its late fee causes license suspension.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: What three events put a finding of responsibility onto your driving record for a civil ticket?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: Paying a civil fine accepts responsibility, and responsibility also appears on the record after a court orders payment or the driver fails to respond within twenty days.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: Which agency logs Massachusetts moving violations, and what two major consequences can follow?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: The RMV records Massachusetts moving violations, which can increase insurance rates and lead to license suspension.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: Who administers parking tickets in Massachusetts instead of treating them as civil motor-vehicle infractions?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: Parking violations are handled by the issuing municipality rather than as civil motor-vehicle infractions.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: Which two RMV renewals get blocked when you leave municipal parking tickets unpaid?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: Unpaid parking violations block renewal of the driver license or vehicle registration.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: What is the minimum penalty amount for a speeding ticket in Massachusetts?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: The minimum speeding penalty is a one-hundred-dollar fine plus a five-dollar public-safety surcharge.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: How is a Massachusetts speeding fine calculated once you exceed the speed limit by more than ten miles per hour?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: For speed more than ten miles per hour above the limit, an extra ten dollars is charged for each mile per hour beyond that first ten.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: In the Driver's Manual example, what total fine applies for driving seventy-three in a fifty-five-mile-per-hour zone?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: The manual illustrates a total fine of one hundred eighty-five dollars for seventy-three miles per hour in a fifty-five-mile-per-hour zone.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: How much of every Massachusetts speeding fine goes to the Head Injury Treatment Services Trust Fund?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: Every speeding fine includes a fifty-dollar surcharge directed to the Head Injury Treatment Services Trust Fund.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: How does speeding inside a posted highway work zone change your fine?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: Speeding in a posted work zone doubles the speeding fine.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: What license penalty hits a driver who racks up three speeding findings within twelve months?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: Three speeding findings within twelve months cause a thirty-day license suspension.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: How long is a Junior Operator suspended after a first speeding offense versus a second or later one?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: A Junior Operator’s first speeding offense causes a ninety-day suspension, and later offenses cause a one-year suspension.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: What four immediate roadside actions can happen when you commit a criminal motor-vehicle offense?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: A criminal motor-vehicle offense can result in immediate arrest, towing, license seizure and detention until court.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: Who decides the fine or prison sentence after a conviction for a criminal motor-vehicle offense?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: After conviction of a criminal motor-vehicle offense, the court sets the fine or prison sentence.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.front: Along with impaired driving and leaving a crash, what third major offense is listed as a criminal driving crime?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.expected_back: Driving with a suspended license, driving under the influence and leaving a crash scene are criminal motor-vehicle offenses.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.front: What can happen if you refuse to tell an officer your name and address or the vehicle owner's name and address?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.expected_back: Refusing to give an officer the driver’s or vehicle owner’s name and address may lead to arrest and criminal charges.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.front: What happens if you refuse to hand over your license or registration, or refuse to sign your name for an officer?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.expected_back: Refusing to show the driver license or valid vehicle registration, or to sign in front of the officer, may lead to arrest and criminal charges.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.front: How do traffic violations committed in other states affect your Massachusetts driving record?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.expected_back: Out-of-state motor-vehicle violations affect the Massachusetts driving record as though committed in Massachusetts.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.front: What happens in Massachusetts if you ignore a ticket payment or court date in another state?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.expected_back: Failure to pay or appear for an out-of-state violation affects Massachusetts license status and operating privileges.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.front: Whose suspension rules apply to an out-of-state violation, and how can they compare with the other state's penalty?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.expected_back: Massachusetts applies its own suspension penalties to out-of-state violations, and its penalty can be stricter than the other state’s.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: What two things must you provide to get reinstated after a suspension caused by an unresolved out-of-state ticket?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: Reinstatement after an out-of-state obligation suspension requires proof of resolution and a Massachusetts reinstatement fee of at least one hundred dollars.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: What standard does an insurer apply as part of determining whether a crash counts as at-fault?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: The at-fault crash test includes an insurer finding under a listed fault standard, such as driving on the wrong side or striking a vehicle from behind.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: Above what insurer-payout dollar mark does an at-fault collision or lone bodily-injury claim trigger a surchargeable crash?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: The additional insurer-payment condition is more than one thousand dollars for collision, limited collision or another person’s property damage, or more than one thousand dollars for bodily injury when the same incident lacks collision or property damage above that amount.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: How does the RMV treat charged at-fault crashes alongside traffic tickets on your record?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: Charged at-fault crashes are entered on the driving record and count with violations toward possible suspension.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: Which two broad categories make up Massachusetts surchargeable events?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: Motor-vehicle violations and at-fault crashes are surchargeable events that count toward possible suspension.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: What exact event starts the twelve-month countdown for the three-speeding-tickets suspension rule?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: The twelve-month window for three speeding violations begins when the driver pays or is found guilty of the first citation.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: How long is a Junior Operator's license suspended for a first drag-racing citation versus a repeat citation?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: A first Junior Operator drag-racing citation causes a one-year suspension, while a later citation causes a three-year suspension.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: What happens if you accumulate three surchargeable events within two years, and how fast must you act?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: Three surchargeable events in two years require driver retraining, which must be completed within ninety days to avoid suspension until completion.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: What automatic penalty kicks in when a driver hits seven surchargeable events within three years?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: Seven surchargeable events within three years cause an automatic sixty-day suspension.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: Which Massachusetts board runs the Safe Driver Insurance Plan that links driving records to insurance premiums?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: The Merit Rating Board administers the Safe Driver Insurance Plan, which uses driving records to determine insurance premiums.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.front: Under the Safe Driver Insurance Plan, what pushes your insurance rate up and what can bring it down?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.expected_back: Moving-violation convictions or crash fault above fifty percent increase the insurance rate under the described plan, while safe driving may reduce it.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.front: What does the Massachusetts Driver Retraining Course target instead of hands-on steering and braking skills?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.expected_back: The Massachusetts Driver Retraining Course addresses driving behavior rather than teaching vehicle-driving skills.

sec08-card-sec08-R13.front: What does the RMV mail you once your record hits at least three surchargeable events?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.expected_back: After notice of at least three surchargeable events, the RMV sends a packet explaining retraining, fees and enrollment.

sec08-card-sec08-R14.front: How many total hours is the Massachusetts driver-retraining program, and how are sessions scheduled?
sec08-card-sec08-R14.expected_back: The driver-retraining program lasts eight hours, usually as two four-hour meetings, with a single Saturday meeting sometimes available.

sec08-card-sec08-R15.front: Does finishing driver retraining wipe surcharges off your record or substitute for other mandatory courses?
sec08-card-sec08-R15.expected_back: Completing driver retraining does not erase offenses or surcharges from the driving record and does not replace other required programs.

sec08-card-sec08-R16.front: If you strike a stationary parked car that was parked illegally, how do Massachusetts fault standards treat the crash?
sec08-card-sec08-R16.expected_back: Collision with a parked vehicle is one of the listed fault standards, whether that vehicle was lawfully or unlawfully parked.

sec08-card-sec08-R17.front: How do Massachusetts insurer fault standards classify striking the back of the vehicle ahead of you?
sec08-card-sec08-R17.expected_back: A rear-end collision is one of the listed fault standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R18.front: What fault status applies when a crash happens because a driver drifts or cuts outside their marked lane?
sec08-card-sec08-R18.expected_back: An out-of-lane collision is one of the listed fault standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R19.front: How do Massachusetts fault rules treat a crash tied to turning or changing lanes without signaling?
sec08-card-sec08-R19.expected_back: Failure to signal is one of the listed fault standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R20.front: What fault rule applies if you pull out from a traffic light or stop sign without checking that the way is clear?
sec08-card-sec08-R20.expected_back: Failure to proceed cautiously from a traffic signal or sign is one of the listed fault standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R21.front: How do insurer fault standards treat a collision that occurs while your vehicle is on the wrong side of the road?
sec08-card-sec08-R21.expected_back: A collision on the wrong side of the road is one of the listed fault standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R22.front: What fault consequence follows crashing while driving the wrong way down a roadway or ramp?
sec08-card-sec08-R22.expected_back: Traveling in the wrong direction is one of the listed fault standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R23.front: Does Massachusetts include crashes at intersections without signals or signs among its preset insurer fault standards?
sec08-card-sec08-R23.expected_back: A collision at an uncontrolled intersection is one of the listed fault standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R24.front: How is blame treated under Massachusetts fault standards when a crash happens while you are backing up?
sec08-card-sec08-R24.expected_back: A collision while backing is one of the listed fault standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R25.front: How do insurer fault standards treat a crash during a left turn or U-turn across another vehicle's path?
sec08-card-sec08-R25.expected_back: A collision during a left turn or U-turn across another vehicle’s travel path is one of the listed fault standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R26.front: What fault rule applies when pulling out from a curb space, parking lot, alley, or private driveway causes a crash?
sec08-card-sec08-R26.expected_back: Leaving a parked position, parking lot, alley or driveway is one of the listed fault standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R27.front: If opening your car door or leaving it open into traffic causes a collision, how is fault assigned?
sec08-card-sec08-R27.expected_back: Opening or having opened a vehicle door is one of the listed fault standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R28.front: If no other driver is involved and you crash into a guardrail, tree, or ditch, how do fault standards treat it?
sec08-card-sec08-R28.expected_back: A single-vehicle collision is one of the listed fault standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R29.front: How do Massachusetts fault standards treat a collision caused by breaking general driving rules and regulations?
sec08-card-sec08-R29.expected_back: Failure to obey driving rules and regulations is one of the listed fault standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R30.front: What fault standard covers a crash involving an unattended vehicle, such as one that rolls away?
sec08-card-sec08-R30.expected_back: An unattended-vehicle collision is one of the listed fault standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R31.front: How do insurer fault standards treat a crash that happens while you merge onto a highway or enter a rotary?
sec08-card-sec08-R31.expected_back: A collision while merging onto a highway or into a rotary is one of the listed fault standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R32.front: Can you be found majority at fault under Massachusetts standards if you force another car to crash without touching it?
sec08-card-sec08-R32.expected_back: Causing a collision without physical contact is one of the listed fault standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R33.front: What fault rule applies when a collision results from failing to yield legally to an emergency vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R33.expected_back: Failing to yield to emergency vehicles when the law requires is one of the listed fault standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R34.front: At a T-intersection, how do fault standards treat a driver who pulls out from the terminating side street and crashes?
sec08-card-sec08-R34.expected_back: A collision at a T intersection after entering from the side road is one of the listed fault standards.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: How much does an attested Massachusetts driving record cost compared with an unattested copy, and where is the cheaper one sold?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: An attested Massachusetts driving record costs twenty dollars, while an unattested record costs eight dollars and is offered only online.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: Through which four channels can you request an attested Massachusetts driving record?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: An attested record can be requested online, at an RMV Service Center, by mail or through the Court Records Department.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: Which three sensitive categories of information are shielded from public Massachusetts driving records?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: Certain drug-offense, expired-warrant and child-support information is restricted from public driving records.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: When can the RMV suspend a learner permit or driver license immediately without waiting?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: The RMV may immediately suspend a learner permit or license when the driver presents an immediate public-safety threat.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: What administrative action can the RMV take for improper operation of a motor vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: Improper motor-vehicle operation can cause the RMV to suspend driving privileges.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: How long can your license be suspended for a listed false-identification offense without a court conviction versus after conviction?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: The specified false-identification offenses can bring a six-month suspension without conviction or one year after conviction.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: Which four types of card or application misconduct count as Massachusetts false-identification offenses?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: The listed identification offenses include transferring, altering or defacing a card, making or distributing a false card, using another person’s card and giving false application information.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.front: Before Massachusetts will lift a suspension tied to another state's action, what must happen first?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.expected_back: An out-of-state suspension or revocation must be cleared before the related Massachusetts suspension can end.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.front: Once another state reinstates you, how recent must your reinstatement letter or driving record be when shown to the RMV?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.expected_back: After another state reinstates the driver, a reinstatement letter or driving record no more than thirty days old must be brought to the RMV, which may request additional information.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.front: How does the RMV decide whether an out-of-state ticket counts as a 'like offense' in Massachusetts?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.expected_back: The RMV identifies a like out-of-state offense by the conduct prohibited, regardless of its penalty or civil or criminal classification in that state.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.front: If another state convicts you of a like offense without suspending you there, what does Massachusetts do?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.expected_back: Massachusetts suspension rules apply to a like out-of-state offense even when the other state did not impose suspension.

sec09-card-sec09-R17.front: Once your license or permit is suspended or revoked, when must you stop driving and where are you barred from driving?
sec09-card-sec09-R17.expected_back: A suspended or revoked driver must stop driving immediately and may not drive in Massachusetts or elsewhere with that invalid license or permit.

sec09-card-sec09-R18.front: How does Massachusetts classify driving on a suspended or revoked license, and what punishments can follow?
sec09-card-sec09-R18.expected_back: Driving on a suspended or revoked license is a criminal motor-vehicle offense that can bring fines, imprisonment and additional penalties.

sec09-card-sec09-R19.front: With whom does a suspended driver have the right to meet regarding license reinstatement?
sec09-card-sec09-R19.expected_back: A driver has the right to a hearing with an RMV Hearings Officer concerning reinstatement.

sec09-card-sec09-R20.front: What does an RMV suspension hearing review and generally verify?
sec09-card-sec09-R20.expected_back: A suspension hearing reviews the record and applicable law and generally addresses whether mandatory suspension law was applied correctly.

sec09-card-sec09-R21.front: Can a Hearings Officer block a valid suspension after a guilty or responsible finding, and how long can a decision take?
sec09-card-sec09-R21.expected_back: A Hearings Officer cannot prevent a valid suspension after a finding of guilt or responsibility and may take up to ten business days to decide.

sec09-card-sec09-R22.front: What is the typical Massachusetts reinstatement fee, and how high can it climb for serious offenses?
sec09-card-sec09-R22.expected_back: Reinstatement requires a fee, usually one hundred dollars but as high as twelve hundred dollars for serious offenses.

sec09-card-sec09-R23.front: What extra steps apply to get reinstated after a suspension that lasted two years or longer?
sec09-card-sec09-R23.expected_back: After a suspension lasting at least two years, reinstatement also requires a permit exam and road test, with identification documents for those tests.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: For drivers eighteen or older, what suspension and reinstatement fee follow three speeding findings within one year?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: For drivers eighteen or older, three speeding violations or responsible findings within one year cause a thirty-day suspension and a one-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: What happens when a driver eighteen or older hits three surchargeable events in two years?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: For drivers eighteen or older, three surchargeable events within two years require retraining within ninety days or indefinite suspension until completion, with a one-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: What penalty and reinstatement fee hit a driver eighteen or older with seven surchargeable events in three years?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: For drivers eighteen or older, seven surchargeable events within three years cause a sixty-day suspension and a one-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: What five-year violation totals brand you a habitual traffic offender, and what suspension and fee follow?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: A habitual traffic offender with three major moving violations or twelve major or minor moving violations within five years receives a four-year suspension and a five-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: In the adult mandatory table, how long does an out-of-state suspension block you in Massachusetts, and what fee applies?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: An out-of-state suspension remains effective in Massachusetts until resolved and carries the listed one-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: When during a mandatory suspension for qualifying drug-trafficking offenses may a person apply for a hardship license?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: A person serving a mandatory suspension for certain drug-trafficking offenses may request a hardship license at any point during the suspension.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: What suspension lengths and reinstatement fee hit a junior permit holder caught driving unaccompanied on first, second, and later offenses?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: The junior-permit table lists unaccompanied-driving suspensions of sixty days for a first offense, one hundred eighty days for a second and one year for later offenses, with a one-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: What exam or course requirements apply after first and second junior-permit unaccompanied-driving offenses?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: Every listed junior-permit unaccompanied-driving offense requires another permit exam, and the second offense requires Driver Attitudinal Retraining.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: What suspension progression and reinstatement fee apply to a junior-permit nighttime driving violation?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: A junior-permit nighttime violation brings sixty days for a first offense, one hundred eighty days for a second and one year for later offenses, with a one-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: Which exams or courses are required after first and second junior-permit nighttime violations?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: Each listed junior-permit nighttime offense requires another permit exam, and the second offense requires Driver Attitudinal Retraining.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: What suspension, testing, and fee penalties hit a junior-permit holder caught speeding?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: The junior-permit speeding suspension is ninety days for a first offense and one year for later offenses, with a new permit exam and a one-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: What suspension lengths and reinstatement fees apply to first and repeat drag racing on a junior permit?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: Junior-permit drag racing brings a one-year suspension for a first offense and three years for later offenses, with reinstatement fees of five hundred dollars and one thousand dollars respectively.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: What testing and courses are required after any junior-permit drag-racing offense?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: Every listed junior-permit drag-racing offense requires a new permit exam and Driver Attitudinal Retraining, and a SCARR course may also be required.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: How long is a junior permit suspended for first, second, and later mobile-device violations, and what is the restore fee?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: A junior-permit mobile-device offense brings sixty days for the first offense, one hundred eighty days for the second and one year for later offenses, with a one-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: What fines and first-offense requirements hit a junior permit holder cited for using a mobile device?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: For junior-permit mobile-device violations, the first offense requires a one-hundred-dollar fine, a new permit exam and Driver Attitudinal Retraining; later listed fines are two hundred fifty dollars and five hundred dollars.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: What suspension terms and reinstatement fee apply to negligent operation with phone-caused injury on a junior permit?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: Negligent operation with injury from phone use on a junior permit brings a first suspension of one hundred eighty days and a later suspension of one year, with a five-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: When does a junior-permit negligent-operation-and-phone-injury offense require retaking the permit exam?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: A second or later junior-permit negligent-operation-and-phone-injury offense requires a new permit exam.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: What suspension ladder and reinstatement fee hit a Junior Operator License holder for passenger or nighttime violations?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: A Junior Operator License passenger or nighttime violation brings sixty days for the first offense, one hundred eighty days for the second and one year for later offenses, with a one-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: When do Junior Operator License passenger or nighttime violations trigger retraining versus full permit and road retesting?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: A second or later Junior Operator License passenger or nighttime violation requires retraining, while a third or later violation also requires a new permit exam and road test.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: What suspension terms and reinstatement fee apply to a speeding conviction on a Junior Operator License?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: A Junior Operator License speeding conviction brings ninety days for the first offense and one year for later offenses, with a five-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: What exams and courses must a Junior Operator License holder complete after even a single speeding conviction?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: Every Junior Operator License speeding offense requires a new permit exam, retraining and road test, and may also require SCARR.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: What suspension lengths and first-offense reinstatement fee apply to drag racing on a Junior Operator License?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: Junior Operator License drag racing brings a one-year first suspension and a three-year later suspension, with a five-hundred-dollar first-offense reinstatement fee listed.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: Which tests and courses are required after every Junior Operator License drag-racing offense?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: Every listed Junior Operator License drag-racing offense requires a new permit exam, retraining and road test, with possible SCARR.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.front: What suspension terms and reinstatement fee hit a Junior Operator convicted of reckless or negligent operation?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.expected_back: Junior Operator reckless or negligent operation brings a first suspension of one hundred eighty days, or one year for another offense within three years, with a five-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.front: When must a Junior Operator retake both the permit exam and road test for reckless or negligent operation?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.expected_back: A second or later listed Junior Operator reckless or negligent operation offense requires a new permit exam and road test.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.front: What suspension progression and reinstatement fee apply to a mobile-device conviction on a Junior Operator License?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.expected_back: A Junior Operator License mobile-device conviction brings sixty days for the first offense, one hundred eighty days for the second and one year for later offenses, with a one-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.front: What fine ladder and first-offense retesting hit a Junior Operator License holder convicted of mobile-device use?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.expected_back: A first Junior Operator License mobile-device offense requires a one-hundred-dollar fine, permit exam, retraining and road test; the second and third fines are two hundred fifty dollars and five hundred dollars.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.front: What suspension lengths and reinstatement fee follow negligent operation with phone-related injury on a Junior Operator License?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.expected_back: Negligent operation with phone-related injury on a Junior Operator License brings a first suspension of one hundred eighty days and a later suspension of one year, with a five-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.front: When does a Junior Operator License phone-injury offense require a new permit exam and road test?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.expected_back: A second or later listed Junior Operator phone-injury offense requires a new permit exam and road test.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.front: Who else gets notified whenever a Junior Operator receives a license or permit suspension?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.expected_back: A junior suspension is also reported to the driver’s parent or guardian.

sec09-card-sec09-F38.front: How long is the extra Junior Operator suspension for specified serious convictions, and what exception prevents double counting?
sec09-card-sec09-F38.expected_back: For the specified Junior Operator convictions, the additional suspension is one hundred eighty days for a first offense and one year for later offenses unless an additional suspension was already imposed for chemical-test failure or refusal.

sec09-card-sec09-F39.front: Which alcohol, endangerment, and crash-scene crimes sit on the additional Junior Operator suspension list?
sec09-card-sec09-F39.expected_back: The specified additional-junior-suspension offenses include operating under the influence, endangerment, leaving a crash, drinking from an open alcohol container and alcohol-impaired operation causing serious injury.

sec09-card-sec09-F40.front: Which four non-alcohol serious offenses also trigger the additional Junior Operator suspension?
sec09-card-sec09-F40.expected_back: Unauthorized vehicle use, reckless or negligent operation, allowing someone else to use a license or permit and motor-vehicle homicide are also in the additional-junior-suspension list.

sec09-card-sec09-F41.front: How many times must a Junior Operator complete the RMV-mandated SCARR program, and who else can order it?
sec09-card-sec09-F41.expected_back: A Junior Operator required to take SCARR needs to complete that course only once, although a court may also order the program.

sec09-card-sec09-F42.front: Which five non-driving obligations or convictions can get your Massachusetts license suspended?
sec09-card-sec09-F42.expected_back: Non-driving suspension grounds include unpaid required child support, failure to register as a sex offender, certain drug-trafficking convictions, unpaid Massachusetts income tax and a bad payment to the RMV.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: What amounts and payment methods are required to clear a bad-payment suspension with the RMV?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: Clearing a bad-payment suspension requires the original amount, the reinstatement fee and an additional fifteen dollars, paid with cash or a certified bank check payable to MassDOT.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: In the criminal suspension table, what suspension range and reinstatement fee apply for driving on a suspended or revoked license?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: Driving on a suspended or revoked license carries a suspension from sixty days to one year and a five-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: What suspension range and reinstatement fee follow unauthorized vehicle operation or vehicle larceny?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: Unauthorized vehicle operation or vehicle larceny carries a one-to-three-year suspension and a five-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: What suspension term and reinstatement fee hit a driver convicted of leaving an injury crash?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: Leaving an injury crash carries a one-to-two-year suspension and a five-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: How long is the suspension and what is the reinstatement fee for leaving a property-damage crash?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: Leaving a property-damage crash carries a suspension from sixty days to one year and a five-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: What suspension range and reinstatement fee apply to a conviction for operating to endanger?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: Operating to endanger carries a suspension from sixty days to one year and a five-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: What suspension span and reinstatement fee apply to motor-vehicle homicide or vehicular manslaughter?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: Motor-vehicle homicide or vehicular manslaughter carries a suspension from fifteen years to life and a five-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: What is the exact suspension sequence across first, second, third, fourth, and fifth OUI convictions?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: The OUI suspension sequence is one year, two years, eight years, ten years and lifetime for the first through fifth convictions.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: How do reinstatement fees progress from a first through fifth OUI conviction?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: The listed OUI reinstatement fees are five hundred dollars for the first conviction, seven hundred for the second and twelve hundred for the third or fourth, with reinstatement not applicable to the fifth.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: What suspension and fee apply to qualifying drug-trafficking convictions outside Class D substances, even if no car was used?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: A qualifying drug-trafficking conviction other than a Class D substance carries a one-to-five-year suspension and one-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee even without vehicle operation.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: For a driver older than eighteen, what suspension range and reinstatement-fee range apply to drag racing?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: For a driver older than eighteen, drag racing carries a thirty-to-one-hundred-eighty-day suspension and a reinstatement fee from five hundred to one thousand dollars.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.front: In the criminal table, what suspension range and restore fee apply to negligent operation causing injury through mobile-phone use?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.expected_back: Negligent operation causing injury through mobile-phone use carries a sixty-day-to-one-year suspension and a five-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee.

sec09-card-sec09-R24.front: What court fine range, maximum jail time, and standard license suspension apply to a first OUI conviction?
sec09-card-sec09-R24.expected_back: A first OUI conviction carries a fine from five hundred to five thousand dollars, imprisonment up to two and a half years and a one-year suspension.

sec09-card-sec09-R25.front: If a court allows alcohol education on a first OUI, how short can the suspension drop for drivers over twenty-one versus under twenty-one?
sec09-card-sec09-R25.expected_back: For a first OUI offense, the court may permit alcohol education to reduce the suspension to forty-five through ninety days for a driver over twenty-one or two hundred ten days for a driver under twenty-one.

sec09-card-sec09-R26.front: What fine range, prison term, and suspension apply to a second OUI conviction?
sec09-card-sec09-R26.expected_back: A second OUI conviction carries a six-hundred-to-ten-thousand-dollar fine, imprisonment from thirty days to two and a half years and a two-year suspension.

sec09-card-sec09-R27.front: How is a third OUI classified, and what fine, prison range, and suspension does it carry?
sec09-card-sec09-R27.expected_back: A third OUI conviction is a felony with a one-thousand-to-fifteen-thousand-dollar fine, imprisonment from one hundred fifty days to five years and an eight-year suspension.

sec09-card-sec09-R28.front: What felony penalties apply upon a fourth Massachusetts OUI conviction?
sec09-card-sec09-R28.expected_back: A fourth OUI conviction is a felony with a fifteen-hundred-to-twenty-five-thousand-dollar fine, imprisonment from one to five years and a ten-year suspension.

sec09-card-sec09-R29.front: What fine range, prison term, and license loss hit a driver convicted of a fifth OUI?
sec09-card-sec09-R29.expected_back: A fifth OUI conviction is a felony with a two-thousand-to-fifty-thousand-dollar fine, imprisonment from two to five years and lifetime suspension.

sec09-card-sec09-R30.front: At what blood-alcohol content reading does every driver fail a chemical test in Massachusetts?
sec09-card-sec09-R30.expected_back: A blood-alcohol content of zero point zero eight or higher fails the chemical test for every driver.

sec09-card-sec09-R31.front: How do the criminal standard and administrative sanction threshold compare for drivers younger than twenty-one?
sec09-card-sec09-R31.expected_back: Drivers younger than twenty-one share the criminal blood-alcohol standard but may receive administrative sanctions at zero point zero two.

sec09-card-sec09-R32.front: How long is the failed-chemical-test suspension for a driver over twenty-one?
sec09-card-sec09-R32.expected_back: The failed-test table assigns drivers over twenty-one a thirty-day suspension or suspension until the court case ends, whichever is shorter.

sec09-card-sec09-R33.front: What failed-test suspension applies to drivers aged eighteen to twenty-one, and how can a first-time OUI case trim the extra period?
sec09-card-sec09-R33.expected_back: The failed-test table assigns ages eighteen to twenty-one thirty days plus one hundred eighty days, with the additional period waivable through approved alcohol education for a first OUI case.
