sec09-card-sec09-R34.front: What failed-test suspension hits a driver under eighteen, and how much can alcohol education trim it on a first OUI?
sec09-card-sec09-R34.expected_back: The failed-test table assigns drivers under eighteen thirty days plus one year, with the added year reducible to one hundred eighty days through approved alcohol education for a first OUI case.

sec09-card-sec09-R35.front: If an under-twenty-one driver wins their OUI court case, what happens to the alcohol-education duty tied to the failed test?
sec09-card-sec09-R35.expected_back: Winning the court case does not eliminate the under-twenty-one alcohol-education requirement associated with the additional failed-test suspension.

sec09-card-sec09-R36.front: Under the chemical-test refusal table, what counts as a prior OUI and what specifically does not?
sec09-card-sec09-R36.expected_back: For the refusal table, a prior OUI means a conviction or court-ordered alcohol-education assignment, while a previous chemical-test refusal is not itself a prior OUI.

sec09-card-sec09-R37.front: For drivers over twenty-one, how long are chemical-test refusal suspensions with zero, one, two, or three-plus prior OUIs?
sec09-card-sec09-R37.expected_back: For drivers over twenty-one, refusing a chemical test brings one hundred eighty days with no prior OUI, three years with one prior, five years with two and lifetime with at least three.

sec09-card-sec09-R38.front: What refusal suspensions apply to ages eighteen through twenty-one with zero or one prior, two priors, or three-plus priors?
sec09-card-sec09-R38.expected_back: For the eighteen-to-twenty-one group, refusal brings three years plus one hundred eighty days with no prior or one prior OUI, five years plus one hundred eighty days with two priors and lifetime with at least three.

sec09-card-sec09-R39.front: What refusal suspensions hit drivers under eighteen across zero or one prior, two priors, and three-plus priors?
sec09-card-sec09-R39.expected_back: For drivers under eighteen, refusal brings three years plus one year with no prior or one prior OUI, five years plus one year with two priors and lifetime with at least three.

sec09-card-sec09-R40.front: On a first OUI case, what does approved alcohol education waive for an eighteen-to-twenty-one driver who refused testing?
sec09-card-sec09-R40.expected_back: For a first OUI case in the eighteen-to-twenty-one refusal group, entering approved alcohol education can waive the additional one-hundred-eighty-day suspension.

sec09-card-sec09-R41.front: For a driver under eighteen in a first OUI case, how does approved alcohol education change the added refusal suspension?
sec09-card-sec09-R41.expected_back: For a first OUI case under eighteen, entering approved alcohol education can reduce the added refusal suspension from one year to one hundred eighty days.

sec09-card-sec09-R42.front: Does winning your OUI case in court cancel the added underage refusal suspension or its alcohol-education rule?
sec09-card-sec09-R42.expected_back: The added underage refusal suspension and its alcohol-education obligation are unaffected by winning the court case.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: How is alcohol classified as a drug, and which four core driving abilities can it impair?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: Alcohol is a depressant that can impair vision, coordination, judgment and reaction time.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: Can small amounts of alcohol, other drugs, or nonprescription medicine weaken safe driving skills?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: Even a small amount of alcohol or another drug, including some nonprescription medicine, can reduce the abilities needed for safe driving.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: Must a driver look visibly drunk or fully intoxicated to become dangerous after substance use?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: A driver need not appear drunk or fully intoxicated to be dangerous after substance use.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: What happens to driving safety whenever you use any substance that alters awareness or reflexes?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: Using a substance that affects awareness or reflexes makes driving unsafe.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: How can alcohol distort a driver's confidence and willingness to take road risks?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: Alcohol can create unwarranted confidence and encourage driving risks the person would otherwise avoid.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: Which three unsafe driving habits become more likely after a person drinks alcohol?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: Alcohol can make a driver less likely to buckle up, more likely to speed and less able to remain in the lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: Beyond court OUI fines, what separate payment is required before the RMV restores a license?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: RMV reinstatement fees must be paid in addition to OUI fines before the license can be restored.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: Can just one drink in an hour impair driving, and what personal states worsen that effect?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: Even one alcoholic drink in an hour can affect driving, with worse effects possible when the person is tired, upset or has not eaten.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: What travel arrangement should you make before planning to drink or after drinking alcohol?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: After drinking or when planning to drink, arrange a designated driver, taxi, rideshare or ride from someone else.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: Do coffee, cold showers, exercise, or food actually speed up alcohol removal from your body?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: Coffee, cold showers, exercise and food do not speed alcohol’s removal from the body even if they make a person feel more alert.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: What does blood-alcohol content measure, and which two test types can determine it?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: Blood-alcohol content measures unprocessed alcohol in the body and can be measured with a breath or blood test.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: Which five personal and drinking factors determine a person's blood-alcohol content?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: Blood-alcohol content depends on body weight, alcohol amount, food eaten beforehand, drinking duration and the person’s alcohol-processing speed.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: Does the beverage category matter more for impairment, or the total alcohol consumed over time?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: The amount of alcohol consumed over time matters more than the beverage category.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: Which serving sizes of beer, wine, and eighty-proof liquor carry roughly equal amounts of alcohol?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: The manual treats a twelve-ounce beer, a five-ounce wine and a one-and-a-half-ounce serving of eighty-proof liquor as approximately equivalent alcohol portions.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: What is the single thing that eliminates alcohol's impairing effects from your body?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: Only the passage of time removes alcohol’s effects.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: Under Massachusetts implied-consent law, what do licensed drivers agree to submit to?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: Massachusetts implied-consent law requires licensed drivers to consent to a breath or blood test in specified circumstances.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: When a police officer suspects a driver is impaired by alcohol, what roadside evaluation may be requested?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: When an officer believes a driver is impaired by alcohol, the officer may request a field sobriety test.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: Following an arrest for alcohol-impaired driving, what tests may an officer request to measure BAC?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: After an alcohol-impaired-driving arrest, the officer may request a breath or blood test to determine blood-alcohol content.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: Which blood-alcohol content number reaches the standard legal-limit threshold in Massachusetts?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: A blood-alcohol content of zero point zero eight or higher meets the stated legal-limit threshold.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: At what blood-alcohol content does a driver younger than twenty-one face zero-tolerance penalties?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: A driver younger than twenty-one faces penalties at a blood-alcohol content of zero point zero two or higher under the zero-tolerance law.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: What immediate actions must an officer take if you fail or refuse a breath or blood test?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: The officer must confiscate the license and issue an immediately effective suspension notice when the driver exceeds the legal limit or refuses a breath or blood test.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: When must an OUI offender pay to install an ignition interlock device for reinstatement or hardship driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: A driver with at least two OUI offenses who is eligible for reinstatement or a hardship license must have an ignition interlock installed in the vehicle at the driver’s expense.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: How long must a required ignition interlock stay in use across hardship and reinstated driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: A required ignition interlock must be used throughout a hardship-license period and for two more years after reinstatement.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: Which three vehicle features let an interlock-required applicant schedule a road test online?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: An interlock-required applicant may book a road test online when the vehicle has the interlock, a center-console brake and a sponsor seat.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: How must an interlock road test be booked if the car lacks a center-console brake or sponsor seat?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: If an interlock-equipped vehicle lacks the center-console brake or sponsor seat, the road test must be arranged through an RMV supervisor rather than online.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: May a person under twenty-one purchase alcohol directly or arrange for someone else to buy it?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: Someone younger than twenty-one may not buy alcohol or have another person buy it for them.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.front: When is someone younger than twenty-one allowed to possess, carry, or transport alcohol?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.expected_back: A person younger than twenty-one may not possess, carry or transport alcohol unless a parent or guardian accompanies them.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.front: What license suspension range applies to prohibited underage alcohol possession, carrying, or transport?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.expected_back: The manual lists suspension from ninety days to one year for prohibited underage alcohol possession, carrying or transport.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: How long is the license suspension specifically assigned for underage buying or attempting to buy alcohol?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: The specific underage-purchase sentence assigns a one-hundred-eighty-day suspension for buying or attempting to buy alcohol.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: Is drinking any alcoholic beverage while driving ever permitted in Massachusetts?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: Drinking alcohol while driving is prohibited.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: Is an open alcoholic beverage legal inside your vehicle if a passenger holds it instead of you?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: An open alcoholic drink is prohibited inside the vehicle even when another person is holding it.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: What dollar fine range applies to an open-container conviction in Massachusetts?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: An open-container conviction brings a fine from one hundred to five hundred dollars.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: Which three consequences hit an offender younger than twenty-one who breaks the open-container rule?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: An offender younger than twenty-one violating the open-container rule faces arrest, a fine and license suspension.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: Is using, altering, borrowing, or lying for an ID illegal even when not trying to buy alcohol?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: Using false identification, altering a card, using another person’s card or providing false information to obtain a card is illegal even without trying to buy alcohol.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: How long can the RMV suspend your license for ID fraud without a conviction versus after conviction?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: The RMV may suspend driving privileges for up to six months for the specified identification offenses without a conviction, while conviction brings a one-year suspension.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: Beyond legal penalties, what personal security danger comes with ordering false identification online?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: Buying false identification online is dangerous and can result in identity theft.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: Do Massachusetts OUI laws cover impairing prescription and over-the-counter medicines as well as alcohol?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: OUI laws apply to drugs as well as alcohol, including prescription and nonprescription medicines that impair driving.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: How can marijuana affect a driver's reaction to sights, sounds, and rapid sequences of road tasks?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: Marijuana can impair response to sights and sounds and make a rapid series of driving tasks harder.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.front: Why does marijuana create added danger when unexpected driving hazards appear at night?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.expected_back: Marijuana-related night-vision impairment makes unexpected driving hazards harder to handle after dark.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.front: Does adult marijuana legalization or decriminalization make driving under marijuana's influence legal for any age?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.expected_back: Driving under marijuana’s influence remains a criminal offense for every age even though some possession or use has been decriminalized.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.front: Which penalty schedule governs drivers convicted of operating under the influence of marijuana?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.expected_back: The OUI penalty table applies to marijuana-impaired driving.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.front: How do prescription sedatives and tranquilizers make operating a motor vehicle hazardous?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.expected_back: Prescription sedatives and tranquilizers can cause drowsiness that makes driving dangerous.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.front: How can illegal drugs like LSD, heroin, and opium distort a driver's situational awareness?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.expected_back: Illegal drugs such as LSD, heroin and opium can impair awareness of location and reduce concern about the surroundings.

sec10-card-sec10-R16.front: How can cold, allergy, headache, pain, or codeine medicines affect your fitness to drive?
sec10-card-sec10-R16.expected_back: Cold, hay-fever and headache medicines may cause drowsiness, and pain medicines or codeine-containing products can impair driving.

sec10-card-sec10-R17.front: Can taking your own prescribed medication still result in an illegal OUI violation?
sec10-card-sec10-R17.expected_back: A driver can commit OUI using prescription drugs, and impairment by any substance makes vehicle operation illegal.

sec10-card-sec10-R18.front: What dangerous symptoms follow temporary alertness from stimulants, including effects on eyesight?
sec10-card-sec10-R18.expected_back: Stimulants can give temporary alertness followed by fatigue, nervousness, dizziness and poor concentration, and can affect vision.

sec10-card-sec10-R19.front: What two dangers arise from inhaling solvent or glue vapors?
sec10-card-sec10-R19.expected_back: Inhaled solvents or glue vapors can leave a person unable to drive properly and pose serious health risks.

sec10-card-sec10-R20.front: What two steps should you take to check side effects before driving on any medicine?
sec10-card-sec10-R20.expected_back: Read medicine labels for side effects and ask a doctor or pharmacist when uncertain.

sec10-card-sec10-R21.front: What happens when you combine alcohol with another drug or medication?
sec10-card-sec10-R21.expected_back: Combining alcohol with other drugs greatly increases their negative effects.

sec10-card-sec10-R22.front: Which two municipal vehicle citations can block you from renewing your Massachusetts license?
sec10-card-sec10-R22.expected_back: Unpaid parking fines and abandoned-vehicle citations can prevent license renewal.

sec10-card-sec10-R23.front: Which unpaid local tax and which unresolved court status can prevent license renewal?
sec10-card-sec10-R23.expected_back: Unpaid local excise tax and outstanding court warrants can prevent license renewal.

sec10-card-sec10-R24.front: Unpaid electronic tolls from which three states, plus which named bridge, can block renewal?
sec10-card-sec10-R24.expected_back: Unpaid Massachusetts, Maine or New Hampshire electronic-toll violations and unpaid Tobin Bridge violations can prevent license renewal.

sec10-card-sec10-R25.front: What documentation must be recorded before the RMV will renew a blocked license?
sec10-card-sec10-R25.expected_back: Before renewal, official releases must prove that the relevant fines and local taxes have been paid or warrants satisfied.

sec10-card-sec10-R26.front: Which exact court document is required to clear an outstanding warrant for the RMV?
sec10-card-sec10-R26.expected_back: An outstanding court warrant requires a court recall notice, and the RMV does not accept substitute documents for it.

sec10-card-sec10-R27.front: Can you renew a Massachusetts driver's license while it is currently suspended or revoked?
sec10-card-sec10-R27.expected_back: A suspended or revoked license cannot be renewed.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: Who gets priority before you turn onto or across a designated throughway?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: Before turning at a designated throughway, yield to vehicles traveling on it.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: From a one-lane or two-lane street, which larger intersecting roadways require you to yield?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: A driver on a one- or two-lane road must yield when intersecting a divided highway or a road with at least three lanes.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: How is a Massachusetts rotary structured, and what traffic control usually governs its entrances?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: A rotary connects roads from several directions around a central island and normally has yield controls at the entrances.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: In which rotational direction does traffic circulate around a Massachusetts rotary?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: Traffic moves counterclockwise around a rotary.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: Unless signs or an officer direct otherwise, to whom must you yield when entering a rotary?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians and traffic already in a rotary unless signs or an officer direct otherwise.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: How should you signal at rotary intersections, especially when exiting the circle?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: Signal as at other intersections and use the right-turn signal when leaving a rotary.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: Which approach lane and destination lane do you use at a single-lane rotary?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: For a single-lane rotary, enter from the approaching road’s right lane and leave into the destination road’s right lane.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: What guides your lane selection when approaching a multilane rotary that has signs?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: At a multilane rotary, follow lane-choice signs when provided.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: Without lane-choice signs at a multilane rotary, which lane handles a quarter-turn or straight-through path?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: Without lane-choice signs, a quarter-turn or straight movement uses the right lane into and through the rotary and exits to the right lane.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: Without signs, what lanes handle a three-quarter or U-turn in a rotary, and what is the single-lane exception?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.memory_hook: Left to inner, single stays right
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: Without lane-choice signs, a three-quarter-turn or U-turn uses the left entry and an inner or middle rotary lane before exiting right, except that entry from a single-lane road stays in the right lane throughout.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: Why must you wait until it is completely safe before changing lanes inside a rotary?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: Do not change rotary lanes until it is safe because traffic may be on either side.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: What should you do instead of stopping if you miss your intended exit inside a rotary?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: After missing a rotary exit, go around again when safe and position for the proper exit rather than stopping in the rotary.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.front: How do roundabouts compare in size to rotaries, and what speed limit applies inside them?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.expected_back: Roundabouts are generally smaller than rotaries and require slowing to twenty-five miles per hour or less because of their small size.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.front: How should you choose lanes and enter when approaching a roundabout?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.expected_back: Choose a roundabout lane using approach signs and apply the rotary’s entry and lane-selection rules.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.front: Does another driver waving you through transfer oncoming traffic's right of way for your turn?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.expected_back: A driver’s wave does not transfer oncoming traffic’s right of way, so a turn must depend on an actual clear or stopped traffic stream and adequate visibility.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.front: On which side do you normally drive and pass, and when is right-side passing allowed?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.expected_back: Drive on the right and ordinarily pass on the left, with right-side passing allowed only in specified circumstances.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.front: When may you pass a person, cyclist, or vehicle, and may you exceed the speed limit to finish?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.expected_back: Pass a person, bicycle or vehicle only when necessary and safe, and never exceed the speed limit to pass.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.front: Which three roadside areas must never be used to pass another vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.expected_back: Never use the shoulder, breakdown lane or sidewalk to pass a vehicle.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.front: Which lanes should you use to pass on a roadway with multiple lanes moving your way?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.expected_back: Use the middle or left lanes to pass on a road with multiple same-direction lanes.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.front: What passing maneuver does a broken yellow center line permit when safe?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.expected_back: A broken yellow center line allows a temporary safe move into the opposing lane to pass.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.front: What checks and minimum forward clear view do you need before crossing a broken yellow line to pass?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.expected_back: Before crossing a broken yellow line to pass, keep a safe gap, check the passing lane, mirrors and blind spot and have a clear view at least four hundred feet ahead.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.front: Which turn signals do you use when starting a pass and when returning to your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.expected_back: Signal left before moving gradually into the passing lane and signal right after getting safely past the other vehicle.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.front: What visual check in your mirror tells you when it is safe to pull back right after passing?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.expected_back: Before returning right after a pass, wait at least until the passed vehicle’s headlights can be seen in the mirror and sufficient room exists.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.front: Before an oncoming car gets within how many feet must you finish returning to the right lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.expected_back: Return to the right lane before an approaching vehicle is within two hundred feet and cancel the signal after the return.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.front: What roadway width and clearance condition must exist before passing on the right is ever legal?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.expected_back: Passing on the right requires a clear roadway wide enough for at least two lines of vehicles.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.front: When the roadway is wide and clear enough, in what three situations may you pass on the right?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.expected_back: Subject to the clear-and-wide-road condition, passing on the right is allowed beside a vehicle turning left or on a one-way street or same-direction roadway.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.front: How must you adjust your speed and lane position when another driver is passing you?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.expected_back: When being passed, slow down and keep right without accelerating.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.front: How must you adjust your approach toward a stopped emergency vehicle showing flashing lights?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.expected_back: Approach a stopped emergency vehicle displaying flashing lights cautiously and slow to a reasonable safe speed for the conditions.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.front: What lane action does Move Over require on a four-or-more-lane highway with at least two lanes your way?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.expected_back: On a highway with at least four lanes and at least two in your direction, safely move to a lane not adjacent to the stopped emergency, highway or recovery vehicle.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.front: What must you do near a stopped flashing responder if traffic prevents changing lanes?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.expected_back: If moving over is not possible, still pass cautiously at a reduced safe speed.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.front: What hidden hazards can a stopped or turning vehicle block from your view?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.expected_back: A stopped or turning vehicle can conceal another vehicle, person or animal.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.front: Which six risky driving actions does the manual identify as aggressive-driving behaviors?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.expected_back: Cutting off traffic, speeding, unsignaled lane changes, tailgating, running red lights and blocking a pass are aggressive-driving behaviors.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.front: What four calm steps should you take if confronted by an aggressive driver?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.memory_hook: Yield space, avoid eyes, stay belted
sec13-card-sec13-F33.expected_back: When confronted by an aggressive driver, get out of the way, avoid a challenge and eye contact, ignore gestures and stay belted.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.front: What can the RMV do before court after an aggressive-driving arrest that threatens public safety?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.expected_back: An aggressive-driving arrest may lead the RMV to suspend the license and registration before court when the driver threatens public safety.

sec13-card-sec13-F35.front: What two warning devices on a school bus alert drivers that children are boarding or leaving?
sec13-card-sec13-F35.expected_back: School-bus warning equipment includes flashing red lights and an extending driver-side stop sign.

sec13-card-sec13-F36.front: How do smaller school-pupil transport vans or sedans warn traffic while loading or unloading students?
sec13-card-sec13-F36.expected_back: School-pupil transport vehicles such as vans or sedans use flashing red lights and roof-mounted School Bus signs while loading or unloading pupils.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: From which approach directions must you stop for a school bus with flashing lights and stop arm out?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: Stop for a school bus displaying flashing lights and an extended stop sign regardless of which direction you approach from.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: Until what bus signal change must you remain stopped for a school bus?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.memory_hook: Hold until lights stop, sign folds
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: Remain stopped until the school-bus lights stop flashing or the stop sign folds back.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: What fine and license action can hit a driver on a first school-bus stopping violation?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: A first school-bus stopping violation can bring license suspension and a two-hundred-fifty-dollar fine.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: How should you resume driving once school-bus warning signals turn off?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: After school-bus warning signals end, proceed slowly and keep watching for children.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: Under what highway setup is oncoming traffic exempt from stopping for a school bus across the road?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: A driver on the opposite side of a divided highway need not stop for a school bus when a barrier separates the travel directions.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.front: What does the manual say you are doing if you follow a truck too closely to see its side mirrors?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.expected_back: If a following driver cannot see a truck’s mirrors, the manual identifies the driver as tailgating.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.front: How much stopping distance may a large truck need compared with a car or motorcycle?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.expected_back: A large truck may need twice a car’s or motorcycle’s stopping distance, especially on wet or icy roads.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.front: Why must you avoid lingering right beside a large truck or cutting in front to brake?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.memory_hook: Never crowd or cut off trucks
sec13-card-sec13-R08.expected_back: Do not enter the space immediately around a large vehicle or cut in front and suddenly slow or stop.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.front: Which lanes do trucks and buses use on a multilane highway for cruising and passing?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.expected_back: On a multilane highway, trucks and buses use the two right lanes, with ordinary travel in the far right and passing in the second.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.front: How should you drive in the second highway lane to avoid bottlenecking trucks and buses?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.expected_back: A driver in the second lane should keep pace with traffic without going below the minimum speed and allow a truck or bus to pass when safe.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.front: How does passing a tractor-trailer or bus differ in time and on hills from passing a car?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.memory_hook: Longer pass, slower up, faster down
sec13-card-sec13-R11.expected_back: Passing a tractor-trailer or bus takes longer than passing a smaller vehicle, and large vehicles may be slower uphill and faster downhill.

sec13-card-sec13-R12.front: Unless strictly necessary, why should you stay off the right side of a truck or bus?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.expected_back: Avoid passing a truck or bus on the right unless absolutely necessary because large vehicles make wide turns.

sec13-card-sec13-R13.front: Why might a truck or bus swing left first, and what should you do behind it?
sec13-card-sec13-R13.expected_back: A truck or bus may move left before turning right, so stay behind until its intended movement is clear.

sec13-card-sec13-R14.front: On an undivided road with a large rig oncoming, where should you steer and why?
sec13-card-sec13-R14.expected_back: Keep right when a large vehicle approaches on an undivided road to avoid sideswipe and air-turbulence hazards.

sec13-card-sec13-R15.front: Before turning across the path of oncoming trucks or buses, why is careful gap judgment essential?
sec13-card-sec13-R15.expected_back: Judge approaching trucks and buses carefully before turning across them because they cannot slow easily after being cut off.

sec13-card-sec13-R16.front: How should you respond when a transit bus signals to pull out from its stop?
sec13-card-sec13-R16.expected_back: Allow a signaling transit bus to leave its stop and watch for people boarding or leaving buses and trolleys.

sec13-card-sec13-R17.front: How much clearance must you keep from a trolley's passenger step while riders board or exit?
sec13-card-sec13-R17.expected_back: Do not drive within eight feet of a trolley’s passenger step while passengers are boarding or leaving.

sec13-card-sec13-R18.front: What precautions apply before crossing trolley tracks or turning near an approaching trolley?
sec13-card-sec13-R18.expected_back: Look for approaching trolleys before crossing tracks and do not turn in front of one that is approaching.

sec13-card-sec13-R19.front: Why must you maintain extra space around a trolley sharing a street with motor traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-R19.expected_back: Keep a safe gap from a trolley sharing the road because it cannot steer away from its tracks.

sec13-card-sec13-R20.front: How should you respond when you spot an orange rear warning sign on a slow-moving vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-R20.expected_back: An orange rear warning on a slow-moving vehicle calls for slowing, caution and ample passing space.

sec13-card-sec13-R21.front: What minimum vehicle count, timing, and purpose define a legal Massachusetts funeral procession?
sec13-card-sec13-R21.expected_back: A funeral procession consists of at least two vehicles including a lead or escort vehicle traveling by daylight with a deceased person’s body or cremated remains.

sec13-card-sec13-R22.front: Although funeral processions hold intersection priority, to what two authorities must they still yield?
sec13-card-sec13-R22.expected_back: A funeral procession has intersection priority but must yield to emergency lights or sirens and obey law-enforcement direction.

sec13-card-sec13-R23.front: Once the funeral lead vehicle lawfully enters an intersection, what may trailing procession cars do?
sec13-card-sec13-R23.expected_back: After a funeral lead vehicle enters an intersection lawfully, following procession vehicles may continue through even after a light changes or at a stop sign.

sec13-card-sec13-R24.front: How closely may drivers inside a funeral procession follow the car ahead?
sec13-card-sec13-R24.expected_back: A procession driver must remain careful and may follow the preceding vehicle as closely as safety allows.

sec13-card-sec13-R25.front: What safety checks still apply to trailing funeral vehicles following their leader through an intersection?
sec13-card-sec13-R25.expected_back: A procession vehicle may follow the leader through an intersection only when safe and must watch for pedestrians and other vehicles.

sec13-card-sec13-R26.front: What maximum speed applies to a funeral procession on a highway posted at fifty-five or higher?
sec13-card-sec13-R26.expected_back: A funeral procession may not exceed fifty-five miles per hour on a highway whose limit is fifty-five or higher.

sec13-card-sec13-R27.front: On public roads below that highway tier, how slow may a funeral procession travel relative to the limit?
sec13-card-sec13-R27.expected_back: On other public roads, a funeral procession may not travel more than five miles per hour below the speed limit.

sec13-card-sec13-R28.front: Which lights must every funeral procession car run, and which cars add hazard flashers?
sec13-card-sec13-R28.expected_back: Every procession vehicle must use headlights and taillights, and the first and last vehicles must use hazard lights.

sec13-card-sec13-R29.front: When may an outside driver cut between vehicles in a funeral procession?
sec13-card-sec13-R29.expected_back: A nonprocession driver may not enter between procession vehicles unless directed by police or operating an emergency vehicle with both siren and flashing lights.

sec13-card-sec13-R30.front: May an uninvolved driver tag onto a funeral procession to share its priority?
sec13-card-sec13-R30.expected_back: A driver may not join a funeral procession without being part of it.

sec13-card-sec13-R31.front: Under what single lane condition may you pass a funeral procession on its right on a multilane highway?
sec13-card-sec13-R31.expected_back: A procession may not be passed on its right on a multilane highway unless it is in the far-left lane.

sec13-card-sec13-R32.front: Does a green traffic light let you drive across a funeral procession moving through its red?
sec13-card-sec13-R32.expected_back: A green light does not allow crossing a procession’s path while it moves through red; crossing is allowed only without crossing that path.

sec13-card-sec13-R33.front: What flashing light color may an eligible funeral-home vehicle display during a procession?
sec13-card-sec13-R33.expected_back: An eligible funeral-home vehicle may display a flashing purple light during a procession, but no other color under the stated funeral-vehicle authorization.

sec13-card-sec13-R34.front: What four precautions apply when driving near roadwork zones?
sec13-card-sec13-R34.memory_hook: Follow orange, watch workers, prepare stop
sec13-card-sec13-R34.expected_back: Near roadwork, follow orange signs, look for workers on foot and sudden roadway changes and be prepared to stop.

sec13-card-sec13-R35.front: What happens to the speeding fine when a violation occurs inside a work area?
sec13-card-sec13-R35.expected_back: The speeding fine is doubled in a work area.

sec13-card-sec13-R36.front: Who gets the right of way when an animal is being led, ridden, or driven on the road?
sec13-card-sec13-R36.expected_back: Give right of way to an animal being led, ridden or driven and slow near animals or horse-drawn vehicles.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.front: What three everyday cabin habits must never distract your full attention from driving?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.expected_back: Give driving full attention rather than being distracted by conversation, radio adjustments or eating.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.front: Why should you scan well ahead and practice defensive driving?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.expected_back: Look ahead and drive defensively so hazards can be seen early enough to avoid them.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.front: Which three driving environments should you practice, and which emergencies should you study?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.expected_back: Practice highway, nighttime and varied-weather driving and learn how to respond to emergencies such as skids and tire failures.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.front: Which warning signals on an emergency vehicle require you to yield the right of way?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.expected_back: Yield to an emergency vehicle using a siren, emergency flashing lights or both.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.front: Where and how must you stop when an emergency vehicle approaches from any direction?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.expected_back: For an emergency vehicle approaching from any direction, pull as far right as possible and stop fully until it passes.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.front: How should you use mirrors, signals, and brakes when pulling over for a responding emergency vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.expected_back: Use mirrors and a right-turn signal to choose a safe pull-over location without moving left, braking harshly or stopping suddenly.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.front: What must you do if an emergency vehicle approaches while you are already inside an intersection?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.expected_back: Do not stop inside an intersection for an emergency vehicle; clear the intersection and pull over when safe.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.front: What must you check and signal after a responding emergency vehicle passes you?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.expected_back: After the emergency vehicle passes, check for additional responders and a clear lane, signal left and merge back safely.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.front: Within how many feet is it illegal to follow a responding emergency vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.expected_back: Following a responding emergency vehicle closer than three hundred feet is illegal.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.front: Which six types of stopped flashing roadside vehicles trigger your duty to slow and stay alert?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.memory_hook: Fire, police, EMS, disaster, road, tow
sec15-card-sec15-F10.expected_back: Slow and stay alert near stopped fire, police, ambulance, disaster-support, highway-maintenance or recovery vehicles with flashing emergency lights.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.front: What speed standard does the Move Over rule set near a stopped flashing emergency vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.expected_back: The move-over rule requires a cautious reasonable safe speed when approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.front: When does Massachusetts require changing into a non-adjacent lane past a stopped emergency vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.expected_back: On a highway with at least four lanes including two in your direction, safely change to a lane not beside the stopped emergency vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.front: Which direction may a safe Move Over lane change go, and what applies if boxed in?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.expected_back: The safe move-over direction may be right or left, and if a lane change is impossible the driver must still slow and proceed cautiously.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.front: What brake readiness and headlight adjustment apply when passing an emergency scene at night?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.expected_back: Be ready to stop when passing an emergency vehicle and dim high beams at night.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.front: Where relative to a parked police cruiser should you pull over when requesting assistance?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.expected_back: If requesting police assistance, stop in front of the cruiser rather than behind it.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.front: What should you do instead of walking up to an officer already handling another traffic stop?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.expected_back: Do not approach an officer handling another stopped driver; wait beside your own vehicle on the shoulder until the officer finishes.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.front: Within how many feet of an active fire is driving past or parking prohibited?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.expected_back: Driving by or parking within eight hundred feet of a fire is prohibited.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.front: When is driving over an unprotected fire hose across the street ever permitted?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.expected_back: Do not drive across an unprotected fire hose unless a firefighter or public-safety official directs you to do so.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.front: Must you pull over and stop when signaled by a police officer standing on foot?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.expected_back: A driver must pull to the roadside and stop when signaled by an officer, whether the officer is on foot or in a police vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.front: How must a driver treat any police signal to pull over?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.expected_back: Do not ignore a police stop signal or pretend not to see it.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.front: Which side of the road and what signal-and-mirror steps apply during a routine police stop?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.expected_back: Signal, check mirrors and move slowly and completely to the road’s right side during a police stop rather than pulling left.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.front: What should you do if the signaling police officer drives right past without stopping behind you?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.expected_back: If the signaling officer continues past without stopping, reenter the travel lane when safe.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.front: Which three spots should you avoid stopping in during a police pull-over, and whose spot choice controls?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.expected_back: Do not stop in an intersection, driveway entrance or travel lane, and follow an officer’s direction to a particular stopping place.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.front: How should you set your transmission, brake, engine, and radio once stopped by police?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.expected_back: During a stop, select Park in an automatic or neutral with the parking brake in a manual vehicle, and turn off the engine and radio.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.front: What should the driver and passengers do inside the car when pulled over by police?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.expected_back: The driver and passengers should remain inside until the officer instructs otherwise.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.front: If an officer directs you to step out during a stop, how should you position yourself and your hands?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.expected_back: If directed out, stay safely away from traffic and keep hands visible.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.front: Which two vehicle lights should be on during a nighttime police traffic stop?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.expected_back: At night during a police stop, leave headlights on and turn on the interior overhead light.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.front: What window action should you take as the officer walks up to your car?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.expected_back: Lower the window as the officer approaches.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.front: How is officer identification handled if the officer stopping you is not wearing a uniform?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.expected_back: An officer not in uniform will show credentials, or the driver may ask to see them.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.front: When should you reach for your license and registration, and how should you hand them over?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.expected_back: Wait for a request before reaching for license or registration and hand the documents over outside a wallet or holder.

sec15-card-sec15-R12.front: What first-offense fine applies if you fail to produce your license or registration when stopped?
sec15-card-sec15-R12.expected_back: Keep license and registration handy while driving; a first failure to produce either document carries a thirty-five-dollar fine.

sec15-card-sec15-R13.front: If you lack your license or registration, whose names and addresses may the officer ask for?
sec15-card-sec15-R13.expected_back: Without the documents, the officer may request the driver’s name and address and the owner’s name and address when different.

sec15-card-sec15-R14.front: What fine and criminal consequences hit drivers who refuse identity details or give fake names or addresses?
sec15-card-sec15-R14.expected_back: Failure to comply with the identity request or giving a false name or address can bring a one-hundred-dollar fine, and refusal may lead to arrest and criminal charges.

sec15-card-sec15-R15.front: How does Massachusetts handle proof of auto insurance compared with other states?
sec15-card-sec15-R15.expected_back: A Massachusetts registration identifies the insurer and explains that Massachusetts does not issue an insurance card, while other jurisdictions may request insurance proof under their laws.

sec15-card-sec15-R16.front: Whose hands should remain plainly visible during a traffic stop?
sec15-card-sec15-R16.expected_back: Keep both the driver’s and passengers’ hands plainly visible.

sec15-card-sec15-R17.front: How should you handle your cell phone and focus during a police stop?
sec15-card-sec15-R17.expected_back: Give the officer full attention without using a cell phone during the stop.

sec15-card-sec15-R18.front: What physical movements should both the driver and passengers avoid during a traffic stop?
sec15-card-sec15-R18.expected_back: Avoid sudden movements or reaching into hidden areas, and make sure passengers avoid those movements too.

sec15-card-sec15-R19.front: Where must you stay while the officer walks back to the police cruiser?
sec15-card-sec15-R19.expected_back: Remain in the vehicle when the officer goes back to the cruiser.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.front: When may you ask the officer a question, and how should you hold a located document while waiting?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.expected_back: Wait until the officer returns before asking a question, and hold a requested item out the window while waiting if it has been found.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.front: How must you respond if an officer asks during a stop whether weapons are inside the vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.expected_back: Answer appropriately when an officer asks whether weapons are in the vehicle.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.front: Can an officer withdraw an issued citation roadside, and where do you contest it instead?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.expected_back: An issued citation must be filed and cannot be withdrawn by the officer, but the driver may ask for clarification and challenge it in court.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.front: Does Massachusetts require signing a traffic citation, and what does signing mean in states that require it?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.expected_back: Massachusetts does not require signing a citation, while other jurisdictions may require a signature acknowledging receipt rather than admitting the violation.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.front: How should you reenter traffic—especially from a highway breakdown lane—once the officer clears you to leave?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.expected_back: After the officer permits departure, signal, check mirrors and reenter traffic, accelerating to a safe speed in the highway breakdown lane before merging.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.front: Where may a driver report a traffic stop they believe involved bias or improper conduct?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.expected_back: A driver who believes a stop involved race or gender bias or improper officer conduct may report it to the officer’s department or agency.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.front: What pedal and gear actions should you take first when your vehicle starts skidding?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.expected_back: In a skid, ease off the accelerator slowly and shift into neutral.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.front: Why must you stay off the brakes while your car is actively skidding?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.expected_back: Do not hit the brakes during a skid because that worsens it.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.front: Which direction do you steer when your rear tires slide left or slide right?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.expected_back: Steer in the direction the rear tires are sliding, left for a leftward slide or right for a rightward slide.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.front: What steering follow-up may be required as a skidding vehicle starts straightening out?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.expected_back: Repeated left and right steering corrections may be needed to regain control after a skid.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.front: What are your first two actions if your tires drop off the pavement onto the shoulder?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.expected_back: After leaving the pavement for the shoulder, hold the wheel firmly and ease off the accelerator.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.front: After stabilizing on the shoulder, what three steps bring you safely back onto the road?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.expected_back: When off the pavement, brake gently to reduce speed, check behind and steer smoothly back onto the road.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.front: How should you handle the wheel and gas pedal during a flat tire, blowout, or lost wheel?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.expected_back: For a flat tire, blowout or wheel loss, hold the steering wheel firmly and gradually release the accelerator.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.front: Once under control after a tire or wheel failure, when should you leave the roadway?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.expected_back: After a tire or wheel failure, leave the roadway as soon as doing so is safe.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.front: If pressing failed antilock brakes all the way down fails to slow you, what gear step comes next?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.expected_back: If fully pressing failed antilock brakes does not work, downshift progressively toward a lower gear.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.front: How should you use the parking brake and its release during total service-brake failure?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.expected_back: During brake failure, apply the parking brake gently while holding its release in case a skid begins.

sec16-card-sec16-F17.front: Which two vehicle alerts should you activate if brake failure prevents you from slowing?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.expected_back: If brake failure prevents slowing, warn nearby drivers and pedestrians with the horn and flashing lights.

sec16-card-sec16-F18.front: How does emergency brake-pedal technique differ between non-antilock brakes and antilock brakes?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.expected_back: For a vehicle without antilock brakes, rapid repeated pedal applications may rebuild pressure, but antilock brakes must not be pumped.

sec16-card-sec16-F19.front: What two places tell you whether a car has antilock or conventional brakes?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.expected_back: The dashboard indicator or vehicle manual can identify the brake-system type.

sec16-card-sec16-F20.front: What four actions handle a stuck accelerator while keeping your car under control?
sec16-card-sec16-F20.expected_back: If the accelerator sticks, select neutral and use the brake to slow, try freeing the pedal with a foot and keep watching the road.

sec16-card-sec16-F21.front: Where should you go once safe after handling a stuck accelerator?
sec16-card-sec16-F21.expected_back: When safe after an accelerator sticks, pull to the roadside and stop.

sec16-card-sec16-F22.front: What three immediate moves dodge a vehicle coming straight at you head-on in your lane?
sec16-card-sec16-F22.expected_back: For a vehicle approaching head-on in your lane, slow, move right and sound the horn.

sec16-card-sec16-F23.front: What backup lights and roadside steps apply if your headlights suddenly go dark?
sec16-card-sec16-F23.memory_hook: Backup flashers, switch check, pull off
sec16-card-sec16-F23.expected_back: If headlights fail, use parking lights, hazard flashers or a turn signal, try the switch and pull off the road promptly with hazards on.

sec16-card-sec16-F24.front: What is the top priority when a train is approaching a vehicle stalled on railroad tracks?
sec16-card-sec16-F24.expected_back: If a train is coming toward a vehicle stalled on the tracks, get every occupant out immediately and as far from the tracks as possible.

sec16-card-sec16-F25.front: At what angle and direction should you run from tracks as a train approaches, and whom do you call?
sec16-card-sec16-F25.expected_back: To avoid train-crash debris, move away from the tracks at a forty-five-degree angle toward the direction the train is approaching from, then call nine one one.

sec16-card-sec16-F26.front: If your car stalls on tracks with zero train approaching, what are your first two steps?
sec16-card-sec16-F26.expected_back: With no train approaching a stalled vehicle, open a window or door to listen and try restarting the engine.

sec16-card-sec16-F27.front: If no train is coming and a stalled car refuses to restart on tracks, how can you try clearing it?
sec16-card-sec16-F27.expected_back: If the stalled vehicle will not restart and no train is approaching, select neutral and try moving it clear of the tracks.

sec16-card-sec16-F28.front: What number and details must you call in if a stalled vehicle cannot be moved off railroad tracks?
sec16-card-sec16-F28.expected_back: If a vehicle cannot be cleared from the tracks, call the crossing’s Emergency Notification System number, provide its crossing-locator number and tell the dispatcher a vehicle is on the tracks.

sec16-card-sec16-F29.front: Through what system should you report suspicious railroad activity such as switch tampering?
sec16-card-sec16-F29.expected_back: Report suspicious railroad activity such as switch tampering through the Emergency Notification System.

sec16-card-sec16-F30.front: Where should you steer during a breakdown, and what two blind road features must you avoid?
sec16-card-sec16-F30.expected_back: For a breakdown, move to the roadside and avoid stopping on a hill or curve where approaching traffic cannot see the vehicle.

sec16-card-sec16-F31.front: What must happen to passengers if a disabled vehicle cannot be moved off the pavement?
sec16-card-sec16-F31.expected_back: If a disabled vehicle cannot be removed from the pavement, get its passengers out and off the roadway.

sec16-card-sec16-F32.front: Once parked far off a highway travel lane on the shoulder, where should occupants stay?
sec16-card-sec16-F32.expected_back: On a highway shoulder, move far from the travel lane and remain inside rather than standing near the travel lane or in the breakdown lane.

sec16-card-sec16-F33.front: Which lights should you turn on once parked safely during a breakdown, including after dark?
sec16-card-sec16-F33.expected_back: Once safely parked during a breakdown, switch on hazard lights and at night the interior lights.

sec16-card-sec16-F34.front: When should you put on an available reflective safety vest during a breakdown?
sec16-card-sec16-F34.expected_back: Put on an available reflective safety vest while still inside the vehicle.

sec16-card-sec16-F35.front: What should you evaluate before getting out of a disabled car, and which door side is safer?
sec16-card-sec16-F35.expected_back: Assess whether it is safe to get out and consider the side away from moving traffic.

sec16-card-sec16-F36.front: Which cloth color tied to an antenna or handle signals a breakdown normally versus in snow?
sec16-card-sec16-F36.expected_back: A white cloth tied to the antenna or door handle marks a breakdown, with a red cloth used during snow.

sec16-card-sec16-F37.front: When in the breakdown sequence should you raise your vehicle's hood?
sec16-card-sec16-F37.expected_back: The breakdown instructions call for raising the hood after the safe-exit assessment.

sec16-card-sec16-F38.front: At what two distances behind a disabled car do warning triangles or LED flares go on a divided highway?
sec16-card-sec16-F38.expected_back: On a divided highway, the listed warning-triangle or LED-flare positions are ten feet and one hundred feet behind the disabled vehicle.

sec16-card-sec16-F39.front: Where do three warning triangles or flares go on a two-way two-lane or undivided highway?
sec16-card-sec16-F39.expected_back: On a two-way two-lane road or undivided highway, the listed warning positions are ten feet behind, one hundred feet behind and one hundred feet in front.

sec16-card-sec16-F40.front: What four actions must you take immediately if smoke starts coming from under your hood?
sec16-card-sec16-F40.memory_hook: Exit road, ignition off, evacuate, call
sec16-card-sec16-F40.expected_back: If smoke appears under the hood, leave the road, shut off the ignition, move away from the vehicle and call the fire department or emergency services.

sec16-card-sec16-F41.front: When should you never attempt to fight a vehicle fire yourself?
sec16-card-sec16-F41.expected_back: Do not attempt to fight a vehicle fire without a fire extinguisher.

sec16-card-sec16-F42.front: What rapid belt-and-window sequence saves you if your vehicle plunges into water?
sec16-card-sec16-F42.expected_back: If a vehicle enters water, unfasten the belt and escape through a window, opening electric windows quickly before water disables them.

sec16-card-sec16-F43.front: Why must you avoid opening a car door after entering deep water?
sec16-card-sec16-F43.expected_back: Do not open the vehicle door in water because water can rush inside and overturn the vehicle.

sec16-card-sec16-F44.front: What four steps apply immediately after a crash or breakdown inside a tunnel?
sec16-card-sec16-F44.memory_hook: Pull aside, hazards, emergency call, obey
sec16-card-sec16-F44.expected_back: For a tunnel crash or breakdown, pull aside if possible, activate hazard lights, call nine one one and follow instructions.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.front: Where should you wait for responders after a non-fire tunnel breakdown when conditions are safe?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.expected_back: Remain in the vehicle after a tunnel incident if safe and wait for emergency assistance.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.front: What three habits apply every time you drive into a tunnel?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.memory_hook: Stay alert, headlights on, obey signs
sec16-card-sec16-R02.expected_back: On entering a tunnel, remain alert, turn on headlights and obey signs and signals.

sec16-card-sec16-R03.front: What two smoke or fire conditions forbid you from driving into a tunnel?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.expected_back: Do not enter a tunnel when smoke is visible near the entrance or the vehicle itself is smoking or burning.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.front: How should you manage following distance inside a tunnel during slow traffic?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.expected_back: Maintain safe spacing in a tunnel even when traffic is slow.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.front: What cargo category—including propane—is barred from the described Massachusetts tunnels?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.expected_back: Hazardous materials including propane are prohibited in the described tunnels.

sec16-card-sec16-R06.front: What three awareness cues help you stay ready while driving through tunnel traffic?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.memory_hook: Radio updates, spot exits, obey signs
sec16-card-sec16-R06.expected_back: In tunnel traffic, listen for radio updates, note emergency exits and follow officials and message signs.

sec16-card-sec16-R07.front: During a tunnel fire, how must you leave your engine, keys, and personal belongings?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.expected_back: During a tunnel fire, stop, shut off the engine and leave the vehicle with its keys and belongings inside.

sec16-card-sec16-R08.front: What three steps apply during a tunnel fire as you evacuate?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.expected_back: During a tunnel fire, call nine one one, follow emergency instructions and help others when able.

sec16-card-sec16-R09.front: Must a driver stop after a minor crash, or only after major collisions?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.expected_back: A driver involved in any crash, even a minor one, must stop rather than leave the scene.

sec16-card-sec16-R10.front: When nobody is hurt in a crash, what does the Driver Removal Law require if cars still drive?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.expected_back: When nobody is injured, the Driver Removal Law requires moving involved vehicles from travel lanes to a safe place if possible.

sec16-card-sec16-R11.front: Which five pieces of information must drivers exchange after a crash, plus what must be shown on request?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.memory_hook: Swap name, address, license, reg, insurer
sec16-card-sec16-R11.expected_back: After a crash, exchange names, addresses, license numbers, registrations and insurance details with involved drivers or property owners, and show license and registration if requested.

sec16-card-sec16-R12.front: What must you do if you strike and damage unattended property such as a parked car?
sec16-card-sec16-R12.expected_back: After damaging unattended property, try to locate the owner and report the crash or notify local police.

sec16-card-sec16-R13.front: What property-damage dollar amount triggers a mandatory five-day crash report to police and the RMV?
sec16-card-sec16-R13.expected_back: A crash with at least one thousand dollars in property damage must be reported to the RMV and local police within five days.

sec16-card-sec16-R14.front: Whom must you notify after striking and injuring an animal on the road?
sec16-card-sec16-R14.expected_back: After injuring an animal, notify local police and the owner when possible.

sec16-card-sec16-R15.front: What three immediate steps follow a crash that involves possible injuries?
sec16-card-sec16-R15.expected_back: After an injury crash, check for injuries, contact police and request an ambulance or emergency medical technicians when needed.

sec16-card-sec16-R16.front: Which three crash outcomes require filing written reports with the RMV and local police within five days?
sec16-card-sec16-R16.expected_back: An injury, fatality or at-least-one-thousand-dollar property-damage crash requires reports to the RMV and local police within five days.

sec16-card-sec16-R17.front: Besides police and the RMV, whom must you notify after an injury crash?
sec16-card-sec16-R17.expected_back: Notify the insurance company after an injury crash.

sec16-card-sec16-R21.front: What four duties bind a driver after any crash involving death, injury, or property damage?
sec16-card-sec16-R21.expected_back: After a crash involving death, injury or property damage, remain at the scene, identify yourself, offer aid when possible and call emergency assistance when needed.

sec16-card-sec16-R22.front: What maximum fine and prison exposure apply to leaving a property-damage crash without identifying yourself?
sec16-card-sec16-R22.expected_back: Leaving a property-damage crash without identifying yourself can bring up to two hundred dollars, up to two years in prison or both.

sec16-card-sec16-R23.front: What maximum fine and prison term apply to leaving a nonfatal injury crash without identifying yourself?
sec16-card-sec16-R23.expected_back: Leaving a nonfatal injury crash without identifying yourself can bring up to one thousand dollars and up to two years of imprisonment.

sec16-card-sec16-R24.front: What maximum fine, jail time, or state prison sentence applies to fleeing a fatal crash?
sec16-card-sec16-R24.expected_back: Leaving a fatal-injury crash without identifying yourself can bring up to five thousand dollars and up to two and a half years in jail or ten years in state prison.

sec16-card-sec16-R25.front: What happens if you injure or kill a cat or dog and fail to notify the owner or local police?
sec16-card-sec16-R25.expected_back: Failing to notify the owner or local police after injuring or killing a cat or dog can result in a fine.

sec16-card-sec16-R26.front: Beyond fines and jail, what three financial or licensing costs can follow a criminal driving conviction?
sec16-card-sec16-R26.expected_back: A criminal conviction can add probation costs, up to six years of insurance surcharges and possible license suspension.

sec16-card-sec16-R18.front: When may you move an injured crash victim, and what body parts must be supported if forced to?
sec16-card-sec16-R18.expected_back: Do not move an injured person unless necessary, and support the head and spine if a life-threatening situation forces movement.

sec16-card-sec16-R19.front: What first-aid technique does the manual advise for an open bleeding wound until paramedics arrive?
sec16-card-sec16-R19.expected_back: For bleeding, the source advises direct pressure on the wound maintained until help arrives.

sec16-card-sec16-R20.front: How can a coat or blanket help an injured person at a crash scene?
sec16-card-sec16-R20.expected_back: The source advises a blanket or coat to keep an injured person warm and help prevent shock.

sec16-card-sec16-R27.front: How should you drive past a crash scene when emergency responders are already on site?
sec16-card-sec16-R27.expected_back: When responders are already at a crash, slow and drive carefully without stopping or lingering to watch.

sec16-card-sec16-R28.front: What four actions should a witness take when arriving at a crash before responders get there?
sec16-card-sec16-R28.expected_back: A witness at a crash without responders should park off the road, activate hazards, check for injuries and arrange a call to police.

sec16-card-sec16-R29.front: At least how far ahead of and behind a crash scene should available flares or triangles sit?
sec16-card-sec16-R29.expected_back: Available crash-warning flares, triangles or reflectors should be placed at least two hundred feet ahead of and behind the crash.

sec16-card-sec16-R30.front: What two vehicle precautions should a witness take with crashed cars when safe and possible?
sec16-card-sec16-R30.expected_back: A witness should move crashed vehicles aside when possible and turn off their ignitions.

sec16-card-sec16-R31.front: What must you do—and tell trapped occupants—when downed electrical wires touch a crashed vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-R31.expected_back: Do not approach downed electrical wires or touch a vehicle they contact; tell occupants to stay inside until emergency personnel arrive.

sec16-card-sec16-R32.front: What penalties can follow failing to file a mandatory Massachusetts crash report?
sec16-card-sec16-R32.expected_back: Failure to submit a required crash report can bring a fine and license suspension or revocation.

sec16-card-sec16-R33.front: Does reporting a crash only to your insurance company fulfill your legal crash-reporting duties?
sec16-card-sec16-R33.expected_back: Reporting only to the insurer does not satisfy the motor-vehicle crash-reporting duties.

sec16-card-sec16-R34.front: From which three sources can you obtain a blank Massachusetts Motor Vehicle Crash Operator Report?
sec16-card-sec16-R34.expected_back: Crash-report forms are available from local police, RMV service centers or the RMV website.

sec16-card-sec16-R35.front: To which three recipients must you send completed copies of a required crash report?
sec16-card-sec16-R35.expected_back: Send completed crash-report copies to local police where the crash occurred, the insurance company and the RMV.

sec16-card-sec16-R36.front: What should you keep for yourself after mailing out your required crash-report copies?
sec16-card-sec16-R36.expected_back: Keep a crash-report copy for your own records.

sec16-card-sec16-R37.front: How can you request a copy of a law-enforcement crash report, and what is the fee?
sec16-card-sec16-R37.expected_back: A law-enforcement crash report may be requested online for twenty dollars.

sec16-card-sec16-R38.front: What travel alternatives reduce solo driving, and how should you group errands when driving?
sec16-card-sec16-R38.expected_back: Transit, walking, bicycling and carpooling can reduce driving, while linking errands can save time and fuel.

sec16-card-sec16-R39.front: Which stop should you visit first when combining multiple errands into one trip, and why?
sec16-card-sec16-R39.expected_back: When combining stops, the source recommends visiting the farthest destination first to warm the engine for better fuel economy.

sec16-card-sec16-R40.front: Which three smooth driving habits cut down wasteful jackrabbit starts and hard stops?
sec16-card-sec16-R40.expected_back: Gradual acceleration, steady speed and coasting when appropriate reduce wasteful rapid starts and hard stops.

sec16-card-sec16-R41.front: Beyond how many minutes does Massachusetts prohibit idling a parked motor vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-R41.expected_back: The manual states that Massachusetts prohibits idling longer than five minutes.

sec16-card-sec16-R42.front: How does a tight, undamaged fuel cap help efficiency and emissions?
sec16-card-sec16-R42.expected_back: A tight undamaged fuel cap helps prevent fuel evaporation.

sec16-card-sec16-R43.front: What three benefits come from keeping your tires inflated to the proper pressure?
sec16-card-sec16-R43.expected_back: Correct tire pressure improves safety, extends tire life and can improve fuel economy.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: Which three unexpected challenges does defensive driving keep you ready to handle?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Defensive driving means staying prepared for unexpected road users, equipment failures and changing conditions.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: What two visual and mental habits anchor every defensive drive?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: Keep a clear view ahead and around the vehicle and remain alert to hazards.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: Why shouldn't you turn your eyes toward a passenger or cabin item even for a split second?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: Looking away from the road at an occupant or object inside the vehicle can be dangerous even briefly.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: Why must you keep open space around your car AND track who is beside and behind you?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: Maintain space around the vehicle for an evasive lane change and know who is beside and behind you.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: What speed habit and pedal readiness belong on every street?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: Use a suitable speed and be ready to slow or stop.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: How often should you check mirrors, and which four directions need active road-condition watching?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: Check mirrors frequently and watch road conditions ahead, to both sides and behind.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: Which four street-edge movements — from brake lights to car doors — must urban scanning catch?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: Watch for stopping vehicles, people entering or leaving parked cars, pedestrians and bicyclists.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: What should you expect from fellow motorists, and what specific rear light warns of a backing car ahead?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: Expect other drivers to make mistakes and watch for reversing lights ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: Why shouldn't a green traffic signal lull you into assuming a crosswalk is clear?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: Do not assume a traffic signal will keep a crosswalk safe because other road users may disregard it.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: At which three community spots must you take special care for hidden pedestrians or bicycles?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: Use particular care near playgrounds, schools and shopping areas where people or bicycles may be hidden.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: What sensory assumption should you never make around pedestrians — especially in parking lots and crosswalks?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: Other road users may not hear your vehicle, especially in parking lots and crosswalks.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: Why should a defensive driver willingly yield right-of-way even when another driver is wrong?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: Giving right of way can prevent an unsafe traffic situation.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: How often does the Massachusetts manual recommend getting an eye exam?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: The manual recommends an eyesight examination every year or two and prompt correction of vision problems.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: How should a driver with diminished hearing adjust behind the wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: A driver with diminished hearing needs extra visual alertness to anticipate changing conditions.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: Which three chemical or medical exposures mean you must stay out of the driver's seat?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: Do not drive after drinking alcohol, while under a drug’s influence or after taking medicine that can cause drowsiness.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: Why shouldn't you drive when exhausted or emotionally upset?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: Do not drive while very tired or emotionally upset because those conditions can undermine safe driving.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: What simple eyewear habit does the manual advise on bright, sunny days?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: The manual advises sunglasses on bright sunny days.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: Along with following the factory maintenance schedule, what quick visual check belongs BEFORE getting into your car?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: Follow the manufacturer’s maintenance schedule and visually check for tire damage or low pressure before entering the vehicle.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: What should you do if you suspect brake trouble — and what does pulling to one side while braking signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: A suspected brake problem requires immediate inspection, and pulling to one side while braking can indicate a need for adjustment or repair.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: Which three routine tire-care tasks follow vehicle or tire-maker recommendations?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: Check tire inflation and wear and rotate tires according to vehicle or tire manufacturer recommendations.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: How does Massachusetts law treat driving on badly worn or damaged tires?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: Driving on badly worn or damaged tires is dangerous and illegal.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: What minimum tread depth in inches — and what structural condition — must legal tires maintain?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: Tires need at least two thirty-seconds of an inch of tread in the specified grooves without fabric breaks or visible cords.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: When you stick a penny into a tire groove, what visual cue tells you the tire is worn out?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: When a penny placed in a tread groove leaves the top of Lincoln’s head visible, the manual identifies the tire as worn out.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: What two warning flaws should never appear when you turn the steering wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: The steering wheel should not be loose or have a delay between wheel movement and tire response.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: What fluid should you check regularly, and what turning noise calls for a steering inspection?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: Check power-steering fluid regularly and have the system inspected if turning produces a high-pitched sound.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: Besides checking that headlights, brake lights, and blinkers work, what three winter or road coatings must you clean off them?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: Regularly check headlights, brake lights and turn signals and remove dirt, snow and ice from the lights.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: When must windshield wiper blades be replaced alongside keeping glass and mirrors clean?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: Keep mirrors and windows clean and replace wipers that streak or fail to clear the windshield.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.front: In what condition must license plates stay, and from how many feet away must numbers read at night?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.expected_back: License plates must be clean and unobstructed, with their numbers visible from sixty feet at night.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.front: In which exact corner of the license plate must your Massachusetts registration sticker go?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.expected_back: Registration stickers belong only in the plate’s upper-right corner.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.front: Under good road conditions and moderate traffic, what minimum following interval is Massachusetts's baseline rule?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.expected_back: Under good road conditions and moderate traffic, a minimum three-second following interval provides the manual’s basic safe-distance rule.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.front: How do you time your three-second gap using a roadside landmark — and what if you reach it early?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.expected_back: Check the following interval by counting three seconds after the vehicle ahead passes a fixed object and slowing down if you arrive before the count ends.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.front: Even in good weather, what spacing upgrade does the manual advise whenever open traffic allows?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.expected_back: Use a larger following interval for extra safety when traffic allows.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.front: At least how many seconds of following space must you leave behind a motorcycle?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.expected_back: Allow at least four seconds of following space behind a motorcycle.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.front: At least how many seconds of following space belong behind heavy equipment like a tractor or dump truck?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.expected_back: Allow at least ten seconds of following space behind heavy equipment such as a tractor or dump truck.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.front: Why must you never cut sharply in front of heavy equipment or a tractor-trailer?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.expected_back: Do not cut in front of heavy equipment or tractor-trailers because their greater weight requires more stopping room.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.front: Up to what dollar fine can unlawful tailgating draw in Massachusetts?
