sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Every smart choice behind the wheel shields everyone inside your cabin and everyone sharing the street.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: Which two ongoing vehicle-care practices does the Massachusetts manual tie directly to driving safety?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Catching worn brakes, bald tires, or burned-out bulbs before a trip prevents mechanical crashes.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: What safety-belt equipment standard must every passenger vehicle meet for everyone aboard?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Frayed webbing or jammed buckles fail inspection and leave passengers unprotected in a collision.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: Which five non-lighting components — covering visibility, sound, security, rain, and exhaust — must passenger cars carry?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Missing an ignition lock, working horn, or intact muffler fails Massachusetts equipment standards.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: Which two separate braking systems must every passenger vehicle have?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Independent hydraulic service brakes and mechanical or electric parking brakes back each other up.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: How must the driver-side window operate on a Massachusetts passenger vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: A stuck driver window prevents giving hand signals, paying tolls, or speaking with officers.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: Which three categories of exterior lights must every passenger vehicle carry?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Seeing the road and signaling stops or turns to surrounding traffic depend on all three.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: How many approved front lights and rear lights — and in what colors — are required for night driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: One burned-out headlamp makes an approaching car look like a motorcycle in the dark.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: How many red rear brake lights and what license-plate light must a passenger vehicle have?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Don't forget the center high-mount third brake lamp alongside the small white plate bulb.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: When directional signals or brake lights fail, how soon must you fix them — and how do you communicate meanwhile?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Extending your left arm for turns and stops bridges the gap straight to the repair shop.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: How often must every Massachusetts vehicle pass a combined safety and emissions inspection?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Checking your windshield sticker month keeps you from driving on an expired annual inspection.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: For which two narrow purposes may a passenger-vehicle spotlight be switched on?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Sweeping a spotlight into traffic blinds oncoming drivers; save it strictly for signs or headlight emergencies.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: At thirty feet ahead of your car, how high above the pavement may a spotlight beam rise?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Keeping the beam low at thirty feet illuminates roadside hazards without dazzling oncoming windshields.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: What authorization is required before mounting flashing, rotating, oscillating, or strobe emergency lights?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Unauthorized emergency strobes impersonate responders and violate Massachusetts equipment law without an RMV permit.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: How dark may side and rear windows be tinted in Massachusetts, and what is the rule on windshield tinting?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Darker aftermarket film or tinted front windshields fail annual inspection and draw citations.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: Which five visibility, medical, escape, and signaling items does the manual recommend packing in a vehicle safety kit?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: High-visibility vests, LED flares, glass breakers, and white-and-red cloths cover breakdowns and entrapments.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: Which four seasonal items does the manual recommend adding for cold and icy Massachusetts driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Dead batteries and sudden snow squalls strand unprepared drivers fast in freezing New England weather.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: Where should you store your vehicle safety kit instead of burying it beneath heavy trunk cargo?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: A glass breaker or first-aid pouch locked under luggage in the trunk cannot help in a rollover.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: Who must wear a belt or child restraint in Massachusetts — including inside vans and small trucks under what weight?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Front and back seats alike require belts across cars, vans, and pickups under eighteen thousand pounds.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: What dollar fine can an unbelted driver receive in Massachusetts?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Massachusetts sets twenty-five dollars as its baseline seat-belt and child-restraint citation fine.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: Starting at what age does an unbelted passenger personally face their own twenty-five-dollar fine?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Once a rider turns sixteen, the officer writes the twenty-five-dollar belt ticket directly to that passenger.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: For which passenger age bracket does the DRIVER get fined twenty-five dollars per unbelted rider?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Notice the split — ages twelve through fifteen bill the driver, while sixteen-plus bills the passenger.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: When may Massachusetts police issue a safety-belt fine?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Massachusetts enforces adult belt fines secondarily after stopping the car for a primary traffic offense.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: Vehicles built before which month and year are exempt from this Massachusetts safety-belt requirement?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Vintage cars assembled prior to July nineteen sixty-six predated federal seat-belt manufacturing mandates.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: Which five commercial or heavy-vehicle driver categories appear on the belt-exemption list — and at what truck weight?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: While listed under state exceptions, federal commercial rules still require belts on many big rigs.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: Which emergency-vehicle occupants and drivers appear on Massachusetts's seat-belt exemption list?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Medics treating patients in the back of an ambulance cannot stay strapped into a bench seat.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: When is a postal employee exempt from the Massachusetts safety-belt rule?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: Curb-to-curb mail delivery exempts on-duty carriers, though personal off-duty driving still requires belts.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.question_text: What documentation must a person carry if a disability makes wearing a safety belt physically impossible?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.teaching_text: Verbal claims fail at a traffic stop without formal certification signed by a physician.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.question_text: Until reaching EITHER what age OR what height in inches must a child ride in a federally approved child restraint?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.teaching_text: Memorize fifty-seven inches — that equals four feet nine inches, where adult belts finally fit.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.question_text: What is required once a child reaches age eight or fifty-seven inches tall?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.teaching_text: Outgrowing a booster never makes riding unrestrained legal — proper lap-and-shoulder belt use takes over.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.question_text: What fine applies for violating the Massachusetts child-restraint law?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.teaching_text: Child-restraint violations match the exact twenty-five-dollar fine used for adult safety-belt citations.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.question_text: What proof of safety testing must appear directly on any legal child restraint?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.teaching_text: Secondhand or uncertified seats missing the federal compliance sticker are illegal and unsafe.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.question_text: How must a child restraint be anchored inside the vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.teaching_text: Setting a carrier loosely on the bench without belting or latching its base turns it into a projectile.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.question_text: Where must you NEVER install a rear-facing child seat?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.teaching_text: An inflating front passenger airbag strikes the back of a rear-facing shell with lethal force.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.question_text: Which row is safest for children, and which specific seating spot in that row is best?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.teaching_text: Sitting in the rear center maximizes crumple-zone buffer from both frontal airbags and side T-bones.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.question_text: Which direction must an infant car seat always face?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.teaching_text: Cradling an infant's heavy head and fragile spine backward spreads crash forces across the seat shell.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.question_text: Which two measurements of the child — paired with what product specs — govern child-seat selection?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.teaching_text: Age alone misleads when a tall or heavy toddler outgrows a shell's printed manufacturer limits early.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: What three pound bands appear in the manual's illustrative seat guide — and what rule overrides rough examples?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Know the twenty/forty/eighty example tiers for the test, while always following your actual seat label.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: Which two deadly crash motions do safety belts prevent?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Getting thrown through glass or tossed around the cabin multiplies fatal injury odds.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: How should you wear a two-part lap-and-shoulder safety belt?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Tucking the shoulder strap behind your back lets your upper torso jackknife into the wheel.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: Which cabin surfaces — and who else inside — does a seat belt keep your body from striking?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Unbelted riders become human battering rams against windshields, steering wheels, and belted friends.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: How does wearing a safety belt help the driver steer or brake through a swerve or glancing hit?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Sliding sideways across the seat in a swerve pulls your hands and feet off the controls.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: Where on your body — and in what condition — does the lap belt belong?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Riding high across your soft stomach causes severe internal injuries that strong pelvic hip bones prevent.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: Across which two body parts must the shoulder belt lie — and which three placements are wrong?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Slipping the strap under your arm breaks ribs, while riding across your neck risks throat injury.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: Why does wearing a seat belt actually IMPROVE your odds of escaping a burning or sinking car?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Busting this myth wins points — you cannot unbuckle or swim out if a head hit knocks you unconscious.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.question_text: Does having airbags replace the need to buckle your safety belt?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.teaching_text: Supplemental airbags assume a belt holds you back instead of throwing your chest onto the inflating bag.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.question_text: For which crash direction are front airbags built — and which two impact types leave you relying on belts?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: Side T-bones and rear-end hits don't deploy front dash airbags, leaving unbelted riders defenseless.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.question_text: What specific danger does an unbelted adult pose to children or small pets during a crash?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.teaching_text: Crash deceleration hurls an unrestrained adult with thousands of pounds of force across smaller passengers.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.question_text: What two factors determine the right child seat for an infant or young child?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.teaching_text: Graduating a toddler too early into a loose seat leaves small shoulders slipping out of harnesses.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.question_text: How should the driver and front passenger position their seats relative to the dashboard?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.teaching_text: Maximizing space from the steering hub and dash gives airbags room to inflate safely.

sec05-card-sec05-R14.question_text: Which three core driving tasks must items inside your car never interfere with?
sec05-card-sec05-R14.teaching_text: Stacked boxes or pets in your lap block sightlines and tangle steering arms.

sec05-card-sec05-R15.question_text: Where must dashboard items, windshield mounts, or hanging mirror objects never block your sightline?
sec05-card-sec05-R15.teaching_text: Dangling air fresheners, suction mounts, or dash clutter hide pedestrians and trailing cars.

sec05-card-sec05-R16.question_text: Why must loose floor items be secured away from the driver's footwell?
sec05-card-sec05-R16.teaching_text: A water bottle rolling wedged behind the brake pedal prevents stopping in an emergency.

sec05-card-sec05-R17.question_text: What is Massachusetts's rule on wearing headphones, a headset, or attention-limiting wired or wireless gear while driving?
sec05-card-sec05-R17.teaching_text: Noise-blocking headphones seal out warning horns, screeching tires, and approaching emergency fire sirens.

sec05-card-sec05-R18.question_text: Who may legally wear ONE earplug with a cell phone while driving in Massachusetts?
sec05-card-sec05-R18.teaching_text: Junior operators under eighteen get zero earbud allowance, and adults must leave one ear open.

sec05-card-sec05-R19.question_text: What practical benchmark sets the maximum safe stereo volume inside your vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-R19.teaching_text: Blasting bass that drowns out ambulances delays pulling right until sirens are on your bumper.

sec05-card-sec05-R20.question_text: Where must any television screen installed inside a vehicle sit?
sec05-card-sec05-R20.teaching_text: Keeping video entertainment strictly for rear-seat riders stops drivers from glancing at movies.

sec05-card-sec05-R21.question_text: Does the ban on television distraction apply even to a screen visible through another car's window?
sec05-card-sec05-R21.teaching_text: Staring sideways at a neighboring SUV's headrest movie yanks your eyes off brake lights ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-R22.question_text: Under what age are children barred from pickup beds — and what speed ceiling caps the rare statutory exceptions?
sec05-card-sec05-R22.teaching_text: Even parade or farm exceptions never allow carrying under-twelve kids faster than five miles per hour.

sec05-card-sec05-R23.question_text: What blanket rule applies to handheld mobile electronic devices while driving in Massachusetts?
sec05-card-sec05-R23.teaching_text: Holding a phone in your hand while operating draws an automatic primary-enforcement citation.

sec05-card-sec05-R24.question_text: Starting at what age may a Massachusetts driver use a mobile electronic device — and in what mode only?
sec05-card-sec05-R24.teaching_text: Drivers under eighteen cannot even use Bluetooth hands-free except to report an emergency.

sec05-card-sec05-R25.question_text: When may an adult touch a phone while driving, and how must the phone be positioned?
sec05-card-sec05-R25.teaching_text: Holding a phone loose in your lap fails hands-free rules even on speakerphone — mount it cleanly.

sec05-card-sec05-R26.question_text: May you pick up your phone while stopped at a red light or stop sign — or where must you be?
sec05-card-sec05-R26.teaching_text: Classic exam trap — waiting at a red light still counts as operating inside a public travel lane.

sec05-card-sec05-R27.question_text: Should you pull onto the shoulder of a busy road or highway just to check your phone?
sec05-card-sec05-R27.teaching_text: Highway breakdown lanes belong to emergencies, not routine texts where fast traffic passes inches away.

sec05-card-sec05-R28.question_text: Which four text and web actions on a mobile device are banned while driving?
sec05-card-sec05-R28.teaching_text: Reading a text at a glance violates the law identically to typing a reply or opening a browser.

sec05-card-sec05-R29.question_text: What installation rule lets you use a GPS unit or phone map app for navigation while driving?
sec05-card-sec05-R29.teaching_text: Securing your phone in a dash or vent cradle keeps maps glanceable without holding the device.

sec05-card-sec05-R30.question_text: What is the ONLY situation in which a driver under eighteen may use ANY mobile electronic device while driving?
sec05-card-sec05-R30.teaching_text: Junior operators lose hands-free and Bluetooth call privileges too — only emergency calls stay legal.

sec05-card-sec05-R31.question_text: Which five portable gadget types count as mobile devices — and which four installed or audio systems are excluded?
sec05-card-sec05-R31.teaching_text: Handheld cameras and game consoles draw tickets, whereas factory radios, OnStar, and mounted GPS stay excluded.

sec05-card-sec05-R32.question_text: What penalty hits a driver for a FIRST Massachusetts handheld-device offense?
sec05-card-sec05-R32.teaching_text: Even your very first handheld stop starts at a crisp one-hundred-dollar citation.

sec05-card-sec05-R33.question_text: What dollar fine AND mandatory requirement hit on a SECOND handheld-device offense?
sec05-card-sec05-R33.teaching_text: Offense number two jumps to two hundred fifty dollars and adds mandatory distracted-driving education.

sec05-card-sec05-R34.question_text: Which three penalties stack on a THIRD or subsequent handheld-device offense?
sec05-card-sec05-R34.teaching_text: Insurance surcharges raise your premiums for years on top of the five-hundred-dollar fine and class.

sec05-card-sec05-R35.question_text: When does negligent phone-distracted driving become a crime — and what two severe consequences can follow a crash?
sec05-card-sec05-R35.teaching_text: Causing injury or property damage over a text escalates past traffic fines into criminal court and suspension.

sec05-card-sec05-R36.question_text: Which three pre-drive steps does the manual suggest to kill phone temptation completely?
sec05-card-sec05-R36.teaching_text: Putting a silenced phone out of reach in the back seat stops reflex reaches at traffic lights.

sec05-card-sec05-R37.question_text: When a call or text genuinely cannot wait, where should you pull over — and what spot should you avoid?
sec05-card-sec05-R37.teaching_text: Exiting into a parking lot or quiet side space beats risking a rear-end hit beside fast traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: What kind of windshield-washer fluid should you keep topped off for Massachusetts winter driving?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Road salt and slush coat glass fast, and summer fluid freezes solid inside lines right when visibility drops.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: Which three emergency items does Massachusetts recommend keeping in your trunk for winter trips?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Getting snowed in or stuck on an icy shoulder turns dangerous fast without warmth, light, and a way to dig out.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: What license plate type is required on a truck used to plow snow for pay?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Plowing driveways or lots for money turns a personal pickup into commercial work under Massachusetts registration rules.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: Alongside pedestrians, bicyclists, and roadside workers, which animal-related travelers count as Massachusetts vulnerable road users?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Test takers remember walkers and cyclists, yet equestrian riders and carriage drivers carry the exact same legal protection.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: Which small wheeled or mobility devices fall inside Massachusetts's vulnerable-road-user definition?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Anyone rolling on wheelchairs, mobility devices, motorized bikes, scooters, skateboards, or skates gets full vulnerable-user passing space.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: At least how many feet of clearance must you leave when passing any vulnerable road user in Massachusetts?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Squeezing closer than four feet leaves zero margin if a cyclist wobbles, hits a pothole, or steps around debris.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: May you cross the center line or use an adjacent lane to give a vulnerable user passing room, and what speed rule still applies?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Massachusetts lets you straddle or cross center markings when clear for space, never to punch past the posted limit.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: What common personal tech habits require extra scanning for pedestrians near the street?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Someone scrolling a screen or wearing earbuds may step off a curb without ever looking up or hearing your engine.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: Why must you use heightened caution around schools, parks, bus stops, and playgrounds?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Small stature hides young pedestrians behind parked cars right before a sudden sprint into traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: What assumption should you avoid making when joggers or skaters approach a crosswalk or signal?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Runners and skaters trying to keep momentum frequently blow past walk lights or dart outside painted crosswalk lines.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: What should you check before getting into your vehicle to back up?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Low rear blind zones can completely hide a toddler or family pet sitting right behind your bumper.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: Instead of trusting mirrors or backup sensors alone, how should you look while reversing?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Cameras and chimes miss side-approaching walkers that only a real shoulder turn through the rear glass catches.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: What must you do when a blind pedestrian is crossing the street ahead of you?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Rolling forward or creeping toward the crosswalk strips away the quiet space a blind traveler needs to finish crossing.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: Which three actions are forbidden when you encounter a blind pedestrian or a car stopped for one?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: A horn blast scrambles audio orientation, hand waves go unseen, and overtaking a stopped car risks hitting the walker.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: Which two mobility aids identify a blind pedestrian at a street crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Spotting either a white cane or a harnessed service dog triggers Massachusetts's strict full-stop crossing rule.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: Why must you never assume a pedestrian or cyclist hears your vehicle approaching and will step aside?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: You cannot spot deafness through a windshield, so counting on engine noise or a tap of the horn invites a collision.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: When claiming your technical right of way would create a dangerous situation, what should you do?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Winning an argument about right of way means nothing if forcing your turn causes an avoidable crash.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: Why should you scan with extra focus around train stations and bus stops?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Commuters rushing to catch a departing bus or stepping off a train often cross mid-block without checking lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: Why do streets near senior centers and older-adult residences call for extra patience and care?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Older walkers may judge gaps differently or need extra seconds to clear wide lanes safely.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: Where might pedestrians walking in the roadway be hidden from your view as you approach?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: Outrunning your sightline around a blind bend, crest, or row of parked SUVs leaves no room to stop for someone in the lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: On which Massachusetts roadways are bicycles and mopeds barred from riding?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: Cyclists and moped riders share public streets by right everywhere except high-speed expressways where signs forbid them.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: Do traffic-control devices and right-of-way laws apply to bicycle and moped riders?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Two-wheeled riders carry the same duty at red lights, stop signs, and intersections as drivers in full-size cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: Which three everyday driver slip-ups can badly hurt a passing bicycle or moped rider?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: With no steel cage around a rider, a split-second glance down, slight drift, or swung car door causes severe trauma.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: Why should you ease off the gas when passing a bicycle or moped even if you have clearance?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: A high-speed gust off your side panels can push or pull a lightweight bike straight toward traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: What must you do when oncoming traffic or a narrow lane prevents passing a bicycle or moped with safe room?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: Hanging back a few seconds until opposing cars clear or pavement widens beats squeezing past inches from handlebars.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: What headlight adjustment must you make for an oncoming bicyclist after dark?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: High-beam glare blinds an approaching cyclist just as badly as an oncoming driver and hides potholes right in front of their tire.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.question_text: What sudden movement should you always anticipate when trailing or passing a bicycle or moped?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.teaching_text: A storm grate, broken bottle, or crack invisible from your seat can force a rider sideways without warning.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: What check is essential before swinging open a parked vehicle's street-side door?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: Flinging a door into a bike lane gives an approaching rider zero time to brake or steer clear.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: How do a motorcycle's roadway rights compare with those of a car or truck?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: Smaller size never shrinks legal status, because Massachusetts treats every motorcycle as a full motor vehicle on the road.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: During which two common maneuvers must drivers look especially carefully for approaching motorcycles?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Pulling into traffic or cutting a left turn across oncoming lanes causes a huge share of car-versus-motorcycle crashes.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.question_text: What three-part routine should you follow before merging or changing lanes near motorcycles?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.teaching_text: A narrow bike slips easily behind roof pillars or side mirrors, so one quick glance misses fast-closing riders.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.question_text: How many seconds of following distance should you keep behind a motorcycle instead of the usual three-second gap?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.teaching_text: Motorcycles can shed speed quicker than heavier cars, so that extra fourth second prevents a rear-end hit.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.question_text: May a car squeeze alongside a motorcycle within the same traffic lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.teaching_text: Every motorcycle owns the full width of its lane to maneuver safely around wind gusts and pavement flaws.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.question_text: Why might a motorcyclist move from one side of their lane to the other without changing lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.teaching_text: Slick oil streaks or sharp potholes that barely rattle a car tire can dump a two-wheeled bike instantly.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.question_text: When is a motorcycle allowed to weave between lanes of traffic in Massachusetts?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.teaching_text: Massachusetts bans lane splitting and weaving between traffic lines at all times, even during dead-stopped highway backups.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: If a lane is extra wide and a motorcyclist rides near one edge, may you pull up into the open half?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Riding along the left or right tire track is smart positioning for visibility, not an invitation to crowd beside them.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: When turning left with a motorcycle approaching from the opposite direction, when should you make your turn?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Beating an oncoming bike across an intersection often ends in impact because narrow headlights make closing speed look slower.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: How does a motorcycle's compact profile affect what other drivers see in traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: One slim silhouette vanishes behind pickups and tricks human eyes into thinking the rider is farther away and slower.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: How can loose gravel, potholes, or slick pavement affect a motorcycle ahead of you?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: With only two small tire contact patches, rough or slick spots force instant braking or steering corrections.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: How should you adjust your space behind a motorcycle during rain or bad weather?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Slick roads stretch your car's braking distance while making abrupt stops or slips far likelier for the rider ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: What transmission, maximum engine size, and top speed capability define a moped in Massachusetts?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Cross past automatic gearing, fifty cubic centimeters, or thirty miles per hour capability and the machine stops qualifying as a moped.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: What credential must you hold to legally ride a moped on Massachusetts roads?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Even though mopeds are smaller than motorcycles, riding one without at least a learner permit or driver license breaks state law.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: Even if a moped's design cap is thirty miles per hour, what is the fastest speed you may legally drive one?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: The RMV frequently tests the split between thirty-mile-per-hour design capability and the strict twenty-five-mile-per-hour operating cap.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: Which high-speed highways are off-limits to moped operators?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: A twenty-five-mile-per-hour moped on a limited-access highway posted off-limits to bikes creates an extreme speed-differential hazard.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: What signaling methods must a moped operator use before turning or stopping?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Combining working blinkers with clear arm signals helps drivers behind a compact moped spot stops and turns early.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.question_text: How does Massachusetts treat mopeds on roadside bike lanes compared with off-street recreational paths?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.teaching_text: Street bike lanes allow mopeds, whereas shared off-street rail trails and park paths stay motor-free for walkers and cyclists.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.question_text: Who on a moped must wear a helmet, and what safety standard must it meet?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.teaching_text: Both the operator and any passenger need headgear meeting federal transportation crash protection, not a thin novelty shell.

sec07-card-sec07-R13.question_text: May a moped rider who holds only a learner permit carry a passenger?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.teaching_text: Carrying a second person shifts braking and cornering weight before a permit holder has earned a full driver license.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.question_text: Up to how much can a rider be fined for breaking Massachusetts's listed moped operating rules?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.teaching_text: Skipping a compliant helmet, riding on an off-street path, or speeding past twenty-five can cost up to a hundred bucks.

sec07-card-sec07-R15.question_text: How many wheels, what steering setup, and what power or riding posture define a Massachusetts motorized scooter?
sec07-card-sec07-R15.teaching_text: Gas or electric motors on two or three wheels with handlebars count as motorized scooters whether built to stand or sit.

sec07-card-sec07-R16.question_text: Does the Massachusetts RMV register motorized scooters?
sec07-card-sec07-R16.teaching_text: Even though motorized scooters are never registered at the RMV, riders still face strict licensing, helmet, and daylight rules.

sec07-card-sec07-R17.question_text: What credential do you need before riding a motorized scooter on public roads?
sec07-card-sec07-R17.teaching_text: Lack of registration plates fools people into thinking kids can ride motorized scooters without a permit or license.

sec07-card-sec07-R18.question_text: What is the top legal speed for a motorized scooter, and which highways can it never use?
sec07-card-sec07-R18.teaching_text: Notice the five-mile-per-hour drop below mopeds, capping scooters at twenty and banning them from limited-access state highways.

sec07-card-sec07-R19.question_text: What helmet requirement applies when operating a motorized scooter?
sec07-card-sec07-R19.teaching_text: Small scooter wheels catch easily in pavement cracks, making a federal-standard helmet essential against head impact.

sec07-card-sec07-R20.question_text: Where on the roadway must a motorized-scooter rider stay, even while passing another vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-R20.teaching_text: Unlike cars or mopeds swinging out into center lanes, motorized scooters must stay hugged to the right side.

sec07-card-sec07-R21.question_text: How must a motorized-scooter operator signal before slowing to stop or turning?
sec07-card-sec07-R21.teaching_text: Low-mounted scooter lights sit below many hood lines, so pairing electronic blinkers with clear arm signals prevents rear-end hits.

sec07-card-sec07-R22.question_text: During what hours of the day is operating a motorized scooter illegal?
sec07-card-sec07-R22.teaching_text: Compact frames and tiny lights disappear in darkness, restricting motorized scooters strictly to daylight between sunrise and sunset.

sec07-card-sec07-R23.question_text: When may a motorized scooter carry a passenger in Massachusetts?
sec07-card-sec07-R23.teaching_text: Unlike mopeds ridden by licensed drivers, motorized scooters ban passengers completely regardless of license class.

sec07-card-sec07-R24.question_text: How do fines escalate across first, second, and later motorized-scooter rule violations?
sec07-card-sec07-R24.teaching_text: First citations top out at twenty-five dollars, second offenses run twenty-five to fifty, and third-plus jump from fifty to one hundred.

sec07-card-sec07-R25.question_text: What top-speed bracket defines a limited-use vehicle, and what decides whether it counts as a motorcycle or passenger car?
sec07-card-sec07-R25.teaching_text: Vehicles topping thirty without passing forty miles per hour fall into motorcycle or passenger classes strictly by wheel count.

sec07-card-sec07-R26.question_text: Which license class is needed for a passenger-type limited-use vehicle versus a motorcycle-type one?
sec07-card-sec07-R26.teaching_text: Matching your credential to the vehicle's wheel-based type prevents an unlicensed-operation ticket on a three- or two-wheeled model.
sec07-card-sec07-R26.must_match_memory_hook: Class D passenger, Class M bike

visual_sync.text_span: Class D passenger, Class M bike

sec07-card-sec07-R27.question_text: Which highways and speed-limit zones are off-limits to a limited-use vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-R27.teaching_text: Because its top speed stops at forty miles per hour, roads posted higher than forty or express highways are illegal.

sec07-card-sec07-R28.question_text: What wheel count, weight rating, and speed range define a Massachusetts low-speed vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-R28.teaching_text: Four wheels under three thousand pounds gross weight with a twenty-to-twenty-five-mile-per-hour top speed separate it from golf carts and cars.

sec07-card-sec07-R29.question_text: What license or permit is required to drive a four-wheeled low-speed vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-R29.teaching_text: Neighborhood-style four-wheelers still share public streets, so operators need either a Class D credential or an active permit.

sec07-card-sec07-R30.question_text: Which highways and posted speed limits ban low-speed vehicles?
sec07-card-sec07-R30.teaching_text: Topping out at twenty-five miles per hour keeps low-speed vehicles off expressways and off any street posted above thirty.

sec07-card-sec07-R31.question_text: Beyond thirty-mile-per-hour caps, where else can low-speed vehicles be barred, and how do traffic laws apply?
sec07-card-sec07-R31.teaching_text: Busy downtown corridors can post extra bans to prevent bottlenecks, and operators must obey every standard traffic rule.

sec07-card-sec07-R32.question_text: If police cite a bicyclist for a traffic violation, how does that fine affect the rider's Massachusetts driving record?
sec07-card-sec07-R32.teaching_text: Officers can write a real ticket for running a light on a bike, yet it stays off your RMV driver history.

sec07-card-sec07-R33.question_text: What must a stopped bicyclist tell police when asked, and what happens for lying versus refusing a name?
sec07-card-sec07-R33.teaching_text: Withholding your true name and address brings a fine, and flatly refusing to state your name lets police arrest you.

sec07-card-sec07-R34.question_text: What safety gear must a bicycle-rental business offer to customers?
sec07-card-sec07-R34.teaching_text: State law puts the duty on rental shops to make approved protective helmets available whenever someone rents a bike.

sec07-card-sec07-R35.question_text: What consequence can a motorist face for breaking passing or safety rules around bicyclists?
sec07-card-sec07-R35.teaching_text: Buzzing past inside four feet, cutting off a bike lane, or careless dooring earns drivers a real traffic citation.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: Which three categories of driving events get logged onto your Massachusetts RMV driving record?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Every civil ticket, criminal driving charge, and crash where you hold over half the blame builds your official RMV file.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: How long do a Massachusetts license suspension or revocation take away your right to drive?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Depending on the violation, the RMV pulls your privilege either for a set calendar stretch or open-endedly until cleared.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: Which unpaid bills or court matters block you from renewing an expired Massachusetts driver license?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Ignoring local parking tickets, car excise taxes, highway tolls, or open court warrants freezes your renewal at the RMV.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: What four outcomes can result from receiving a Massachusetts motor-vehicle citation?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Depending on severity, one roadside stop can cost money, pull your license, summon you before a judge, or bring jail.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: Which two serious driving violations does the manual highlight as criminal motor-vehicle offenses?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Operating under the influence and fleeing a crash scene cross straight out of civil tickets into criminal prosecution.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: What can happen to your license if you rack up repeated violations like speeding or running traffic signals?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Even noncriminal habits like blowing lights or speeding stack up fast until the RMV pulls your driving privilege.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: Which three driver factors make penalties steeper across many Massachusetts traffic violations?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Holding a Junior Operator credential, being younger than twenty-one, or repeating mistakes triggers tougher suspensions and fees.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: Can one motor-vehicle offense trigger only one type of punishment, or several at once?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: A single serious charge can hit you simultaneously with a steep fine, a suspended license, and time behind bars.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: How is a civil motor-vehicle infraction classified legally, and how is it usually settled?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Standard moving infractions are noncriminal matters, so most drivers wrap them up without court simply by paying the assessment.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: How many days do you have after getting a civil citation to either pay it or request a court hearing?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Letting that twenty-day calendar window slip shut locks in automatic responsibility and triggers painful late charges.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: What extra surcharge gets tacked onto civil fines under Massachusetts General Laws chapters eighty-nine or ninety?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Standard road-rule tickets under chapters eighty-nine and ninety carry a mandatory five-dollar public-safety add-on.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: What filing fee does the RMV charge when you request a hearing to fight a civil citation?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Booking a magistrate hearing to contest a civil ticket costs twenty-five dollars upfront just to get on the docket.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: Under what exact outcome is your twenty-five-dollar civil-hearing filing fee refunded?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Beating one item while losing another keeps your fee at the court, because refunds require winning every charge on that ticket.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: What happens if you neither pay nor contest a civil citation within twenty days?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Silence past day twenty forfeits your chance to argue and slaps a heavy late penalty onto the unpaid balance.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: What happens to your license if you still fail to pay a civil citation and its added late fee?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: What started as a simple noncriminal ticket snowballs into a full license suspension once late balances go ignored.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: What three events put a finding of responsibility onto your driving record for a civil ticket?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Sending payment counts just like losing in court or blowing past twenty days—all three post responsibility onto your record.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: Which agency logs Massachusetts moving violations, and what two major consequences can follow?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Tracked moving offenses hit both your wallet through higher insurance premiums and your freedom through potential suspension.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: Who administers parking tickets in Massachusetts instead of treating them as civil motor-vehicle infractions?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: You pay or appeal a meter ticket through the local city or town parking clerk rather than the RMV court track.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: Which two RMV renewals get blocked when you leave municipal parking tickets unpaid?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Towns flag delinquent parking plates to the RMV, freezing both your driver license renewal and your car's registration.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: What is the minimum penalty amount for a speeding ticket in Massachusetts?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Even going a few miles over the posted sign starts at one hundred five dollars once the five-dollar surcharge lands.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: How is a Massachusetts speeding fine calculated once you exceed the speed limit by more than ten miles per hour?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: The base fine covers the first ten miles per hour over, then tacks on ten bucks for every extra mile per hour.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: In the Driver's Manual example, what total fine applies for driving seventy-three in a fifty-five-mile-per-hour zone?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Eighteen over means eight miles past the first ten—eighty dollars added onto one hundred five equals one eighty-five.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: How much of every Massachusetts speeding fine goes to the Head Injury Treatment Services Trust Fund?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Half of the base hundred-dollar speeding assessment is earmarked directly for brain-and-head-trauma rehabilitation across the state.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: How does speeding inside a posted highway work zone change your fine?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Road crews work feet from live bumpers, so Massachusetts doubles the speeding penalty inside active posted work zones.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: What license penalty hits a driver who racks up three speeding findings within twelve months?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Collecting three responsible speeding outcomes inside a rolling year sidelines you automatically for thirty days.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: How long is a Junior Operator suspended after a first speeding offense versus a second or later one?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Unlike adults who get three strikes, one single Junior Operator speeding ticket pulls your privilege for ninety days immediately.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: What four immediate roadside actions can happen when you commit a criminal motor-vehicle offense?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Criminal traffic charges skip mail-in tickets—police can cuff you, tow your car, take your card, and hold you for court.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: Who decides the fine or prison sentence after a conviction for a criminal motor-vehicle offense?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: While the RMV enforces administrative license suspensions, only a judge in court sets criminal fines and jail terms.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.question_text: Along with impaired driving and leaving a crash, what third major offense is listed as a criminal driving crime?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.teaching_text: Getting behind the wheel while suspended puts you in the same criminal court bucket as OUI and hit-and-run.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.question_text: What can happen if you refuse to tell an officer your name and address or the vehicle owner's name and address?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.teaching_text: Stonewalling police about who is driving or who owns the car escalates a traffic stop into arrest and criminal charges.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.question_text: What happens if you refuse to hand over your license or registration, or refuse to sign your name for an officer?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.teaching_text: Massachusetts law requires displaying both credentials and signing in the officer's presence when asked, under penalty of arrest.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.question_text: How do traffic violations committed in other states affect your Massachusetts driving record?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.teaching_text: Crossing state lines gives zero immunity—out-of-state convictions post to your RMV history as if they happened in Boston.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.question_text: What happens in Massachusetts if you ignore a ticket payment or court date in another state?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.teaching_text: States share default notices electronically, so ghosting a New Hampshire or Connecticut ticket suspends your home license.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.question_text: Whose suspension rules apply to an out-of-state violation, and how can they compare with the other state's penalty?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.teaching_text: Even if another state lets you off with a small fine, the RMV enforces Massachusetts's own harsher suspension schedule.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: What two things must you provide to get reinstated after a suspension caused by an unresolved out-of-state ticket?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Paying the other state is only step one—you still owe clearance proof and at least one hundred dollars to Massachusetts.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: What standard does an insurer apply as part of determining whether a crash counts as at-fault?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Insurance adjusters match crash facts against preset scenarios like rear-ending or driving wrong-side to assign majority blame.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: Above what insurer-payout dollar mark does an at-fault collision or lone bodily-injury claim trigger a surchargeable crash?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Modern bumper repairs easily top one thousand dollars, turning minor fender-benders into official surchargeable record events.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: How does the RMV treat charged at-fault crashes alongside traffic tickets on your record?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Crashes where you carry majority blame sit right beside speeding tickets in the tally that can pull your license.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: Which two broad categories make up Massachusetts surchargeable events?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Knowing that moving tickets and majority-fault wrecks share the same surchargeable bucket explains how drivers hit suspension thresholds fast.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: What exact event starts the twelve-month countdown for the three-speeding-tickets suspension rule?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Test trap alert—the rolling year starts on the date you pay or are found guilty, not the roadside stop date.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: How long is a Junior Operator's license suspended for a first drag-racing citation versus a repeat citation?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Street racing on a junior credential wipes out an entire year immediately and triples to three years if repeated.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: What happens if you accumulate three surchargeable events within two years, and how fast must you act?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Miss that ninety-day completion window after three events in two years and your license suspends until you finish class.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: What automatic penalty kicks in when a driver hits seven surchargeable events within three years?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: Piling up seven combined tickets and at-fault crashes across three years triggers a mandatory two-month suspension with no grace.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: Which Massachusetts board runs the Safe Driver Insurance Plan that links driving records to insurance premiums?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: Every ticket or surchargeable claim flows through that state board so insurers can price risk under plan rules.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.question_text: Under the Safe Driver Insurance Plan, what pushes your insurance rate up and what can bring it down?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.teaching_text: Moving convictions or crashes above fifty percent blame hike your bill for years, while clean driving earns plan discounts.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.question_text: What does the Massachusetts Driver Retraining Course target instead of hands-on steering and braking skills?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.teaching_text: Repeat violators usually know how pedals work—the class confronts risk-taking habits, impatience, and poor decisions behind the wheel.

sec08-card-sec08-R13.question_text: What does the RMV mail you once your record hits at least three surchargeable events?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.teaching_text: Watch your mailbox closely—the ninety-day countdown runs whether or not you open the RMV's enrollment packet on time.

sec08-card-sec08-R14.question_text: How many total hours is the Massachusetts driver-retraining program, and how are sessions scheduled?
sec08-card-sec08-R14.teaching_text: Expect eight classroom hours total, split across two four-hour sessions or occasionally packed into one full Saturday.

sec08-card-sec08-R15.question_text: Does finishing driver retraining wipe surcharges off your record or substitute for other mandatory courses?
sec08-card-sec08-R15.teaching_text: Completing the eight-hour class only prevents the ninety-day default suspension—every prior point, surcharge, and other course stays.

sec08-card-sec08-R16.question_text: If you strike a stationary parked car that was parked illegally, how do Massachusetts fault standards treat the crash?
sec08-card-sec08-R16.teaching_text: Classic test trap—hitting a motionless vehicle puts you over fifty percent at fault even if they parked in a no-parking zone.

sec08-card-sec08-R17.question_text: How do Massachusetts insurer fault standards classify striking the back of the vehicle ahead of you?
sec08-card-sec08-R17.teaching_text: Safe following gaps give you stopping room, so running into someone's rear bumper lands squarely on the preset fault list.

sec08-card-sec08-R18.question_text: What fault status applies when a crash happens because a driver drifts or cuts outside their marked lane?
sec08-card-sec08-R18.teaching_text: Sideswiping adjacent traffic while wandering over lane stripes triggers an automatic insurer fault-standard finding.

sec08-card-sec08-R19.question_text: How do Massachusetts fault rules treat a crash tied to turning or changing lanes without signaling?
sec08-card-sec08-R19.teaching_text: Moving without a blinker robs surrounding drivers of warning and places your crash straight onto the insurer fault list.

sec08-card-sec08-R20.question_text: What fault rule applies if you pull out from a traffic light or stop sign without checking that the way is clear?
sec08-card-sec08-R20.teaching_text: Even a fresh green light or completed stop requires verifying clear cross-traffic before rolling forward into an intersection.

sec08-card-sec08-R21.question_text: How do insurer fault standards treat a collision that occurs while your vehicle is on the wrong side of the road?
sec08-card-sec08-R21.teaching_text: Drifting or passing across the center divider into opposing lanes triggers a clear-cut majority-fault surcharge finding.

sec08-card-sec08-R22.question_text: What fault consequence follows crashing while driving the wrong way down a roadway or ramp?
sec08-card-sec08-R22.teaching_text: Entering a one-way street, rotary, or highway ramp backward guarantees majority fault under Massachusetts insurance standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R23.question_text: Does Massachusetts include crashes at intersections without signals or signs among its preset insurer fault standards?
sec08-card-sec08-R23.teaching_text: Failing to yield properly where two unsigned streets cross puts the resulting wreck directly under state fault standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R24.question_text: How is blame treated under Massachusetts fault standards when a crash happens while you are backing up?
sec08-card-sec08-R24.teaching_text: Drivers in reverse bear the duty to keep the path behind clear, making backing hits a textbook surchargeable event.

sec08-card-sec08-R25.question_text: How do insurer fault standards treat a crash during a left turn or U-turn across another vehicle's path?
sec08-card-sec08-R25.teaching_text: Turning across oncoming or through lanes requires yielding first, so misjudging that gap lands on the fault list.

sec08-card-sec08-R26.question_text: What fault rule applies when pulling out from a curb space, parking lot, alley, or private driveway causes a crash?
sec08-card-sec08-R26.teaching_text: Traffic already moving on the street holds right of way over anyone pulling out from roadside spaces or driveways.

sec08-card-sec08-R27.question_text: If opening your car door or leaving it open into traffic causes a collision, how is fault assigned?
sec08-card-sec08-R27.teaching_text: Swinging a street-side door into passing cars or cyclists makes the door opener majority at fault under state standards.

sec08-card-sec08-R28.question_text: If no other driver is involved and you crash into a guardrail, tree, or ditch, how do fault standards treat it?
sec08-card-sec08-R28.teaching_text: Sliding solo into a pole or curb above the payout threshold still triggers a surchargeable at-fault crash on your record.

sec08-card-sec08-R29.question_text: How do Massachusetts fault standards treat a collision caused by breaking general driving rules and regulations?
sec08-card-sec08-R29.teaching_text: Even if a crash scenario looks unusual, violating state road regulations to cause it triggers majority insurer fault.

sec08-card-sec08-R30.question_text: What fault standard covers a crash involving an unattended vehicle, such as one that rolls away?
sec08-card-sec08-R30.teaching_text: Failing to secure your parking brake and gear so an empty car rolls into damage counts as a listed fault event.

sec08-card-sec08-R31.question_text: How do insurer fault standards treat a crash that happens while you merge onto a highway or enter a rotary?
sec08-card-sec08-R31.teaching_text: Vehicles already circulating in a Massachusetts rotary or cruising on a highway have priority over entering traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R32.question_text: Can you be found majority at fault under Massachusetts standards if you force another car to crash without touching it?
sec08-card-sec08-R32.teaching_text: Cutting someone off so sharply that they hit a barrier makes you at fault even with zero paint traded.

sec08-card-sec08-R33.question_text: What fault rule applies when a collision results from failing to yield legally to an emergency vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R33.teaching_text: Ignoring flashing lights and sirens instead of pulling right and stopping puts any resulting collision onto your record.

sec08-card-sec08-R34.question_text: At a T-intersection, how do fault standards treat a driver who pulls out from the terminating side street and crashes?
sec08-card-sec08-R34.teaching_text: Drivers on the ending stem road must yield to through traffic on the top bar of the T every time.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: How much does an attested Massachusetts driving record cost compared with an unattested copy, and where is the cheaper one sold?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Save twelve dollars when you do not need a certified stamp by ordering the eight-dollar unattested copy online.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: Through which four channels can you request an attested Massachusetts driving record?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Unlike online-only unattested copies, certified attested records are available online, by mail, at RMV centers, or via Court Records.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: Which three sensitive categories of information are shielded from public Massachusetts driving records?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Privacy rules keep select drug convictions, expired warrants, and child-support actions hidden from standard public record checks.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: When can the RMV suspend a learner permit or driver license immediately without waiting?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Whenever a driver's conduct poses an urgent danger on public streets, the RMV pulls credentials on the spot.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: What administrative action can the RMV take for improper operation of a motor vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Unsafe handling behind the wheel gives the RMV direct authority to suspend your driving privileges.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: How long can your license be suspended for a listed false-identification offense without a court conviction versus after conviction?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: You do not even need a criminal conviction to lose six months—and a court conviction doubles it to one year.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: Which four types of card or application misconduct count as Massachusetts false-identification offenses?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Tampering with a card, printing fakes, flashing someone else's ID, or lying on an RMV form all trigger suspension.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.question_text: Before Massachusetts will lift a suspension tied to another state's action, what must happen first?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.teaching_text: The RMV will never restore your home license while another state still lists you as suspended or revoked.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.question_text: Once another state reinstates you, how recent must your reinstatement letter or driving record be when shown to the RMV?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.teaching_text: Bring paperwork older than thirty days and the RMV will turn it away or ask for fresh verification.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.question_text: How does the RMV decide whether an out-of-state ticket counts as a 'like offense' in Massachusetts?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.teaching_text: Even if another state calls the violation minor or civil, Massachusetts matches the underlying driving behavior itself.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.question_text: If another state convicts you of a like offense without suspending you there, what does Massachusetts do?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.teaching_text: Avoiding license loss in the state where you got cited will not shield you from Massachusetts's mandatory suspension schedule.

sec09-card-sec09-R17.question_text: Once your license or permit is suspended or revoked, when must you stop driving and where are you barred from driving?
sec09-card-sec09-R17.teaching_text: An invalid Massachusetts credential bans you behind the wheel right away both inside the Commonwealth and across state lines.

sec09-card-sec09-R18.question_text: How does Massachusetts classify driving on a suspended or revoked license, and what punishments can follow?
sec09-card-sec09-R18.teaching_text: Getting caught behind the wheel while suspended turns an administrative hold into a criminal arrest risking prison and extra penalties.

sec09-card-sec09-R19.question_text: With whom does a suspended driver have the right to meet regarding license reinstatement?
sec09-card-sec09-R19.teaching_text: Drivers seeking reinstatement or checking a record error have the right to present their matter to an RMV Hearings Officer.

sec09-card-sec09-R20.question_text: What does an RMV suspension hearing review and generally verify?
sec09-card-sec09-R20.teaching_text: Suspension hearings are not second trials on the ticket—they check whether your record is accurate and mandatory law fits.

sec09-card-sec09-R21.question_text: Can a Hearings Officer block a valid suspension after a guilty or responsible finding, and how long can a decision take?
sec09-card-sec09-R21.teaching_text: Once a court logs guilt or responsibility, a valid mandatory suspension stands, and complex rulings can take ten business days.

sec09-card-sec09-R22.question_text: What is the typical Massachusetts reinstatement fee, and how high can it climb for serious offenses?
sec09-card-sec09-R22.teaching_text: Routine suspensions cost one hundred dollars to clear, while major repeat OUI cases spike all the way to twelve hundred.

sec09-card-sec09-R23.question_text: What extra steps apply to get reinstated after a suspension that lasted two years or longer?
sec09-card-sec09-R23.teaching_text: Spend at least two years off the road and you must bring fresh ID documents and pass full knowledge and road exams.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: For drivers eighteen or older, what suspension and reinstatement fee follow three speeding findings within one year?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Adults get three speeding strikes inside a year before triggering a thirty-day timeout and a hundred-dollar restore fee.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: What happens when a driver eighteen or older hits three surchargeable events in two years?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Skip that ninety-day retraining deadline and an indefinite suspension locks your license until you finish and pay one hundred dollars.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: What penalty and reinstatement fee hit a driver eighteen or older with seven surchargeable events in three years?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Seven surchargeable hits in three years trigger a sixty-day mandatory suspension plus a hundred-dollar fee to return.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: What five-year violation totals brand you a habitual traffic offender, and what suspension and fee follow?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Three major moving convictions—or twelve combined major and minor ones—in five years wipe out four years of driving.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: In the adult mandatory table, how long does an out-of-state suspension block you in Massachusetts, and what fee applies?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Your Massachusetts status stays frozen for as long as the other state keeps you suspended, plus one hundred dollars to restore.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: When during a mandatory suspension for qualifying drug-trafficking offenses may a person apply for a hardship license?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Unlike waiting periods attached to many driving suspensions, eligible drug-trafficking suspensions allow a hardship petition immediately.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: What suspension lengths and reinstatement fee hit a junior permit holder caught driving unaccompanied on first, second, and later offenses?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Driving a learner permit without a qualified supervising adult jumps from sixty days to six months to a full year.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: What exam or course requirements apply after first and second junior-permit unaccompanied-driving offenses?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Every solo-permit catch forces you to pass the learner permit exam again, and catch number two tacks on attitudinal retraining.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: What suspension progression and reinstatement fee apply to a junior-permit nighttime driving violation?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Breaking the junior-permit night rule mirrors unaccompanied driving—sixty days first, one hundred eighty second, one year third.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: Which exams or courses are required after first and second junior-permit nighttime violations?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Just like solo-permit violations, every curfew ticket resets your permit exam and adds Driver Attitudinal Retraining on offense two.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: What suspension, testing, and fee penalties hit a junior-permit holder caught speeding?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Notice the permit fee difference—speeding on a junior permit carries a hundred-dollar restore fee alongside ninety-day or one-year loss.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: What suspension lengths and reinstatement fees apply to first and repeat drag racing on a junior permit?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Street racing on a permit pulls a year and five hundred dollars first, then three years and one thousand later.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: What testing and courses are required after any junior-permit drag-racing offense?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Every permit street-racing offense mandates both Driver Attitudinal Retraining and a fresh permit exam, plus possible SCARR enrollment.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: How long is a junior permit suspended for first, second, and later mobile-device violations, and what is the restore fee?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Touching a phone behind the wheel on a junior permit triggers sixty days right away, climbing to six months and one year.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: What fines and first-offense requirements hit a junior permit holder cited for using a mobile device?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Even your very first permit phone ticket costs one hundred dollars, Driver Attitudinal Retraining, and a brand-new permit exam.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: What suspension terms and reinstatement fee apply to negligent operation with phone-caused injury on a junior permit?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Hurting someone while distracted by a phone on a permit jumps straight to six months first and five hundred to restore.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: When does a junior-permit negligent-operation-and-phone-injury offense require retaking the permit exam?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: In the junior-permit table, the mandatory new permit exam kicks in on a second or subsequent phone-injury conviction.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: What suspension ladder and reinstatement fee hit a Junior Operator License holder for passenger or nighttime violations?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Breaking under-eighteen passenger caps or late-night curfew costs sixty days first, six months second, and a year third.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: When do Junior Operator License passenger or nighttime violations trigger retraining versus full permit and road retesting?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Offense two mandates retraining, and offense three wipes your slate back to passing both the permit exam and road test.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: What suspension terms and reinstatement fee apply to a speeding conviction on a Junior Operator License?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Spot the huge trap—speeding on a Junior License charges a five-hundred-dollar reinstatement fee versus one hundred on a permit.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: What exams and courses must a Junior Operator License holder complete after even a single speeding conviction?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: One JOL speeding ticket forces you back through the permit exam, retraining, a fresh road test, and possibly SCARR.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: What suspension lengths and first-offense reinstatement fee apply to drag racing on a Junior Operator License?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Racing on a JOL pulls your license for one full year first—with a five-hundred-dollar fee—and three years if repeated.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: Which tests and courses are required after every Junior Operator License drag-racing offense?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: Getting back on the road after JOL street racing requires passing the permit exam, retraining, a road test, and possibly SCARR.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: What suspension terms and reinstatement fee hit a Junior Operator convicted of reckless or negligent operation?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: Reckless or negligent operation pulls six months first—jumping to a full year if repeated within three years—plus five hundred dollars.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.question_text: When must a Junior Operator retake both the permit exam and road test for reckless or negligent operation?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.teaching_text: A repeat reckless or negligent conviction sends a Junior Operator back to square one for both permit and road exams.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.question_text: What suspension progression and reinstatement fee apply to a mobile-device conviction on a Junior Operator License?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.teaching_text: Holding or tapping a phone on a JOL sidelines you sixty days first, six months second, and one year third.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.question_text: What fine ladder and first-offense retesting hit a Junior Operator License holder convicted of mobile-device use?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.teaching_text: Unlike adults, one single JOL phone ticket costs one hundred dollars plus retraining, a permit exam, and a road test.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.question_text: What suspension lengths and reinstatement fee follow negligent operation with phone-related injury on a Junior Operator License?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.teaching_text: Causing an injury crash while using a phone on a JOL brings a six-month or one-year suspension and five hundred dollars.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.question_text: When does a Junior Operator License phone-injury offense require a new permit exam and road test?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.teaching_text: A second or subsequent phone-injury conviction forces a Junior Operator to pass both the permit exam and road test again.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.question_text: Who else gets notified whenever a Junior Operator receives a license or permit suspension?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.teaching_text: There is no hiding a junior suspension at home—the RMV reports the action directly to your parent or guardian.

sec09-card-sec09-F38.question_text: How long is the extra Junior Operator suspension for specified serious convictions, and what exception prevents double counting?
sec09-card-sec09-F38.teaching_text: First convictions add one hundred eighty days—and repeats add a year—unless a chemical-test failure or refusal already added time.

sec09-card-sec09-F39.question_text: Which alcohol, endangerment, and crash-scene crimes sit on the additional Junior Operator suspension list?
sec09-card-sec09-F39.teaching_text: Impaired driving, alcohol-injury crashes, open-container drinking, endangerment, and leaving a crash all tack extra time onto junior suspensions.

sec09-card-sec09-F40.question_text: Which four non-alcohol serious offenses also trigger the additional Junior Operator suspension?
sec09-card-sec09-F40.teaching_text: Unauthorized car use, reckless or negligent driving, loaning out your credential, and vehicular homicide all carry extra junior suspension time.

sec09-card-sec09-F41.question_text: How many times must a Junior Operator complete the RMV-mandated SCARR program, and who else can order it?
sec09-card-sec09-F41.teaching_text: Even if multiple junior triggers mention SCARR, the RMV requires completing that crash-reduction course only once unless a judge orders more.

sec09-card-sec09-F42.question_text: Which five non-driving obligations or convictions can get your Massachusetts license suspended?
sec09-card-sec09-F42.teaching_text: Unpaid child support, skipped sex-offender registration, qualifying drug trafficking, unpaid state income taxes, or bounced RMV payments all pull licenses.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: What amounts and payment methods are required to clear a bad-payment suspension with the RMV?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Personal checks will not clear a bounced payment—bring cash or a certified bank check to MassDOT including the fifteen-dollar penalty.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: In the criminal suspension table, what suspension range and reinstatement fee apply for driving on a suspended or revoked license?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Getting convicted of driving while suspended tacks another sixty days to a year onto your wait plus five hundred dollars.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: What suspension range and reinstatement fee follow unauthorized vehicle operation or vehicle larceny?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Joyriding without permission or stealing a car pulls your privilege for up to three years and costs five hundred dollars.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: What suspension term and reinstatement fee hit a driver convicted of leaving an injury crash?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Walking or driving away when someone is hurt carries one to two years off the road and five hundred dollars.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: How long is the suspension and what is the reinstatement fee for leaving a property-damage crash?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Even when nobody is hurt, fleeing a bent fender or struck fence brings sixty days to a year plus five hundred.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: What suspension range and reinstatement fee apply to a conviction for operating to endanger?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Driving recklessly enough to put lives at risk pulls your license from two months up to twelve plus five hundred.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: What suspension span and reinstatement fee apply to motor-vehicle homicide or vehicular manslaughter?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Causing a death through criminal operation strips your driving privilege for at least fifteen years and potentially for life.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: What is the exact suspension sequence across first, second, third, fourth, and fifth OUI convictions?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Notice the huge jump at offense three—OUI suspensions climb from one and two years straight to eight, ten, and lifetime.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: How do reinstatement fees progress from a first through fifth OUI conviction?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Fees climb from five hundred to seven hundred to twelve hundred on third and fourth convictions, and offense five never reinstates.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: What suspension and fee apply to qualifying drug-trafficking convictions outside Class D substances, even if no car was used?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Trafficking non-Class-D controlled substances pulls your license one to five years even when the crime happened nowhere near a vehicle.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.question_text: For a driver older than eighteen, what suspension range and reinstatement-fee range apply to drag racing?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.teaching_text: Adults convicted of street racing lose thirty to one hundred eighty days and pay five hundred to one thousand dollars.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.question_text: In the criminal table, what suspension range and restore fee apply to negligent operation causing injury through mobile-phone use?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.teaching_text: Injuring someone because you looked at a phone carries sixty days to a year off the road plus five hundred dollars.

sec09-card-sec09-R24.question_text: What court fine range, maximum jail time, and standard license suspension apply to a first OUI conviction?
sec09-card-sec09-R24.teaching_text: Even a first impaired-driving conviction exposes you to five thousand dollars in fines, two and a half years, and one year suspended.

sec09-card-sec09-R25.question_text: If a court allows alcohol education on a first OUI, how short can the suspension drop for drivers over twenty-one versus under twenty-one?
sec09-card-sec09-R25.teaching_text: Court-approved alcohol education trims an adult's first suspension to forty-five through ninety days, while under-twenty-one drivers still serve two hundred ten.

sec09-card-sec09-R26.question_text: What fine range, prison term, and suspension apply to a second OUI conviction?
sec09-card-sec09-R26.teaching_text: Conviction number two introduces a thirty-day jail floor up to two and a half years, ten-thousand-dollar max fine, and two years suspended.

sec09-card-sec09-R27.question_text: How is a third OUI classified, and what fine, prison range, and suspension does it carry?
