sec09-card-sec09-R27.teaching_text: Offense three crosses into felony status—carrying up to fifteen thousand in fines, five months minimum prison, and eight years suspended.

sec09-card-sec09-R28.question_text: What felony penalties apply upon a fourth Massachusetts OUI conviction?
sec09-card-sec09-R28.teaching_text: A fourth OUI brings a felony record, fifteen hundred to twenty-five thousand in fines, one to five years imprisoned, and ten years suspended.

sec09-card-sec09-R29.question_text: What fine range, prison term, and license loss hit a driver convicted of a fifth OUI?
sec09-card-sec09-R29.teaching_text: A fifth felony OUI permanently ends your driving privilege alongside two to five years in prison and up to fifty thousand dollars.

sec09-card-sec09-R30.question_text: At what blood-alcohol content reading does every driver fail a chemical test in Massachusetts?
sec09-card-sec09-R30.teaching_text: Registering zero point zero eight or higher triggers an immediate administrative chemical-test failure regardless of age.

sec09-card-sec09-R31.question_text: How do the criminal standard and administrative sanction threshold compare for drivers younger than twenty-one?
sec09-card-sec09-R31.teaching_text: Underage drivers face the same criminal court standard, yet just zero point zero two triggers immediate youth administrative sanctions.

sec09-card-sec09-R32.question_text: How long is the failed-chemical-test suspension for a driver over twenty-one?
sec09-card-sec09-R32.teaching_text: Drivers over twenty-one serve either thirty days or until the court case wraps up, whichever finishes sooner.

sec09-card-sec09-R33.question_text: What failed-test suspension applies to drivers aged eighteen to twenty-one, and how can a first-time OUI case trim the extra period?
sec09-card-sec09-R33.teaching_text: Enrolling in approved alcohol education on a first case waives the extra six-month youth sanction after the base thirty days.

sec09-card-sec09-R34.question_text: What failed-test suspension hits a driver under eighteen, and how much can alcohol education trim it on a first OUI?
sec09-card-sec09-R34.teaching_text: Drivers under eighteen cannot waive the extra year completely—approved education only cuts that added year down to one hundred eighty days.

sec09-card-sec09-R35.question_text: If an under-twenty-one driver wins their OUI court case, what happens to the alcohol-education duty tied to the failed test?
sec09-card-sec09-R35.teaching_text: Youth chemical-test rules are administrative, so even a not-guilty verdict in court leaves the alcohol-education requirement standing.

sec09-card-sec09-R36.question_text: Under the chemical-test refusal table, what counts as a prior OUI and what specifically does not?
sec09-card-sec09-R36.teaching_text: Classic exam distinction—past convictions or court-assigned alcohol programs count as priors, whereas an earlier test refusal alone does not.

sec09-card-sec09-R37.question_text: For drivers over twenty-one, how long are chemical-test refusal suspensions with zero, one, two, or three-plus prior OUIs?
sec09-card-sec09-R37.teaching_text: Refusing the breath test over twenty-one jumps from six months with clean history to three years, five years, and life.

sec09-card-sec09-R38.question_text: What refusal suspensions apply to ages eighteen through twenty-one with zero or one prior, two priors, or three-plus priors?
sec09-card-sec09-R38.teaching_text: Notice that zero and one prior both start at three years plus one hundred eighty days before climbing to five-plus-one-eighty and life.

sec09-card-sec09-R39.question_text: What refusal suspensions hit drivers under eighteen across zero or one prior, two priors, and three-plus priors?
sec09-card-sec09-R39.teaching_text: Under eighteen swaps the extra six months for a full added year—making it four years total first, six with two priors, then life.

sec09-card-sec09-R40.question_text: On a first OUI case, what does approved alcohol education waive for an eighteen-to-twenty-one driver who refused testing?
sec09-card-sec09-R40.teaching_text: Approved alcohol education wipes out the extra one hundred eighty days, though the base three-year refusal suspension still remains.

sec09-card-sec09-R41.question_text: For a driver under eighteen in a first OUI case, how does approved alcohol education change the added refusal suspension?
sec09-card-sec09-R41.teaching_text: Just like failed tests under eighteen, approved education cuts the extra refusal year in half rather than waiving it completely.

sec09-card-sec09-R42.question_text: Does winning your OUI case in court cancel the added underage refusal suspension or its alcohol-education rule?
sec09-card-sec09-R42.teaching_text: Refusal sanctions run on an independent RMV track, so beating the charge in court leaves underage time and coursework intact.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: How is alcohol classified as a drug, and which four core driving abilities can it impair?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Slowing the central nervous system delays hazard recognition, steering coordination, and braking decisions all at once.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: Can small amounts of alcohol, other drugs, or nonprescription medicine weaken safe driving skills?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Waiting until you feel impaired ignores how early trace doses and over-the-counter drugs degrade split-second control.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: Must a driver look visibly drunk or fully intoxicated to become dangerous after substance use?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Subtle tracking errors and slowed reactions start well before slurred speech or stumbling ever show up.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: What happens to driving safety whenever you use any substance that alters awareness or reflexes?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Safe traffic scanning depends on sharp alertness and fast muscle response to sudden braking ahead.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: How can alcohol distort a driver's confidence and willingness to take road risks?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Impaired self-judgment tricks drivers into attempting tight gaps or high speeds they would soberly reject.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: Which three unsafe driving habits become more likely after a person drinks alcohol?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Skipping the seat belt while driving faster and weaving compounds both crash probability and injury severity.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: Beyond court OUI fines, what separate payment is required before the RMV restores a license?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Settling court fines alone leaves your driving privilege suspended until every Registry reinstatement fee clears.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: Can just one drink in an hour impair driving, and what personal states worsen that effect?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Being tired, emotionally upset, or driving on an empty stomach magnifies impairment from even one drink.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: What travel arrangement should you make before planning to drink or after drinking alcohol?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Locking in a sober designated driver, taxi, rideshare, or trusted ride beforehand eliminates impaired-driving temptation.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: Do coffee, cold showers, exercise, or food actually speed up alcohol removal from your body?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Caffeine or cold water only creates a wide-awake impaired driver while blood alcohol stays unchanged.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: What does blood-alcohol content measure, and which two test types can determine it?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Chemical testing quantifies circulating alcohol your liver has not yet metabolized, regardless of perceived sobriety.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: Which five personal and drinking factors determine a person's blood-alcohol content?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Two friends finishing identical drinks can reach very different BAC levels based on body size and stomach contents.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: Does the beverage category matter more for impairment, or the total alcohol consumed over time?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Switching from liquor to beer or wine offers zero protection when total ethanol intake stays high.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: Which serving sizes of beer, wine, and eighty-proof liquor carry roughly equal amounts of alcohol?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: A standard can of beer, glass of wine, and one-and-a-half-ounce liquor shot deliver comparable pure alcohol.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: What is the single thing that eliminates alcohol's impairing effects from your body?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Your liver oxidizes alcohol at a fixed pace that willpower, fresh air, or snacks cannot rush.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: Under Massachusetts implied-consent law, what do licensed drivers agree to submit to?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Operating on Massachusetts roadways carries automatic legal agreement to chemical breath or blood testing when required.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: When a police officer suspects a driver is impaired by alcohol, what roadside evaluation may be requested?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Officers use roadside balance, eye-tracking, and divided-attention tasks to evaluate suspected alcohol impairment.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: Following an arrest for alcohol-impaired driving, what tests may an officer request to measure BAC?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: An OUI arrest triggers formal chemical testing to record exact blood-alcohol concentration for court and RMV action.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: Which blood-alcohol content number reaches the standard legal-limit threshold in Massachusetts?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: Reaching eight-hundredths of a percent triggers per se legal-limit enforcement, though lower levels still impair driving.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: At what blood-alcohol content does a driver younger than twenty-one face zero-tolerance penalties?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Even a fraction of one drink pushes an underage driver past Massachusetts' strict zero-tolerance cutoff.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: What immediate actions must an officer take if you fail or refuse a breath or blood test?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Refusing chemical testing never saves your license on the spot because confiscation and suspension take effect immediately.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: When must an OUI offender pay to install an ignition interlock device for reinstatement or hardship driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Repeat OUI history mandates breath-tested vehicle startup paid entirely out of the returning driver's pocket.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: How long must a required ignition interlock stay in use across hardship and reinstated driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Completing a hardship period does not end monitoring because two full post-reinstatement years still remain.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: Which three vehicle features let an interlock-required applicant schedule a road test online?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Examiners need accessible emergency braking and proper seating alongside the installed breath device during road testing.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: How must an interlock road test be booked if the car lacks a center-console brake or sponsor seat?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Nonstandard vehicle layouts bypass self-service online booking so a supervisor can review test safety arrangements.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.question_text: May a person under twenty-one purchase alcohol directly or arrange for someone else to buy it?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.teaching_text: Both walking up to the register yourself and recruiting an older buyer violate underage alcohol law.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.question_text: When is someone younger than twenty-one allowed to possess, carry, or transport alcohol?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.teaching_text: Driving unopened drinks for older friends without a parent or legal guardian riding along still triggers penalties.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.question_text: What license suspension range applies to prohibited underage alcohol possession, carrying, or transport?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.teaching_text: You do not even have to take a sip in the car to lose driving privileges for months.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: How long is the license suspension specifically assigned for underage buying or attempting to buy alcohol?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Even an unsuccessful attempt at the counter costs roughly half a year of legal driving privileges.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: Is drinking any alcoholic beverage while driving ever permitted in Massachusetts?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Consuming alcohol behind the wheel is flatly illegal regardless of whether your BAC stays below zero point zero eight.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: Is an open alcoholic beverage legal inside your vehicle if a passenger holds it instead of you?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Handing an unsealed can or cup to a sober passenger still violates the cabin open-container ban.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: What dollar fine range applies to an open-container conviction in Massachusetts?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Carrying an unsealed alcoholic drink inside the passenger area brings immediate triple-digit financial penalties.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: Which three consequences hit an offender younger than twenty-one who breaks the open-container rule?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Underage offenders face custodial arrest and license loss on top of the standard financial fine.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: Is using, altering, borrowing, or lying for an ID illegal even when not trying to buy alcohol?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Possessing or tampering with credentials is a standalone offense whether or not alcohol is ever involved.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: How long can the RMV suspend your license for ID fraud without a conviction versus after conviction?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Administrative RMV action can pull your license for six months before court, and conviction doubles it to one year.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: Beyond legal penalties, what personal security danger comes with ordering false identification online?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Handing personal photos, addresses, and payment details to illicit ID sellers exposes buyers directly to identity theft.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.question_text: Do Massachusetts OUI laws cover impairing prescription and over-the-counter medicines as well as alcohol?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.teaching_text: A valid pharmacy label or store receipt never excuses driving when a medication dulls safe control.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.question_text: How can marijuana affect a driver's reaction to sights, sounds, and rapid sequences of road tasks?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.teaching_text: Complex merges and city intersections demand rapid chained reactions that cannabis impairment breaks apart.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.question_text: Why does marijuana create added danger when unexpected driving hazards appear at night?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.teaching_text: Degraded night vision leaves less time to spot dark-clothed pedestrians, cyclists, or unlit obstacles ahead.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.question_text: Does adult marijuana legalization or decriminalization make driving under marijuana's influence legal for any age?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.teaching_text: Adult possession rules never carry over to behind-the-wheel operation, which remains a crime at every age.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.question_text: Which penalty schedule governs drivers convicted of operating under the influence of marijuana?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.teaching_text: Cannabis-impaired driving triggers the exact same fines, suspensions, and criminal sanctions as alcohol OUI.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.question_text: How do prescription sedatives and tranquilizers make operating a motor vehicle hazardous?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.teaching_text: Calming medications depress alertness enough to cause microsleeps and delayed braking in live traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.question_text: How can illegal drugs like LSD, heroin, and opium distort a driver's situational awareness?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.teaching_text: Losing track of where you are or caring less about nearby traffic makes safe vehicle control impossible.

sec10-card-sec10-R16.question_text: How can cold, allergy, headache, pain, or codeine medicines affect your fitness to drive?
sec10-card-sec10-R16.teaching_text: Everyday allergy pills and codeine pain relievers cause heavy drowsiness that rivals alcohol behind the wheel.

sec10-card-sec10-R17.question_text: Can taking your own prescribed medication still result in an illegal OUI violation?
sec10-card-sec10-R17.teaching_text: Traffic law judges whether your driving ability is impaired, not whether a doctor wrote the prescription.

sec10-card-sec10-R18.question_text: What dangerous symptoms follow temporary alertness from stimulants, including effects on eyesight?
sec10-card-sec10-R18.teaching_text: Once artificial energy wears off mid-trip, sudden exhaustion, jitters, dizziness, and blurred vision take over.

sec10-card-sec10-R19.question_text: What two dangers arise from inhaling solvent or glue vapors?
sec10-card-sec10-R19.teaching_text: Toxic chemical fumes rapidly starve brain function, wrecking vehicle control while risking severe medical harm.

sec10-card-sec10-R20.question_text: What two steps should you take to check side effects before driving on any medicine?
sec10-card-sec10-R20.teaching_text: Checking warning labels and consulting professionals catches hidden drowsiness or drug-interaction warnings before you drive.

sec10-card-sec10-R21.question_text: What happens when you combine alcohol with another drug or medication?
sec10-card-sec10-R21.teaching_text: Alcohol compounds drug side effects synergistically rather than merely adding them together, accelerating severe impairment.

sec10-card-sec10-R22.question_text: Which two municipal vehicle citations can block you from renewing your Massachusetts license?
sec10-card-sec10-R22.teaching_text: Ignoring local parking tickets or abandoned-vehicle notices places an administrative hold on your next RMV renewal.

sec10-card-sec10-R23.question_text: Which unpaid local tax and which unresolved court status can prevent license renewal?
sec10-card-sec10-R23.teaching_text: Town excise collectors and state courts share nonrenewal flags directly with the Registry database.

sec10-card-sec10-R24.question_text: Unpaid electronic tolls from which three states, plus which named bridge, can block renewal?
sec10-card-sec10-R24.teaching_text: Reciprocal New England toll enforcement means unpaid interstate gantries and Tobin Bridge bills freeze Massachusetts renewals.

sec10-card-sec10-R25.question_text: What documentation must be recorded before the RMV will renew a blocked license?
sec10-card-sec10-R25.teaching_text: Personal receipts are not enough until official releases confirm paid taxes, cleared fines, or satisfied warrants.

sec10-card-sec10-R26.question_text: Which exact court document is required to clear an outstanding warrant for the RMV?
sec10-card-sec10-R26.teaching_text: Showing up at the Registry with payment receipts or letters fails without the official court recall notice.

sec10-card-sec10-R27.question_text: Can you renew a Massachusetts driver's license while it is currently suspended or revoked?
sec10-card-sec10-R27.teaching_text: Expiration dates do not reset active sanctions, so full reinstatement must happen before any renewal.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: Who gets priority before you turn onto or across a designated throughway?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Vehicles already cruising along a marked throughway expect uninterrupted right of way past cross streets.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: From a one-lane or two-lane street, which larger intersecting roadways require you to yield?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Pulling out from a small side road onto a multi-lane or divided artery invites high-speed broadside crashes.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.question_text: How is a Massachusetts rotary structured, and what traffic control usually governs its entrances?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.teaching_text: Multiple roads feed into one circular loop around an island where incoming drivers normally face yield signs.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: In which rotational direction does traffic circulate around a Massachusetts rotary?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: Keeping the central island on your left ensures every entering driver moves counterclockwise with traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: Unless signs or an officer direct otherwise, to whom must you yield when entering a rotary?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: Darting ahead of cars already circling the island or walkers in entry crosswalks causes classic rotary collisions.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: How should you signal at rotary intersections, especially when exiting the circle?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Flashing your right signal before peeling off tells waiting drivers whether you are exiting or staying inside.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: Which approach lane and destination lane do you use at a single-lane rotary?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: Staying in the right lane entering and exiting keeps single-lane rotary traffic smooth and predictable.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: What guides your lane selection when approaching a multilane rotary that has signs?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: Custom overhead or roadside lane arrows override general rotary defaults whenever engineers post them.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: Without lane-choice signs at a multilane rotary, which lane handles a quarter-turn or straight-through path?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Taking the first exit or going straight never needs inner lanes that force tricky last-second lane cuts.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: Without signs, what lanes handle a three-quarter or U-turn in a rotary, and what is the single-lane exception?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: Multi-lane approaches use left and inner lanes before exiting right, while single-lane approaches stay right throughout.
sec13-card-sec13-F10.must_match_memory_hook: Left to inner, single stays right

visual_sync.text_span: Left to inner, single stays right

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: Why must you wait until it is completely safe before changing lanes inside a rotary?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: Curving geometry creates blind angles where circulating cars can sit alongside either side of your vehicle.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.question_text: What should you do instead of stopping if you miss your intended exit inside a rotary?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.teaching_text: Slamming on the brakes or cutting sharply across outer lanes triggers instant rear-end or sideswipe crashes.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.question_text: How do roundabouts compare in size to rotaries, and what speed limit applies inside them?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.teaching_text: Tighter roundabout geometry cuts tire grip fast if you enter at open-road rotary speeds.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.question_text: How should you choose lanes and enter when approaching a roundabout?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.teaching_text: Approach arrows plus the same yield-and-lane logic used at rotaries guide every roundabout entry.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.question_text: Does another driver waving you through transfer oncoming traffic's right of way for your turn?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.teaching_text: Trusting a polite hand wave gets drivers T-boned by unseen cars rushing up an adjacent lane.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.question_text: On which side do you normally drive and pass, and when is right-side passing allowed?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.teaching_text: Drivers scan their left mirror expecting passes there, making right-side passes legal only under narrow conditions.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.question_text: When may you pass a person, cyclist, or vehicle, and may you exceed the speed limit to finish?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.teaching_text: Pushing past the posted limit to overtake faster is a classic exam trap that stays illegal.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.question_text: Which three roadside areas must never be used to pass another vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.teaching_text: Shoulders, breakdown lanes, and sidewalks hold stalled cars, debris, and pedestrians rather than passing traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.question_text: Which lanes should you use to pass on a roadway with multiple lanes moving your way?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.teaching_text: Keeping faster passing moves toward the middle and left lanes leaves the right lane calm for merges.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.question_text: What passing maneuver does a broken yellow center line permit when safe?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.teaching_text: Dashed yellow paint marks sightline zones where briefly borrowing the oncoming lane to pass is allowed.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.question_text: What checks and minimum forward clear view do you need before crossing a broken yellow line to pass?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.teaching_text: Closing speeds on two-lane roads eat space fast, demanding mirrors, head checks, and four hundred clear feet.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.question_text: Which turn signals do you use when starting a pass and when returning to your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.teaching_text: Signaling both lane shifts warns trailing and overtaken drivers before you move laterally.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.question_text: What visual check in your mirror tells you when it is safe to pull back right after passing?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.teaching_text: Cutting back before both headlights appear in your rearview mirror clips the front bumper you just passed.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.question_text: Before an oncoming car gets within how many feet must you finish returning to the right lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.teaching_text: Two hundred feet vanishes in roughly a second at highway speeds, leaving zero margin for late returns.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.question_text: What roadway width and clearance condition must exist before passing on the right is ever legal?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.teaching_text: Squeezing past on a narrow single lane forces wheels onto gravel shoulders or curbs.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.question_text: When the roadway is wide and clear enough, in what three situations may you pass on the right?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.teaching_text: Outside left-turning cars or multi-lane one-direction streets, overtaking on the right surprises drivers.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.question_text: How must you adjust your speed and lane position when another driver is passing you?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.teaching_text: Speeding up to trap a passing car in the oncoming lane risks a deadly head-on collision.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.question_text: How must you adjust your approach toward a stopped emergency vehicle showing flashing lights?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.teaching_text: First responders walk inches from live traffic, so scrubbing speed protects crews working at the roadside.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.question_text: What lane action does Move Over require on a four-or-more-lane highway with at least two lanes your way?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.teaching_text: Opening an empty buffer lane shields police, tow operators, and highway crews from mirror strikes.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.question_text: What must you do near a stopped flashing responder if traffic prevents changing lanes?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.teaching_text: Never force an unsafe lane cut into adjacent cars when slowing way down keeps everyone safe.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.question_text: What hidden hazards can a stopped or turning vehicle block from your view?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.teaching_text: Whip around a stopped car blindly and you can hit a crossing pedestrian, pet, or turning car.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.question_text: Which six risky driving actions does the manual identify as aggressive-driving behaviors?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.teaching_text: Recognizing erratic lane cuts, tailgating, and pass-blocking early lets you create space before tempers escalate.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.question_text: What four calm steps should you take if confronted by an aggressive driver?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.teaching_text: Refusing eye contact, ignoring gestures, staying buckled, and clearing out starves road rage of fuel.
sec13-card-sec13-F33.must_match_memory_hook: Yield space, avoid eyes, stay belted

visual_sync.text_span: Yield space, avoid eyes, stay belted

sec13-card-sec13-F34.question_text: What can the RMV do before court after an aggressive-driving arrest that threatens public safety?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.teaching_text: Public-safety threats allow immediate RMV suspension of both your license and plates ahead of trial.

sec13-card-sec13-F35.question_text: What two warning devices on a school bus alert drivers that children are boarding or leaving?
sec13-card-sec13-F35.teaching_text: Red flashers paired with the swing-out driver-side stop sign turn the road into a protected crossing.

sec13-card-sec13-F36.question_text: How do smaller school-pupil transport vans or sedans warn traffic while loading or unloading students?
sec13-card-sec13-F36.teaching_text: Small student-transport vans carry the exact same stop duty when roof signs and red lights activate.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: From which approach directions must you stop for a school bus with flashing lights and stop arm out?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: Students cross in front of and across oncoming lanes, so undivided traffic from every direction halts.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: Until what bus signal change must you remain stopped for a school bus?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: Rolling forward while red lights still flash risks striking a late-running child near the bumper.
sec13-card-sec13-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Hold until lights stop, sign folds

visual_sync.text_span: Hold until lights stop, sign folds

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: What fine and license action can hit a driver on a first school-bus stopping violation?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: Even a first-time pass of a stopped school bus risks losing your license plus two hundred fifty dollars.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: How should you resume driving once school-bus warning signals turn off?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: Kids sometimes drop papers or dart back toward the curb right after the bus starts rolling.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: Under what highway setup is oncoming traffic exempt from stopping for a school bus across the road?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: Painted center lines never excuse stopping, because only a physical barrier separating directions lifts that duty.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.question_text: What does the manual say you are doing if you follow a truck too closely to see its side mirrors?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.teaching_text: When you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you behind the trailer either.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.question_text: How much stopping distance may a large truck need compared with a car or motorcycle?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.teaching_text: Loaded trailers carry massive momentum, especially on rain or ice where stopping room stretches to double.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.question_text: Why must you avoid lingering right beside a large truck or cutting in front to brake?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.teaching_text: Stealing a semi's front safety cushion leaves the driver nowhere to stop tens of thousands of pounds.
sec13-card-sec13-R08.must_match_memory_hook: Never crowd or cut off trucks

visual_sync.text_span: Never crowd or cut off trucks

sec13-card-sec13-R09.question_text: Which lanes do trucks and buses use on a multilane highway for cruising and passing?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.teaching_text: Expect heavy rigs in the two rightmost lanes, cruising far right and overtaking one lane left.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.question_text: How should you drive in the second highway lane to avoid bottlenecking trucks and buses?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.teaching_text: Dawdling below traffic pace in lane two boxes heavy trucks behind slower merges on the right.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.question_text: How does passing a tractor-trailer or bus differ in time and on hills from passing a car?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.teaching_text: Factor extra passing room for sixty-foot trailers that lose speed climbing grades and gain momentum downhill.
sec13-card-sec13-R11.must_match_memory_hook: Longer pass, slower up, faster down

visual_sync.text_span: Longer pass, slower up, faster down

sec13-card-sec13-R12.question_text: Unless strictly necessary, why should you stay off the right side of a truck or bus?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.teaching_text: Long trailers track inward during turns, pinching cars tucked along their right-side blind zone.

sec13-card-sec13-R13.question_text: Why might a truck or bus swing left first, and what should you do behind it?
sec13-card-sec13-R13.teaching_text: Mistaking a left setup swing for a left turn tempts drivers into the right lane mid-turn.

sec13-card-sec13-R14.question_text: On an undivided road with a large rig oncoming, where should you steer and why?
sec13-card-sec13-R14.teaching_text: Air blasts pushed off an oncoming semi can shove a drifting car toward the centerline.

sec13-card-sec13-R15.question_text: Before turning across the path of oncoming trucks or buses, why is careful gap judgment essential?
sec13-card-sec13-R15.teaching_text: Large profiles can look slower than they are, and cutting across leaves a truck unable to scrub speed.

sec13-card-sec13-R16.question_text: How should you respond when a transit bus signals to pull out from its stop?
sec13-card-sec13-R16.teaching_text: Yielding to signaling buses and scanning for rushing riders prevents curb-lane collisions around transit stops.

sec13-card-sec13-R17.question_text: How much clearance must you keep from a trolley's passenger step while riders board or exit?
sec13-card-sec13-R17.teaching_text: Street-level trolley riders step directly onto pavement, making that eight-foot buffer essential for safety.

sec13-card-sec13-R18.question_text: What precautions apply before crossing trolley tracks or turning near an approaching trolley?
sec13-card-sec13-R18.teaching_text: Steel wheels on steel rails need long stopping distances, so turning across an approaching trolley invites impact.

sec13-card-sec13-R19.question_text: Why must you maintain extra space around a trolley sharing a street with motor traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-R19.teaching_text: Unlike a bus or car, a rail-bound trolley has zero ability to steer around your mistake.

sec13-card-sec13-R20.question_text: How should you respond when you spot an orange rear warning sign on a slow-moving vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-R20.teaching_text: Farm tractors and maintenance rigs crawl far below road speed, closing your following gap in seconds.

sec13-card-sec13-R21.question_text: What minimum vehicle count, timing, and purpose define a legal Massachusetts funeral procession?
sec13-card-sec13-R21.teaching_text: Single cars or nighttime drives do not qualify for special funeral-procession intersection rights.

sec13-card-sec13-R22.question_text: Although funeral processions hold intersection priority, to what two authorities must they still yield?
sec13-card-sec13-R22.teaching_text: Active emergency sirens or lights and officer hand signals always outrank funeral procession right of way.

sec13-card-sec13-R23.question_text: Once the funeral lead vehicle lawfully enters an intersection, what may trailing procession cars do?
sec13-card-sec13-R23.teaching_text: Keeping the cortege together lets trailing cars follow the lawful leader past changed signals or stop signs.

sec13-card-sec13-R24.question_text: How closely may drivers inside a funeral procession follow the car ahead?
sec13-card-sec13-R24.teaching_text: Tight spacing signals a continuous procession to cross traffic while still preserving safe braking margin.

sec13-card-sec13-R25.question_text: What safety checks still apply to trailing funeral vehicles following their leader through an intersection?
sec13-card-sec13-R25.teaching_text: Intersection priority inside a procession never excuses striking a crossing pedestrian or unaware cross-street motorist.

sec13-card-sec13-R26.question_text: What maximum speed applies to a funeral procession on a highway posted at fifty-five or higher?
sec13-card-sec13-R26.teaching_text: Even on sixty-five-mile-per-hour expressways, funeral processions top out at fifty-five to stay grouped safely.

sec13-card-sec13-R27.question_text: On public roads below that highway tier, how slow may a funeral procession travel relative to the limit?
sec13-card-sec13-R27.teaching_text: Keeping within five miles per hour of local limits prevents extreme speed backups on surface streets.

sec13-card-sec13-R28.question_text: Which lights must every funeral procession car run, and which cars add hazard flashers?
sec13-card-sec13-R28.teaching_text: Headlights and taillights mark every car in line while hazards bookend the first and final vehicles.

sec13-card-sec13-R29.question_text: When may an outside driver cut between vehicles in a funeral procession?
sec13-card-sec13-R29.teaching_text: Everyday commuters must wait out the line unless waved in by police or running emergency siren and lights.

sec13-card-sec13-R30.question_text: May an uninvolved driver tag onto a funeral procession to share its priority?
sec13-card-sec13-R30.teaching_text: Slipping into the back of a funeral line to run red lights breaks Massachusetts traffic law.

sec13-card-sec13-R31.question_text: Under what single lane condition may you pass a funeral procession on its right on a multilane highway?
sec13-card-sec13-R31.teaching_text: Right-side highway passes stay banned around processions unless the entire cortege travels in the far-left lane.

sec13-card-sec13-R32.question_text: Does a green traffic light let you drive across a funeral procession moving through its red?
sec13-card-sec13-R32.teaching_text: Even on a fresh green light, you may move only if your turn or lane avoids crossing the cortege.

sec13-card-sec13-R33.question_text: What flashing light color may an eligible funeral-home vehicle display during a procession?
sec13-card-sec13-R33.teaching_text: Purple distinguishes authorized funeral-home escorts without mimicking red or blue emergency beacons.

sec13-card-sec13-R34.question_text: What four precautions apply when driving near roadwork zones?
sec13-card-sec13-R34.teaching_text: Shifted lanes, flaggers on foot, and sudden stops leave zero room for distraction inside orange cone zones.
sec13-card-sec13-R34.must_match_memory_hook: Follow orange, watch workers, prepare stop

visual_sync.text_span: Follow orange, watch workers, prepare stop

sec13-card-sec13-R35.question_text: What happens to the speeding fine when a violation occurs inside a work area?
sec13-card-sec13-R35.teaching_text: Massachusetts doubles speeding penalties in construction zones to protect crews working feet from traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-R36.question_text: Who gets the right of way when an animal is being led, ridden, or driven on the road?
sec13-card-sec13-R36.teaching_text: Startled horses can bolt into traffic, so yielding and easing off the gas keeps riders and drivers safe.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.question_text: What three everyday cabin habits must never distract your full attention from driving?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.teaching_text: Even quick bites, lively passenger chats, or tuning stations steal critical reaction time at road speed.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.question_text: Why should you scan well ahead and practice defensive driving?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.teaching_text: Spotting brake lights or road debris early lets you steer or slow smoothly instead of panic-braking.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.question_text: Which three driving environments should you practice, and which emergencies should you study?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.teaching_text: Building comfort in rain, darkness, highway merges, skids, and blowouts prevents freezing during a real crisis.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.question_text: Which warning signals on an emergency vehicle require you to yield the right of way?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.teaching_text: Waiting to hear a siren when lights are already flashing breaks the law because either signal alone counts.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.question_text: Where and how must you stop when an emergency vehicle approaches from any direction?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.teaching_text: Rolling slowly down the center blocks ambulances, so clear all the way right and hold a full stop.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.question_text: How should you use mirrors, signals, and brakes when pulling over for a responding emergency vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.teaching_text: Swerving left or slamming your brakes right in front of an ambulance causes secondary crashes.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.question_text: What must you do if an emergency vehicle approaches while you are already inside an intersection?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.teaching_text: Freezing mid-intersection corks every cross lane and traps the fire truck or ambulance behind you.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.question_text: What must you check and signal after a responding emergency vehicle passes you?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.teaching_text: Police cruisers and second ambulances frequently trail the first siren, catching hasty mergers off guard.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.question_text: Within how many feet is it illegal to follow a responding emergency vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.teaching_text: Fire trucks and ambulances brake or turn without warning, making closer than three hundred feet illegal.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.question_text: Which six types of stopped flashing roadside vehicles trigger your duty to slow and stay alert?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.teaching_text: Move-over caution covers highway maintenance, disaster-support, and tow crews alongside police, fire, and ambulances.
sec15-card-sec15-F10.must_match_memory_hook: Fire, police, EMS, disaster, road, tow

visual_sync.text_span: Fire, police, EMS, disaster, road, tow

sec15-card-sec15-F11.question_text: What speed standard does the Move Over rule set near a stopped flashing emergency vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.teaching_text: Wet pavement, darkness, or tight shoulders demand scrubbing well below posted limits near stopped flashers.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.question_text: When does Massachusetts require changing into a non-adjacent lane past a stopped emergency vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.teaching_text: Whenever at least two lanes run in your direction on a four-lane highway, open a full buffer lane.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.question_text: Which direction may a safe Move Over lane change go, and what applies if boxed in?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.teaching_text: Responders sometimes park in median lanes, meaning a safe buffer shift can move either left or right.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.question_text: What brake readiness and headlight adjustment apply when passing an emergency scene at night?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.teaching_text: High beams blind officers and paramedics working on foot, so click down to low beams early.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.question_text: Where relative to a parked police cruiser should you pull over when requesting assistance?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.teaching_text: Pulling up in front keeps you inside the officer's windshield view rather than approaching unexpectedly from behind.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.question_text: What should you do instead of walking up to an officer already handling another traffic stop?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.teaching_text: Walking up behind an active traffic stop divides an officer's safety focus, so wait by your car.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.question_text: Within how many feet of an active fire is driving past or parking prohibited?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.teaching_text: Keep eight hundred feet for fire scenes distinct from three hundred feet for following responding rigs.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.question_text: When is driving over an unprotected fire hose across the street ever permitted?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.teaching_text: Crushing a pressurized supply line cuts water to crews inside a burning building unless directed across.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.question_text: Must you pull over and stop when signaled by a police officer standing on foot?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.teaching_text: Hand or whistle signals from an officer on foot carry the exact same legal weight as cruiser lights.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.question_text: How must a driver treat any police signal to pull over?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.teaching_text: Looking straight ahead and pretending not to notice flashing blue lights turns a minor stop into fleeing.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.question_text: Which side of the road and what signal-and-mirror steps apply during a routine police stop?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.teaching_text: Pulling onto a narrow left median traps the officer beside fast passing lane traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.question_text: What should you do if the signaling police officer drives right past without stopping behind you?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.teaching_text: Often the cruiser was responding to an emergency ahead, so check mirrors and reenter safely.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.question_text: Which three spots should you avoid stopping in during a police pull-over, and whose spot choice controls?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.teaching_text: Clearing intersections, active lanes, and driveways—or rolling to where the officer points—protects everyone.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.question_text: How should you set your transmission, brake, engine, and radio once stopped by police?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.teaching_text: Securing gear, killing the engine, and muting music prevents accidental lurching and lets instructions carry clearly.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.question_text: What should the driver and passengers do inside the car when pulled over by police?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.teaching_text: Popping your door open uninvited alarms approaching officers and puts you inches from passing traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.question_text: If an officer directs you to step out during a stop, how should you position yourself and your hands?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.teaching_text: Standing clear of live lanes with empty visible hands keeps roadside communication calm and safe.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.question_text: Which two vehicle lights should be on during a nighttime police traffic stop?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.teaching_text: Headlights mark your car on dark shoulders while the cabin dome light shows calm visible hands.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.question_text: What window action should you take as the officer walks up to your car?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.teaching_text: Lowering your glass early lets you speak clearly without muffled shouting through closed windows.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.question_text: How is officer identification handled if the officer stopping you is not wearing a uniform?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.teaching_text: Unmarked plainclothes officers display official badges and ID, and you always have the right to ask.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.question_text: When should you reach for your license and registration, and how should you hand them over?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.teaching_text: Rummaging in gloveboxes before the officer arrives looks suspicious, and loose cards prevent fumbling.

sec15-card-sec15-R12.question_text: What first-offense fine applies if you fail to produce your license or registration when stopped?
sec15-card-sec15-R12.teaching_text: Leaving your wallet or registration slip on the kitchen counter costs thirty-five dollars on a first stop.

sec15-card-sec15-R13.question_text: If you lack your license or registration, whose names and addresses may the officer ask for?
sec15-card-sec15-R13.teaching_text: Borrowing a parent's or friend's car means knowing the registered owner's full name and address too.

sec15-card-sec15-R14.question_text: What fine and criminal consequences hit drivers who refuse identity details or give fake names or addresses?
sec15-card-sec15-R14.teaching_text: Giving a fake name escalates a thirty-five-dollar paperwork slip into arrest, criminal court, and hundred-dollar fines.

sec15-card-sec15-R15.question_text: How does Massachusetts handle proof of auto insurance compared with other states?
sec15-card-sec15-R15.teaching_text: Massachusetts prints your insurer directly on the registration certificate instead of issuing separate insurance cards.

sec15-card-sec15-R16.question_text: Whose hands should remain plainly visible during a traffic stop?
sec15-card-sec15-R16.teaching_text: Resting steering-wheel hands and visible passenger hands reassure the officer that everyone inside is cooperative.

sec15-card-sec15-R17.question_text: How should you handle your cell phone and focus during a police stop?
sec15-card-sec15-R17.teaching_text: Scrolling or calling mid-stop distracts from officer instructions and slows down getting back on your way.

sec15-card-sec15-R18.question_text: What physical movements should both the driver and passengers avoid during a traffic stop?
sec15-card-sec15-R18.teaching_text: Ducking under seats or lunging toward consoles mimics reaching for a weapon in low roadside visibility.

sec15-card-sec15-R19.question_text: Where must you stay while the officer walks back to the police cruiser?
sec15-card-sec15-R19.teaching_text: Stepping out to explain something while the officer checks records in the cruiser creates an immediate hazard.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.question_text: When may you ask the officer a question, and how should you hold a located document while waiting?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.teaching_text: Calling out or opening your door risks misunderstanding, whereas holding a found card out the window stays clear.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.question_text: How must you respond if an officer asks during a stop whether weapons are inside the vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.teaching_text: Clear, truthful answers keep roadside interactions calm and prevent sudden safety escalations.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.question_text: Can an officer withdraw an issued citation roadside, and where do you contest it instead?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.teaching_text: Arguing on the shoulder never erases a written ticket because only a court hearing can overturn it.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.question_text: Does Massachusetts require signing a traffic citation, and what does signing mean in states that require it?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.teaching_text: Massachusetts skips ticket signatures, and out-of-state signatures merely confirm receipt rather than pleading guilty.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.question_text: How should you reenter traffic—especially from a highway breakdown lane—once the officer clears you to leave?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.teaching_text: Building safe speed along the breakdown lane before merging keeps fast highway cars from rear-ending you.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.question_text: Where may a driver report a traffic stop they believe involved bias or improper conduct?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.teaching_text: Filing through the officer's department or agency creates a formal review record safely after the stop ends.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.question_text: What pedal and gear actions should you take first when your vehicle starts skidding?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.teaching_text: Cutting drive torque smoothly lets slipping tires regain rolling grip without sudden weight transfer.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.question_text: Why must you stay off the brakes while your car is actively skidding?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.teaching_text: Stomping the brake locks sliding wheels deeper and turns a recoverable slide into a spin.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.question_text: Which direction do you steer when your rear tires slide left or slide right?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.teaching_text: Turning left into a leftward tail slide aligns your front wheels with your car's travel path.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.question_text: What steering follow-up may be required as a skidding vehicle starts straightening out?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.teaching_text: Tires often rebound the opposite way as grip returns, requiring calm back-and-forth steering inputs.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.question_text: What are your first two actions if your tires drop off the pavement onto the shoulder?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.teaching_text: Jerking back immediately catches the asphalt lip and slingshots your car across oncoming lanes.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.question_text: After stabilizing on the shoulder, what three steps bring you safely back onto the road?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.teaching_text: Shedding speed gently and checking trailing traffic lets your tires climb the pavement edge without snapping.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.question_text: How should you handle the wheel and gas pedal during a flat tire, blowout, or lost wheel?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.teaching_text: Hard braking on a blown tire yanks steering toward the damaged corner and triggers rollovers.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.question_text: Once under control after a tire or wheel failure, when should you leave the roadway?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.teaching_text: Limping far down live lanes shreds rims and hazards faster drivers coming up behind you.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.question_text: If pressing failed antilock brakes all the way down fails to slow you, what gear step comes next?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.teaching_text: Stepping down gear by gear harnesses engine compression to scrub speed without locking the wheels.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.question_text: How should you use the parking brake and its release during total service-brake failure?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.teaching_text: Keeping your thumb on the release lets you ease cable pressure instantly if rear wheels lock.

sec16-card-sec16-F17.question_text: Which two vehicle alerts should you activate if brake failure prevents you from slowing?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.teaching_text: Loud horn blasts plus flashing lights clear intersections and alert pedestrians to get back.

sec16-card-sec16-F18.question_text: How does emergency brake-pedal technique differ between non-antilock brakes and antilock brakes?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.teaching_text: Rapid pumping can rebuild hydraulic pressure in conventional brakes, whereas antilock computers pulse automatically.

sec16-card-sec16-F19.question_text: What two places tell you whether a car has antilock or conventional brakes?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.teaching_text: Knowing your brake system before driving ensures you use the right emergency footwork instinctively.

sec16-card-sec16-F20.question_text: What four actions handle a stuck accelerator while keeping your car under control?
sec16-card-sec16-F20.teaching_text: Shifting to neutral disconnects runaway engine power immediately while keeping power steering and brakes alive.

sec16-card-sec16-F21.question_text: Where should you go once safe after handling a stuck accelerator?
sec16-card-sec16-F21.teaching_text: Never keep driving a car with a binding throttle linkage that can jam wide open again.

sec16-card-sec16-F22.question_text: What three immediate moves dodge a vehicle coming straight at you head-on in your lane?
sec16-card-sec16-F22.teaching_text: Never swerve left into the oncoming lane where a waking driver will instinctively yank back.

sec16-card-sec16-F23.question_text: What backup lights and roadside steps apply if your headlights suddenly go dark?
sec16-card-sec16-F23.teaching_text: Parking lights, hazards, or turn signals keep your outline visible while you promptly exit live lanes.
sec16-card-sec16-F23.must_match_memory_hook: Backup flashers, switch check, pull off

visual_sync.text_span: Backup flashers, switch check, pull off

sec16-card-sec16-F24.question_text: What is the top priority when a train is approaching a vehicle stalled on railroad tracks?
sec16-card-sec16-F24.teaching_text: Forget belongings or restarting attempts because trains need a mile to stop and obliterate stalled cars.

sec16-card-sec16-F25.question_text: At what angle and direction should you run from tracks as a train approaches, and whom do you call?
sec16-card-sec16-F25.teaching_text: Running forty-five degrees toward the oncoming locomotive keeps you behind flying wreckage before calling emergency dispatch.

sec16-card-sec16-F26.question_text: If your car stalls on tracks with zero train approaching, what are your first two steps?
sec16-card-sec16-F26.teaching_text: Cracking a window or door lets you hear distant horns immediately while attempting a quick restart.

sec16-card-sec16-F27.question_text: If no train is coming and a stalled car refuses to restart on tracks, how can you try clearing it?
sec16-card-sec16-F27.teaching_text: Selecting neutral unlocks the drivetrain so occupants can push or coast the car off the rails.

sec16-card-sec16-F28.question_text: What number and details must you call in if a stalled vehicle cannot be moved off railroad tracks?
sec16-card-sec16-F28.teaching_text: Phoning the crossing's Emergency Notification System with its locator ID lets railroad dispatchers halt trains directly.

sec16-card-sec16-F29.question_text: Through what system should you report suspicious railroad activity such as switch tampering?
sec16-card-sec16-F29.teaching_text: The same Emergency Notification System sign connects straight to rail security for track hazards or tampering.

sec16-card-sec16-F30.question_text: Where should you steer during a breakdown, and what two blind road features must you avoid?
sec16-card-sec16-F30.teaching_text: Stopping just over a crest or around a bend gives fast traffic zero sightline to miss you.

sec16-card-sec16-F31.question_text: What must happen to passengers if a disabled vehicle cannot be moved off the pavement?
sec16-card-sec16-F31.teaching_text: Sitting inside a dead car blocking an active lane invites catastrophic rear-end impacts.

sec16-card-sec16-F32.question_text: Once parked far off a highway travel lane on the shoulder, where should occupants stay?
sec16-card-sec16-F32.teaching_text: Standing outside in a highway breakdown lane exposes you directly to drifting cars.

sec16-card-sec16-F33.question_text: Which lights should you turn on once parked safely during a breakdown, including after dark?
sec16-card-sec16-F33.teaching_text: Four-way flashers plus nighttime cabin dome lights make your disabled car unmistakable on dark shoulders.

sec16-card-sec16-F34.question_text: When should you put on an available reflective safety vest during a breakdown?
sec16-card-sec16-F34.teaching_text: Putting your vest on inside the cabin ensures you step out already visible to headlights.

sec16-card-sec16-F35.question_text: What should you evaluate before getting out of a disabled car, and which door side is safer?
sec16-card-sec16-F35.teaching_text: Climbing out the curb or guardrail side keeps your body out of fast passing lanes.

sec16-card-sec16-F36.question_text: Which cloth color tied to an antenna or handle signals a breakdown normally versus in snow?
sec16-card-sec16-F36.teaching_text: White stands out against dark asphalt and trees, whereas red contrasts sharply against blowing white snow.

sec16-card-sec16-F37.question_text: When in the breakdown sequence should you raise your vehicle's hood?
sec16-card-sec16-F37.teaching_text: Confirming it is safe to step outside comes before walking forward to prop the hood.

sec16-card-sec16-F38.question_text: At what two distances behind a disabled car do warning triangles or LED flares go on a divided highway?
sec16-card-sec16-F38.teaching_text: Divided highways carry one-way traffic only, placing both markers behind you at ten and one hundred feet.

sec16-card-sec16-F39.question_text: Where do three warning triangles or flares go on a two-way two-lane or undivided highway?
sec16-card-sec16-F39.teaching_text: Two-way roads add a third marker one hundred feet ahead to warn oncoming passers.

sec16-card-sec16-F40.question_text: What four actions must you take immediately if smoke starts coming from under your hood?
sec16-card-sec16-F40.teaching_text: Killing fuel and spark, getting everyone well back, and calling firefighters prevents hood-flash burns.
sec16-card-sec16-F40.must_match_memory_hook: Exit road, ignition off, evacuate, call

visual_sync.text_span: Exit road, ignition off, evacuate, call

sec16-card-sec16-F41.question_text: When should you never attempt to fight a vehicle fire yourself?
sec16-card-sec16-F41.teaching_text: Popping a burning hood bare-handed feeds oxygen to fuel vapors that can explode outward.

sec16-card-sec16-F42.question_text: What rapid belt-and-window sequence saves you if your vehicle plunges into water?
sec16-card-sec16-F42.teaching_text: Power windows still work briefly before water shorts the wiring, giving you seconds to roll down and climb out.

sec16-card-sec16-F43.question_text: Why must you avoid opening a car door after entering deep water?
sec16-card-sec16-F43.teaching_text: Opening a door lets water rush into the cabin, killing buoyancy and flipping the vehicle.

sec16-card-sec16-F44.question_text: What four steps apply immediately after a crash or breakdown inside a tunnel?
sec16-card-sec16-F44.teaching_text: Tight tunnel walls lack wide shoulders, so hazards and rapid nine-one-one dispatch close lanes overhead.
sec16-card-sec16-F44.must_match_memory_hook: Pull aside, hazards, emergency call, obey

visual_sync.text_span: Pull aside, hazards, emergency call, obey

sec16-card-sec16-R01.question_text: Where should you wait for responders after a non-fire tunnel breakdown when conditions are safe?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.teaching_text: Narrow tunnel walkways put pedestrians inches from echoing traffic unless smoke forces evacuation.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.question_text: What three habits apply every time you drive into a tunnel?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.teaching_text: Eyes need a moment to adjust inside portals, making headlights and overhead lane signals critical.
sec16-card-sec16-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Stay alert, headlights on, obey signs

visual_sync.text_span: Stay alert, headlights on, obey signs

sec16-card-sec16-R03.question_text: What two smoke or fire conditions forbid you from driving into a tunnel?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.teaching_text: Driving a smoking car underground or entering visible portal smoke traps everyone in toxic air.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.question_text: How should you manage following distance inside a tunnel during slow traffic?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.teaching_text: Bumper-to-bumper packing inside a tunnel leaves zero room to steer around a stalled car.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.question_text: What cargo category—including propane—is barred from the described Massachusetts tunnels?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.teaching_text: Pressurized gas cylinders and hazardous loads turn enclosed underwater or urban tunnels into blast hazards.

sec16-card-sec16-R06.question_text: What three awareness cues help you stay ready while driving through tunnel traffic?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.teaching_text: Clocking emergency exit doors as you pass saves precious seconds if smoke fills the bore.
sec16-card-sec16-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Radio updates, spot exits, obey signs

visual_sync.text_span: Radio updates, spot exits, obey signs

sec16-card-sec16-R07.question_text: During a tunnel fire, how must you leave your engine, keys, and personal belongings?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.teaching_text: Firefighters need keys inside to move abandoned cars while you evacuate without heavy bags.

sec16-card-sec16-R08.question_text: What three steps apply during a tunnel fire as you evacuate?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.teaching_text: Alerting dispatchers, following illuminated exit guidance, and helping nearby motorists gets everyone to fresh air.

sec16-card-sec16-R09.question_text: Must a driver stop after a minor crash, or only after major collisions?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.teaching_text: Driving off after even a tiny bumper tap turns an insurance claim into criminal hit-and-run.

sec16-card-sec16-R10.question_text: When nobody is hurt in a crash, what does the Driver Removal Law require if cars still drive?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.teaching_text: Leaving drivable fender-bender cars parked in live highway lanes triggers far worse secondary pileups.

sec16-card-sec16-R11.question_text: Which five pieces of information must drivers exchange after a crash, plus what must be shown on request?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.teaching_text: Capturing all five details and displaying your physical license and registration prevents disputed claims later.
sec16-card-sec16-R11.must_match_memory_hook: Swap name, address, license, reg, insurer

visual_sync.text_span: Swap name, address, license, reg, insurer

sec16-card-sec16-R12.question_text: What must you do if you strike and damage unattended property such as a parked car?
sec16-card-sec16-R12.teaching_text: Driving off quietly from a scraped bumper or mailbox counts as leaving a property-damage scene.

sec16-card-sec16-R13.question_text: What property-damage dollar amount triggers a mandatory five-day crash report to police and the RMV?
sec16-card-sec16-R13.teaching_text: Modern bumper sensors top a thousand dollars fast, starting that strict five-day filing clock.

sec16-card-sec16-R14.question_text: Whom must you notify after striking and injuring an animal on the road?
sec16-card-sec16-R14.teaching_text: Promptly calling police and the owner gets veterinary help moving and satisfies state reporting law.

sec16-card-sec16-R15.question_text: What three immediate steps follow a crash that involves possible injuries?
sec16-card-sec16-R15.teaching_text: Summoning police and paramedics right away gets trauma care rolling before shock sets in.

sec16-card-sec16-R16.question_text: Which three crash outcomes require filing written reports with the RMV and local police within five days?
sec16-card-sec16-R16.teaching_text: Any hurt person, fatality, or damage reaching one thousand dollars locks in five-day dual reporting.

sec16-card-sec16-R17.question_text: Besides police and the RMV, whom must you notify after an injury crash?
sec16-card-sec16-R17.teaching_text: Delaying notice to your carrier complicates medical coverage and liability defense after an injury crash.

sec16-card-sec16-R21.question_text: What four duties bind a driver after any crash involving death, injury, or property damage?
sec16-card-sec16-R21.teaching_text: Remaining on scene, giving your identity, helping safely, and calling emergency crews separates lawful conduct from crime.

sec16-card-sec16-R22.question_text: What maximum fine and prison exposure apply to leaving a property-damage crash without identifying yourself?
sec16-card-sec16-R22.teaching_text: Fleeing even a non-injury fender-bender risks up to two years behind bars plus two hundred dollars.

sec16-card-sec16-R23.question_text: What maximum fine and prison term apply to leaving a nonfatal injury crash without identifying yourself?
sec16-card-sec16-R23.teaching_text: Compare property versus nonfatal injury carefully, where maximum fine jumps from two hundred to one thousand dollars.

sec16-card-sec16-R24.question_text: What maximum fine, jail time, or state prison sentence applies to fleeing a fatal crash?
sec16-card-sec16-R24.teaching_text: Leaving a fatal collision carries felony exposure up to five thousand dollars and ten years in state prison.

sec16-card-sec16-R25.question_text: What happens if you injure or kill a cat or dog and fail to notify the owner or local police?
sec16-card-sec16-R25.teaching_text: Massachusetts specifically protects cats and dogs with a fine when drivers fail to report hitting them.

sec16-card-sec16-R26.question_text: Beyond fines and jail, what three financial or licensing costs can follow a criminal driving conviction?
sec16-card-sec16-R26.teaching_text: Up to six years of hiked insurance surcharges plus probation fees cost far more than the ticket.

sec16-card-sec16-R18.question_text: When may you move an injured crash victim, and what body parts must be supported if forced to?
sec16-card-sec16-R18.teaching_text: Shifting a hurt person unnecessarily can sever spinal nerves unless fire or oncoming danger forces evacuation.

sec16-card-sec16-R19.question_text: What first-aid technique does the manual advise for an open bleeding wound until paramedics arrive?
sec16-card-sec16-R19.teaching_text: Continuous firm pressure directly over the wound slows blood loss until trained medics take over.

sec16-card-sec16-R20.question_text: How can a coat or blanket help an injured person at a crash scene?
sec16-card-sec16-R20.teaching_text: Trauma victims lose body heat rapidly even in mild weather, accelerating dangerous circulatory shock.

sec16-card-sec16-R27.question_text: How should you drive past a crash scene when emergency responders are already on site?
sec16-card-sec16-R27.teaching_text: Rubbernecking slows emergency ambulances and triggers rear-end chain collisions in passing lanes.

sec16-card-sec16-R28.question_text: What four actions should a witness take when arriving at a crash before responders get there?
sec16-card-sec16-R28.teaching_text: Parking clear with flashers on keeps your car from becoming part of the wreck while summoning police.

sec16-card-sec16-R29.question_text: At least how far ahead of and behind a crash scene should available flares or triangles sit?
sec16-card-sec16-R29.teaching_text: Notice crash scenes call for at least two hundred feet each way, double the breakdown hundred-foot mark.

sec16-card-sec16-R30.question_text: What two vehicle precautions should a witness take with crashed cars when safe and possible?
sec16-card-sec16-R30.teaching_text: Turning off ignitions cuts electrical sparks near leaking fuel while clearing lanes prevents secondary hits.

sec16-card-sec16-R31.question_text: What must you do—and tell trapped occupants—when downed electrical wires touch a crashed vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-R31.teaching_text: Touching the car bridges lethal voltage to ground, whereas rubber-tired cabins shield riders until utility crews cut power.

sec16-card-sec16-R32.question_text: What penalties can follow failing to file a mandatory Massachusetts crash report?
sec16-card-sec16-R32.teaching_text: Blowing past the five-day crash-report deadline puts both your wallet and your license on the line.

sec16-card-sec16-R33.question_text: Does reporting a crash only to your insurance company fulfill your legal crash-reporting duties?
sec16-card-sec16-R33.teaching_text: Many drivers assume their agent files state paperwork, then get blindsided by RMV non-reporting notices.

sec16-card-sec16-R34.question_text: From which three sources can you obtain a blank Massachusetts Motor Vehicle Crash Operator Report?
sec16-card-sec16-R34.teaching_text: Downloading from the RMV website is fastest when the five-day filing clock is ticking.

sec16-card-sec16-R35.question_text: To which three recipients must you send completed copies of a required crash report?
sec16-card-sec16-R35.teaching_text: Leaving out any one of the three—local police, your insurer, or the RMV—leaves your filing incomplete.

sec16-card-sec16-R36.question_text: What should you keep for yourself after mailing out your required crash-report copies?
sec16-card-sec16-R36.teaching_text: Saving a personal copy proves what you filed if mail delays or claim questions surface months later.

sec16-card-sec16-R37.question_text: How can you request a copy of a law-enforcement crash report, and what is the fee?
sec16-card-sec16-R37.teaching_text: Keep twenty dollars for police crash reports distinct from thirty-dollar permit fees and fifty-dollar appeals.

sec16-card-sec16-R38.question_text: What travel alternatives reduce solo driving, and how should you group errands when driving?
sec16-card-sec16-R38.teaching_text: Combining stops into one trip and using transit, walking, biking, or carpools cuts fuel burn.

sec16-card-sec16-R39.question_text: Which stop should you visit first when combining multiple errands into one trip, and why?
sec16-card-sec16-R39.teaching_text: Driving the longest leg first brings the cold engine up to efficient operating temperature for every short stop afterward.

sec16-card-sec16-R40.question_text: Which three smooth driving habits cut down wasteful jackrabbit starts and hard stops?
sec16-card-sec16-R40.teaching_text: Gentle throttle, steady cruising, and early coasting save both fuel and brake-pad wear.

sec16-card-sec16-R41.question_text: Beyond how many minutes does Massachusetts prohibit idling a parked motor vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-R41.teaching_text: Shutting the engine off during long waits saves fuel and keeps exhaust out of neighborhood air.

sec16-card-sec16-R42.question_text: How does a tight, undamaged fuel cap help efficiency and emissions?
sec16-card-sec16-R42.teaching_text: Loose or cracked gas caps let gasoline vapors escape straight into the air and trigger check-engine lights.

sec16-card-sec16-R43.question_text: What three benefits come from keeping your tires inflated to the proper pressure?
sec16-card-sec16-R43.teaching_text: Underinflated tires flex, overheat, wear unevenly, and drag down your miles per gallon.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: Which three unexpected challenges does defensive driving keep you ready to handle?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Staying mentally ready for jaywalkers, blown tires, and sudden rain prevents panic reactions.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: What two visual and mental habits anchor every defensive drive?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Keeping sightlines unobstructed ahead and around lets sharp focus spot hazards early.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: Why shouldn't you turn your eyes toward a passenger or cabin item even for a split second?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: At highway speed, even a one-second glance inside covers dozens of blind feet.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: Why must you keep open space around your car AND track who is beside and behind you?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: When traffic ahead locks up suddenly, only a pre-checked open flank lets you swerve safely.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: What speed habit and pedal readiness belong on every street?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Matching pace to real traffic and grip lets you slow or stop without skidding.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: How often should you check mirrors, and which four directions need active road-condition watching?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Sweeping mirrors every few seconds keeps your mental map of all four sides fresh.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: Which four street-edge movements — from brake lights to car doors — must urban scanning catch?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Swinging parked-car doors and stepping-out pedestrians appear suddenly along busy New England curbs.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: What should you expect from fellow motorists, and what specific rear light warns of a backing car ahead?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: White backup lamps glowing on a parked car warn you before its bumper swings out.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: Why shouldn't a green traffic signal lull you into assuming a crosswalk is clear?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Distracted walkers or cyclists sometimes step against red signals right into live lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: At which three community spots must you take special care for hidden pedestrians or bicycles?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Parked SUVs and delivery vans near schools, parks, and plazas hide darting children and bikes.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: What sensory assumption should you never make around pedestrians — especially in parking lots and crosswalks?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Quiet modern engines, hybrids, earbuds, and street noise mask approaching cars completely.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: Why should a defensive driver willingly yield right-of-way even when another driver is wrong?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Insisting stubbornly on technical right-of-way never repairs a crumpled fender or prevents injuries.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: How often does the Massachusetts manual recommend getting an eye exam?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Gradual vision changes sneak up unnoticed unless an eye exam catches and corrects them promptly.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: How should a driver with diminished hearing adjust behind the wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: More frequent mirror sweeps catch flashing strobes and merging cars when horns sound faint.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: Which three chemical or medical exposures mean you must stay out of the driver's seat?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Over-the-counter allergy or cold pills that cause drowsiness impair reaction timing like alcohol.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: Why shouldn't you drive when exhausted or emotionally upset?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Heavy eyelids or heated anger tunnel your attention and ruin safe decision-making.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: What simple eyewear habit does the manual advise on bright, sunny days?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Cutting harsh daytime glare prevents squinting fatigue and reveals brake lights faster.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: Along with following the factory maintenance schedule, what quick visual check belongs BEFORE getting into your car?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Spotting a sidewall bulge or flat tire in the driveway beats suffering a highway blowout.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: What should you do if you suspect brake trouble — and what does pulling to one side while braking signal?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Uneven caliper grip or worn linings pull the nose sideways and worsen rapidly if ignored.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: Which three routine tire-care tasks follow vehicle or tire-maker recommendations?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: Proper PSI and timely rotations spread tread wear evenly for balanced wet braking.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: How does Massachusetts law treat driving on badly worn or damaged tires?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Driving on slick or bulging rubber violates state law on top of inviting blowouts.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: What minimum tread depth in inches — and what structural condition — must legal tires maintain?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: Shallow grooves under two thirty-seconds of an inch cannot channel rain out from under rubber.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: When you stick a penny into a tire groove, what visual cue tells you the tire is worn out?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: Seeing all of Abe Lincoln's head means less than two thirty-seconds of rubber remains.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: What two warning flaws should never appear when you turn the steering wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Sloppy free play in the wheel delays emergency swerves when fractions of a second count.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: What fluid should you check regularly, and what turning noise calls for a steering inspection?
