sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Whining or screeching on turns warns of low fluid, slipping belts, or failing pumps.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: Besides checking that headlights, brake lights, and blinkers work, what three winter or road coatings must you clean off them?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: Working bulbs buried behind slush or road salt stay invisible to trailing drivers.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: When must windshield wiper blades be replaced alongside keeping glass and mirrors clean?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Hardened rubber that smears rain turns oncoming night headlights into blinding sheets of glare.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: In what condition must license plates stay, and from how many feet away must numbers read at night?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: Tinted plastic plate covers, mud, or trailer hitches hiding numbers draw equipment tickets.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.question_text: In which exact corner of the license plate must your Massachusetts registration sticker go?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.teaching_text: Sticking renewal decals across the plate face or wrong corners fails plate-display rules.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.question_text: Under good road conditions and moderate traffic, what minimum following interval is Massachusetts's baseline rule?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.teaching_text: Three full seconds on clean dry asphalt gives alert drivers baseline reaction and braking margin.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.question_text: How do you time your three-second gap using a roadside landmark — and what if you reach it early?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.teaching_text: Passing that pole before reaching three proves you are tailgating and need to ease back.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.question_text: Even in good weather, what spacing upgrade does the manual advise whenever open traffic allows?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.teaching_text: Three seconds is a bare floor, not a target — extra seconds make stops effortless.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.question_text: At least how many seconds of following space must you leave behind a motorcycle?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.teaching_text: Light motorcycles stop faster than sedans and spill riders onto the lane if they skid.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.question_text: At least how many seconds of following space belong behind heavy equipment like a tractor or dump truck?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.teaching_text: Watch that big jump — three seconds cars, four motorcycles, ten full seconds behind dump trucks.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.question_text: Why must you never cut sharply in front of heavy equipment or a tractor-trailer?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.teaching_text: Loaded semis physically cannot scrub momentum fast enough if a sedan steals their front buffer.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.question_text: Up to what dollar fine can unlawful tailgating draw in Massachusetts?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.teaching_text: Riding bumpers breaks Massachusetts law and risks up to a one-hundred-dollar ticket.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.question_text: Which two calm moves let an aggressive tailgater get past you safely?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.teaching_text: Putting an impatient driver ahead of your windshield beats brake-checking or getting rear-ended.

sec06-card-sec06-F38.question_text: How must your following interval change whenever weather or pavement turns poor?
sec06-card-sec06-F38.teaching_text: Wet, icy, or broken asphalt multiplies braking distance well past dry-road assumptions.

sec06-card-sec06-F39.question_text: Near which three roadside wildcards should you open extra space cushion?
sec06-card-sec06-F39.teaching_text: Hedged driveways, backing bumpers, and playing kids can put someone in your lane without warning.

sec06-card-sec06-F40.question_text: What two-part delay makes up driver reaction time?
sec06-card-sec06-F40.teaching_text: Your car rolls at full speed through every millisecond it takes eyes and foot to act.

sec06-card-sec06-F41.question_text: What fraction of a second does the Massachusetts manual use as its educational reaction-time example?
sec06-card-sec06-F41.teaching_text: Even an alert three-quarter-second reaction delay eats surprising pavement at fast highway speeds.

sec06-card-sec06-F42.question_text: In the manual's fifty-mile-per-hour example, roughly how many feet roll by during reaction BEFORE braking starts?
sec06-card-sec06-F42.teaching_text: Fifty-five feet — more than three car lengths — vanishes before brake pads even touch rotors.

sec06-card-sec06-F43.question_text: Once braking begins at fifty miles per hour on dry, clear, flat pavement, roughly how many MORE feet does stopping take?
sec06-card-sec06-F43.teaching_text: Adding fifty-five reaction feet to over one hundred sixty deceleration feet reveals total stopping distance.

sec06-card-sec06-F44.question_text: Combining reaction and braking at fifty miles per hour on dry flat pavement, what total stopping distance does the manual illustrate?
sec06-card-sec06-F44.teaching_text: Fifty-five reaction feet plus one hundred sixty braking feet sums cleanly to two hundred fifteen.

sec06-card-sec06-F45.question_text: At sixty miles per hour on a dry flat road, roughly how many total feet does reacting and stopping take?
sec06-card-sec06-F45.teaching_text: Adding just ten miles per hour jumps total stop nearly eighty feet — nearly a football field.

sec06-card-sec06-F46.question_text: At thirty miles per hour, roughly how many total feet does the manual's stopping example cover?
sec06-card-sec06-F46.teaching_text: Even neighborhood thirty-mile-per-hour cruising needs over a hundred feet to react and halt.

sec06-card-sec06-F47.question_text: Are the manual's stopping-distance numbers exact guarantees — and which three real-world variables shift them?
sec06-card-sec06-F47.teaching_text: Worn tires, rain, or steep grades stretch real stopping room well beyond textbook dry numbers.
sec06-card-sec06-F47.must_match_memory_hook: Examples vary by road, weather, car

visual_sync.text_span: Examples vary by road, weather, car

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: Which vehicle traits, road slope, and three surface conditions demand extra stopping time?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Gravity on downgrades and heavy cargo fight your brakes while wet or rough asphalt cuts grip.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: Compared with passenger cars, how much stopping distance can large trucks require?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Never dart into the open gap ahead of an eighteen-wheeler — that space is its two-times brake zone.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: How should you apply the brakes when preparing to turn or stop?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Lighting your red brake lamps early gives drivers behind smooth notice before deceleration builds.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: Why shouldn't you rest your left or right foot lightly on the brake pedal while cruising?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Riding the pedal overheats brake pads and keeps constant false brake lights crying wolf behind you.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: What must you NEVER do to the pedal on a vehicle equipped with antilock brakes?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: ABS computers pulse pressure automatically; pumping the pedal defeats the system and lengthens stops.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: When should you scrub speed for a bend or limited-sightline stretch?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Braking hard mid-curve upsets tire grip, whereas slowing beforehand lets you steer smoothly.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: For what safety purpose does your horn exist — and which two emotional uses are wrong?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Save short horn taps to prevent real collisions, never to scold or rush slow traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: Between what exact clock offsets after sunset and before sunrise must headlights and taillights burn?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Massachusetts buffers dusk and dawn by thirty minutes on each end rather than full dark.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: Even during daytime hours, what sightline distance triggers mandatory headlights and taillights?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Heavy overcast, blowing snow, or mist hiding people five hundred feet out requires full lights.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: What lighting rule triggers whenever your windshield wipers are running — and do daytime running lights count?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: Daytime running lights leave your red taillights dark in rain spray, failing Massachusetts's wiper law.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.question_text: In which three precipitation types — plus what enclosed roadway structure — must headlights and taillights be on?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.teaching_text: Switching full lights on inside Boston tunnels and storms keeps your rear taillights glowing.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.question_text: How can you politely alert another driver at dusk or night that their headlights are off?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.teaching_text: A brief headlight cue alerts dark-hooded drivers who forgot they only had dash glow on.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.question_text: What three lighting, positioning, and personal-safety steps apply right after a vehicle breakdown?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.teaching_text: Getting both the car and people completely off live asphalt prevents secondary breakdown strikes.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.question_text: If a tire goes flat where you cannot clear a live traffic lane, should you jack it up yourself?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.teaching_text: Kneeling beside a jack in live traffic is lethal — keep hazards on and wait for roadside help.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.question_text: How can your four-way emergency flashers help vehicles behind you when you spot a crash or road hazard ahead?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.teaching_text: Tapping four-way hazards alerts fast-closing highway drivers before they crest into stopped traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R16.question_text: Where and when should you learn how your car's lane-keeping or adaptive-cruise systems behave?
sec06-card-sec06-R16.teaching_text: Figuring out unfamiliar assistance chimes at sixty-five miles per hour invites dangerous surprises.

sec06-card-sec06-R17.question_text: What rule sets your maximum safe speed at night even below the posted sign?
sec06-card-sec06-R17.teaching_text: Driving faster than your low beams reach means hitting dark obstacles before you can stop.

sec06-card-sec06-R18.question_text: How should your space cushion change after dark — especially around which vehicles?
sec06-card-sec06-R18.teaching_text: Depth perception drops at night, and long trailers carry wide blind zones.

sec06-card-sec06-R19.question_text: Which two interior adjustments cut glare and preserve your night vision?
sec06-card-sec06-R19.teaching_text: Bright dome or map bulbs reflect off glass and shrink your pupils against dark roads.

sec06-card-sec06-R20.question_text: Where should you aim your eyes instead of staring into bright oncoming headlights?
sec06-card-sec06-R20.teaching_text: Tracking the white fog line at your lower right guides lane position without dazzling retinas.

sec06-card-sec06-R21.question_text: Which two lighting mistakes on YOUR car might an oncoming driver's quick headlight flash be warning about?
sec06-card-sec06-R21.teaching_text: Check your stalk right away — either your headlamps are dark or your high beams are dazzling them.

sec06-card-sec06-R22.question_text: Roughly how many feet ahead do normal high beams illuminate versus normal low beams?
sec06-card-sec06-R22.teaching_text: Notice low beams reach only one hundred feet — shorter than a fifty-mph stop!

sec06-card-sec06-R23.question_text: In what lighting environment should you switch on high-beam headlights?
sec06-card-sec06-R23.teaching_text: Well-lit city avenues don't need brights that blind pedestrians and cross traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R24.question_text: Within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle — and within how many feet behind a vehicle ahead — must you dim high beams?
sec06-card-sec06-R24.teaching_text: High beams reflected in a lead driver's mirrors blind them almost as badly as head-on glare.
sec06-card-sec06-R24.must_match_memory_hook: Five hundred oncoming, two hundred behind

visual_sync.text_span: Five hundred oncoming, two hundred behind

sec06-card-sec06-R25.question_text: If an oncoming driver leaves high beams blazing after a reminder flash, how must you respond?
sec06-card-sec06-R25.teaching_text: Blinding an oncoming driver in revenge puts two sightless cars closing head-on.

sec06-card-sec06-R26.question_text: What provides true protection against drowsy driving — and how does the manual rate coffee or a brief nap?
sec06-card-sec06-R26.teaching_text: Caffeine masks yawns briefly before microsleeps return; only adequate rest truly prevents nod-offs.

sec06-card-sec06-R27.question_text: Which six-hour overnight window should you avoid driving — and what two lane clues warn of nodding off?
sec06-card-sec06-R27.teaching_text: Your body clock dips hardest between midnight and six a.m., when drifting onto rumble strips screams stop.

sec06-card-sec06-R28.question_text: How does alcohol interact with fatigue, and which two kinds of medicine labels require drowsiness checks?
sec06-card-sec06-R28.teaching_text: Both prescription bottles and drugstore over-the-counter boxes carry warning labels for behind-the-wheel drowsiness.

sec06-card-sec06-R29.question_text: Why are roads especially slick right when rain first starts falling?
sec06-card-sec06-R29.teaching_text: Before heavy downpours wash grime away, light rain mixes oil drippings into a greasy film.

sec06-card-sec06-R30.question_text: What happens physically to your tires during hydroplaning, and which three factors govern it?
sec06-card-sec06-R30.teaching_text: Once water wedges beneath tread faster than grooves evacuate it, steering and braking vanish.

sec06-card-sec06-R31.question_text: What exact pedal and wheel response brings your tires safely back onto pavement if hydroplaning starts?
sec06-card-sec06-R31.teaching_text: Slamming brakes or yanking the wheel spins the car the instant front tires regain grip.

sec06-card-sec06-R32.question_text: Which two adjustments keep you from rear-ending stalled traffic in rain or fog?
sec06-card-sec06-R32.teaching_text: Shrinking sightlines and longer wet stops require pacing strictly within visible clear pavement.

sec06-card-sec06-R33.question_text: What winter hazard does the Massachusetts manual compare wet fallen leaves to?
sec06-card-sec06-R33.teaching_text: Crushed wet New England foliage coats October corners with traction loss rivaling black ice.

sec06-card-sec06-R34.question_text: Which headlight setting belongs in fog, and why?
sec06-card-sec06-R34.teaching_text: High beams bounce straight back off water droplets into your eyes as a white wall.

sec06-card-sec06-R35.question_text: Alongside using turn signals in rain, which two glass-clearing systems need to work properly?
sec06-card-sec06-R35.teaching_text: Humid rainy air fogs interior glass fast unless defoggers back up outside wiper blades.

sec06-card-sec06-R36.question_text: When heavy weather hides signposts and forward pavement, how do you stay inside your lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R36.teaching_text: Following painted right-edge lines guides you steadily until you can exit safely.

sec06-card-sec06-R37.question_text: Why should you steer clear of deep puddles — and how do you dry soaked brakes afterward?
sec06-card-sec06-R37.teaching_text: Gentle brake-pedal drag warms wet pads and rotors until normal stopping bite returns.

sec06-card-sec06-R38.question_text: How must speed, throttle input, and following room change on snow or ice?
sec06-card-sec06-R38.teaching_text: Stomping the gas spins tires on ice, and short gaps guarantee sliding into bumpers.

sec06-card-sec06-R39.question_text: What happens if your brakes lock on ice — and which way do you steer if a skid starts?
sec06-card-sec06-R39.teaching_text: Sliding front tires cannot steer at all; turning in the skid's direction realigns rolling grip.

sec06-card-sec06-R40.question_text: How must you behave around working snowplows, and what other fleet needs watching in storms?
sec06-card-sec06-R40.teaching_text: Plows throw heavy snow clouds at slow speeds and have wide wings and blind spots.

sec06-card-sec06-R41.question_text: Why do bridges and highway overpasses ice over before regular ground-supported roads?
sec06-card-sec06-R41.teaching_text: Freezing wind chills elevated bridge decks from both top and bottom while regular asphalt stays bare.

sec06-card-sec06-R42.question_text: When snow starts falling, how should you pull away and safely gauge road grip?
sec06-card-sec06-R42.teaching_text: A gentle early brake check reveals slickness at low speed before approaching a busy intersection.

sec06-card-sec06-R43.question_text: Which two vehicle systems must stay in solid working shape before winter weather arrives?
sec06-card-sec06-R43.teaching_text: Without strong heat on the glass, blowing snow freezes onto wiper blades mid-sweep.

sec06-card-sec06-R44.question_text: Which flat body panels — beyond windows — must you clear completely of snow and ice before driving?
sec06-card-sec06-R44.teaching_text: Frozen roof sheets peel off at highway speed and smash through windshields behind you.

sec06-card-sec06-R45.question_text: What serious Massachusetts charge can hit a driver who fails to clear snow and ice off their vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-R45.teaching_text: Driving an igloo car down the turnpike isn't minor — police can cite negligent operation.

sec06-card-sec06-R46.question_text: How full should you keep your gas tank in winter, and what cold-weather problem does that prevent?
sec06-card-sec06-R46.teaching_text: Keeping the tank at least half full cuts condensation moisture that freezes inside fuel lines.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: Which four traffic-control elements govern road travel and must be obeyed by every driver?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Predictable traffic flow depends on every motorist following the same visual controls and statutory rules together.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: How does driving at higher speed affect crash severity, sight and stopping ability, and vehicle control?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Kinetic energy climbs fast with speed, shrinking your time to spot hazards while multiplying impact force.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: What happens to reaction distance and braking distance as your vehicle's speed climbs?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Even before your foot reaches the brake pedal, faster speed rolls your car much farther forward.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: Beyond safety hazards, which three financial costs come with driving at higher speeds?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Aggressive speed burns more gas every mile and triggers citations that raise annual insurance premiums.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: What five real-time surroundings determine the maximum safe speed under the fundamental speed rule?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Safe speed always adjusts to congestion, pavement grip, weather, sight distance, and nearby pedestrians or cyclists.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: When poor conditions or road hazards appear, can you still legally drive at the posted speed limit?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Driving the posted number during heavy rain, glare, or ice can still earn an unsafe-speed citation.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: May you ever exceed a posted speed limit, and what driving conditions does a posted limit assume?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Posted numbers mark the legal ceiling for dry daylight pavement, never a minimum target to chase.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: What speed-limit ranges apply to Massachusetts limited-access highways versus smaller highways?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Major divided expressways carry higher posted ceilings than secondary state highways with intersections and driveways.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: What is the minimum legal speed on the Massachusetts Turnpike?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Creeping below forty miles per hour on high-speed turnpike lanes creates severe rear-end closing hazards.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: What minimum speed applies inside the Callahan, Sumner, and Ted Williams tunnels?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Enclosed tunnel lanes lack breakdown shoulders, so steady movement above twenty miles per hour prevents dangerous backups.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: Even without a posted minimum speed, what can an officer direct a slow driver delaying traffic to do?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Impeding normal flow on a state highway lets police order you off to the roadside so cars pass.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: Unless another limit is posted, speeds above what number are improper inside a school zone?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Keeping school-zone speed at twenty miles per hour or below preserves stopping room for darting children.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: What is the default speed threshold in a thickly settled or business district unless twenty-five is posted?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Dense storefronts and closely spaced homes bring cross-traffic and pedestrians that cap unposted speeds at thirty.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: Outside a thickly settled or business district, what are the unposted default thresholds on roads versus highways?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Memorizing the twenty-thirty-forty-fifty ladder keeps you legal whenever speed signs have not yet appeared.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: What building spacing and road length define a thickly settled district in Massachusetts?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Recognizing closely spaced buildings over a quarter mile tells you the thirty-mile-per-hour rule applies without signs.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: How do towns notify motorists when adopting twenty-five miles per hour across thickly settled streets?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Boundary signs at municipal entrances lower every unposted thickly settled street inside town to twenty-five.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: Which two roadside indicators tell you a twenty-mile-per-hour school-zone limit is in effect?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Checking beacon lights and time plaques ensures you slow to twenty whenever school-zone enforcement is active.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: Who specifically should you scan for while driving through a school zone?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Young pedestrians, student cyclists, school patrols, and adult guards often step out from between parked cars.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: From top to bottom, how are the colors arranged on a standard vertical traffic signal?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Standardized top-to-bottom placement helps drivers with color-vision differences read every traffic light instantly.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: What does a steady round red light require when you are not making a legal turn on red?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Rolling past the line on steady red puts your vehicle directly into cross-street traffic and crosswalks.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: Under what conditions may you turn right at a steady red light, and what sign forbids it?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: Skipping the full stop or missing a posted No Turn on Red sign earns an automatic citation.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: Between which street types is a left turn on red legal after stopping and yielding?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: Turning left on red from or onto a two-way street crosses opposing lanes and is never legal.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.question_text: How does Massachusetts treat a steady red arrow compared with a steady round red light?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.teaching_text: Unlike states that ban all red-arrow turns, Massachusetts applies standard round-red and turn-on-red rules.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.question_text: Which roadside traffic sign carries the exact same stop-and-yield duty as a flashing red signal?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.teaching_text: Driver confusion between flashing red and steady red disappears once you equate flashing red with a stop sign.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.question_text: At a flashing red light, where must you stop when lines exist versus when none are painted?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.teaching_text: Stopping behind painted crosswalks protects walkers, while stopping at the sightline point lets you scan cross traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.question_text: What signal change does a steady yellow light announce, and what must you do if safe?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.teaching_text: Yellow clears the intersection before red appears, not an invitation to mash the gas pedal.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.question_text: If you are already stopped at a stop line or intersection, may you launch forward on steady yellow?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.teaching_text: Pulling out from a standstill on steady yellow virtually guarantees getting caught mid-intersection on red.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.question_text: How should you drive through an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow signal?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.teaching_text: Cross-street drivers usually face flashing red or stop signs, so staying alert prevents side-impact crashes.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.question_text: What two conditions must be clear before turning on a flashing yellow arrow?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.teaching_text: Permissive yellow arrows never stop opposing straight traffic or crossing walkers, so you must yield to both.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.question_text: Before accelerating on a green light, who still holds priority inside the intersection?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.teaching_text: Green grants permission to go only after pedestrians, cyclists, and lingering cars finish clearing the box.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.question_text: Even when facing a green light, what space check is required before entering an intersection?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.teaching_text: Pulling into backed-up traffic traps your car inside the box when cross-street signals turn green.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.question_text: Who has the right-of-way when you want to turn left on a steady round green light?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.teaching_text: Cutting across opposing straight-through lanes on a round green is a classic intersection crash cause.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.question_text: What movement does a lighted green arrow allow, and what signal should conflicting traffic face?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.teaching_text: Even during a protected arrow phase, scanning quickly guards against red-light runners or late walkers.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.question_text: What triggers a rectangular rapid-flashing beacon, and what must drivers do when its amber lights flash?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.teaching_text: Irregular high-intensity amber strobes alert every lane that someone is actively crossing at a crosswalk.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.question_text: How should you drive past a pedestrian hybrid beacon when all of its lights are dark?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.teaching_text: Unlike a power-outage intersection light, a pedestrian hybrid beacon stays dark whenever nobody has pressed it.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.question_text: On a pedestrian hybrid beacon, what do flashing yellow and steady yellow each require?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.teaching_text: The two-stage yellow warning gives approaching drivers smooth braking time before twin red lights lock in.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.question_text: What must you do when a pedestrian hybrid beacon displays two steady red lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.teaching_text: Twin solid red lamps mean the WALK interval is active and pedestrians are stepping across the road.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.question_text: How should you respond when a pedestrian hybrid beacon switches to two alternating flashing red lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.teaching_text: Alternating red flashes act like a stop sign so drivers wait until walkers finish clearing the crosswalk.

sec11-card-sec11-F39.question_text: How do bicycle traffic signals work when their bicycle symbol turns green?
sec11-card-sec11-F39.teaching_text: Dedicated bike phases separate straight-moving cyclists from turning motor vehicles that might otherwise hook them.

sec11-card-sec11-F40.question_text: If a malfunctioning traffic light flashes red or flashes yellow, what rule governs your approach?
sec11-card-sec11-F40.teaching_text: Backup flash mode assigns stop-sign duty to flashing red approaches and caution to flashing yellow approaches.

sec11-card-sec11-F41.question_text: How must every driver treat a completely dark, nonfunctioning intersection traffic signal?
sec11-card-sec11-F41.teaching_text: Assuming your street is the main road during a power outage causes high-speed T-bone collisions.

sec11-card-sec11-F42.question_text: Who has the right-of-way if a pedestrian is still in the crosswalk when the countdown hits zero?
sec11-card-sec11-F42.teaching_text: Slower walkers and seniors legally keep right-of-way until they reach the curb safely.

sec11-card-sec11-F43.question_text: What is your duty toward walkers stepping into or crossing a crosswalk ahead of your car?
sec11-card-sec11-F43.teaching_text: Stepping off the curb into your lane triggers an immediate duty to slow or stop short.

sec11-card-sec11-F44.question_text: May you ever stop your vehicle so that it blocks a pedestrian crosswalk?
sec11-card-sec11-F44.teaching_text: Parking your hood across crosswalk stripes forces walkers out into live moving traffic lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F45.question_text: Must drivers yield to pedestrians when facing a red light or a combined red-and-yellow signal?
sec11-card-sec11-F45.teaching_text: Massachusetts exclusive pedestrian phases light red and yellow together so walkers cross every direction unimpeded.

sec11-card-sec11-F46.question_text: What is the rule if a vehicle ahead stops or slows down for a pedestrian?
sec11-card-sec11-F46.teaching_text: Swinging into the next lane around a stopped car blinds you to the person walking across its bumper.

sec11-card-sec11-F47.question_text: Who has priority when you turn across a sidewalk into a driveway or parking lot?
sec11-card-sec11-F47.teaching_text: Sidewalk continuity gives pedestrians priority over every car pulling into or out of commercial entrances.

sec11-card-sec11-F48.question_text: Where crosswalks and push buttons exist, what must pedestrians do to cross?
sec11-card-sec11-F48.teaching_text: Activating the signal button triggers dedicated crossing time and warning lights for approaching traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F49.question_text: When may a pedestrian begin crossing, and what should someone mid-street do on DON'T WALK?
sec11-card-sec11-F49.teaching_text: DON'T WALK bars new curb step-outs while giving people already in the street buffer time to finish.

sec11-card-sec11-F50.question_text: What three checks should a pedestrian make at the curb before stepping into the street?
sec11-card-sec11-F50.teaching_text: Drivers making right or left turns often scan vehicle gaps while overlooking walkers stepping off the corner.

sec11-card-sec11-F51.question_text: On roadway signs, what do red backgrounds versus green backgrounds communicate?
sec11-card-sec11-F51.teaching_text: Instant color recognition lets you distinguish mandatory stops from directional highway exits at long range.

sec11-card-sec11-F52.question_text: What sign categories use yellow backgrounds versus black-and-white combinations?
sec11-card-sec11-F52.teaching_text: Yellow alerts you to upcoming physical hazards while black-and-white posts enforceable speed or lane laws.

sec11-card-sec11-F53.question_text: What information do blue signs versus brown signs provide along the road?
sec11-card-sec11-F53.teaching_text: Blue points toward gas, food, hospitals, or evacuation routes while brown marks historic and scenic sites.

sec11-card-sec11-F54.question_text: What road activity does an orange traffic sign warn you about?
sec11-card-sec11-F54.teaching_text: Spotting orange ahead is your cue to slow down and watch for crews, cones, and shifted lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F55.question_text: Which four specific warnings use high-visibility fluorescent yellow-green signs?
sec11-card-sec11-F55.teaching_text: Bright yellow-green stands out in dawn, dusk, and shade where walkers, cyclists, and curves appear.

sec11-card-sec11-F56.question_text: What special meanings belong to fluorescent pink signs and purple signs?
sec11-card-sec11-F56.teaching_text: Fluorescent pink marks temporary crash or emergency detours while purple flags electronic-toll lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-R28.question_text: Which motorist needs and facilities are identified by blue highway service signs?
sec11-card-sec11-R28.teaching_text: Scanning blue roadside panels lets highway drivers exit smoothly for gas, medical care, rest stops, or accessibility.

sec11-card-sec11-R29.question_text: What is the purpose of Bicycle Route and Bay State Greenway signs?
sec11-card-sec11-R29.teaching_text: Seeing green bike-corridor markers reminds motorists to expect steady bicycle traffic along that road.

sec11-card-sec11-R30.question_text: What upcoming highway feature does a Junction sign announce?
sec11-card-sec11-R30.teaching_text: Advance junction notices give you time to move into the right lane before routes intersect.

sec11-card-sec11-R31.question_text: In what unit of measurement do destination and highway-exit signs state distances?
sec11-card-sec11-R31.teaching_text: Reading green distance numbers in miles tells you whether your exit is seconds or minutes away.

sec11-card-sec11-R32.question_text: What do roadside mile markers identify along a highway?
sec11-card-sec11-R32.teaching_text: Noting milepost numbers lets you give emergency dispatchers your exact highway location during a breakdown.

sec11-card-sec11-R33.question_text: What do Parking guide signs and Rest Area signs each identify for motorists?
sec11-card-sec11-R33.teaching_text: Using designated rest areas instead of highway shoulders gives tired drivers a safe place off live lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-R34.question_text: What type of toll roadway is marked by an Electronic Tolling Only sign?
sec11-card-sec11-R34.teaching_text: Never slow or stop looking for a cash collector beneath overhead electronic toll gantries.

sec11-card-sec11-R35.question_text: Which traffic command belongs to an eight-sided octagon, and which belongs to a downward-pointing triangle?
sec11-card-sec11-R35.teaching_text: Unique silhouettes let you recognize Stop and Yield from the back or when snow covers the lettering.

sec11-card-sec11-R36.question_text: What do a sideways pennant sign shape and a five-sided pentagon sign shape each identify?
sec11-card-sec11-R36.teaching_text: Test questions regularly pair these two shapes to verify you never confuse passing bans with school zones.

sec11-card-sec11-R37.question_text: Which sign category uses a diamond shape, and what specific hazard uses a round sign?
sec11-card-sec11-R37.teaching_text: Only advance railroad-crossing warnings use a full circular sign, setting rail tracks apart from standard diamonds.

sec11-card-sec11-R38.question_text: What sign meanings correspond to a horizontal rectangle, a vertical rectangle, and a shield?
sec11-card-sec11-R38.teaching_text: Orientation separates directional highway boards from upright speed and parking rules, while shields mark interstates.

sec11-card-sec11-R43.question_text: What background colors appear on regulatory signs, and how do they state traffic laws?
sec11-card-sec11-R43.teaching_text: Regulatory panels post enforceable laws rather than optional tips, using crisp symbols, text, or both.

sec11-card-sec11-R44.question_text: What does a red circle with a diagonal red slash across a symbol mean?
sec11-card-sec11-R44.teaching_text: Any maneuver or vehicle pictured beneath a diagonal red slash is strictly prohibited ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-R45.question_text: What do yellow or fluorescent yellow-green warning signs announce, and how must you respond?
sec11-card-sec11-R45.teaching_text: Warning diamonds give advance notice so you shed speed before reaching the curve, merge, or crossing.

sec11-card-sec11-R46.question_text: What two navigation aids do green guide signs provide on highways?
sec11-card-sec11-R46.teaching_text: Reading overhead green panels early prevents last-second lane dives across exit gore zones.

sec11-card-sec11-R47.question_text: How are numbered Massachusetts state-route signs shaped and colored?
sec11-card-sec11-R47.teaching_text: Telling white rectangular state markers apart from interstate shields keeps you on the right numbered corridor.

sec11-card-sec11-R48.question_text: What shape and three colors identify an Interstate highway route marker?
sec11-card-sec11-R48.teaching_text: Distinctive tri-color shields mark multi-state controlled-access interstates like I-90, I-93, and I-95.

sec11-card-sec11-F57.question_text: Alongside Yield, which three prohibited turns and three barred road users open the regulatory sign group?
sec11-card-sec11-F57.teaching_text: Checking entry signs before turning into unfamiliar streets prevents illegal turns or entering restricted corridors.
sec11-card-sec11-F57.must_match_memory_hook: No turns; no trucks, walkers, bikes

visual_sync.text_span: No turns; no trucks, walkers, bikes

sec11-card-sec11-F58.question_text: What do a crossed-out right-turn arrow and a crossed-out left-turn arrow each forbid?
sec11-card-sec11-F58.teaching_text: Turning across a posted prohibition risks head-on conflict with one-way traffic or dedicated transit lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F59.question_text: What maneuver is barred by a regulatory sign showing a crossed-out U-shaped arrow?
sec11-card-sec11-F59.teaching_text: Reversing direction where sightlines or medians are tight traps your car sideways across oncoming lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F60.question_text: What does a red slash over a truck, pedestrian, or bicycle symbol mean?
sec11-card-sec11-F60.teaching_text: High-speed expressways and narrow weight-limited bridges use symbol bans to keep incompatible traffic separated.

sec11-card-sec11-F61.question_text: What does a No Parking sign displaying specific clock hours prohibit?
sec11-card-sec11-F61.teaching_text: Rush-hour and street-cleaning bans clear curb lanes during peak windows and trigger towing if ignored.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: How must traffic move when a One Way sign is posted?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Turning against a One Way arrow puts you nose-to-nose with every lane on that street.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: What maneuver does a rectangular white Do Not Pass sign forbid?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Hills, curves, and intersections hide oncoming cars where passing ahead would turn fatal.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: What does a posted No Turn on Red sign forbid after you stop at a red light?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Heavy pedestrian crossings and blind cross-street angles make red-light turns unsafe at posted corners.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: What must drivers do when occupying a lane signed with a left arrow and the word Only?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Driving straight out of a mandatory turn pocket sideswipes adjacent through-lane traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: What does a regulatory sign showing an arrow curving right around a divider island command?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Steering left of a raised median nose sends you straight into opposing oncoming lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: How does a general school-zone sign differ from a school-crossing sign?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: Spotting crosswalk lines beneath the walking students pinpoints the exact spot where kids cross.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: What does a warning diamond with a side arrow joining an upward arrow from the right mean?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Adjusting speed or lane position early helps ramp drivers blend in without sudden braking.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: What is the difference between Divided Highway Begins and Divided Highway Ends warning signs?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: Confusing the two is dangerous when a median ends and opposing traffic returns beside a yellow line.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.question_text: What road geometry ahead does a winding-road warning sign announce?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.teaching_text: Entering linked bends too fast compounds weight transfer and pulls tires wide across the centerline.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.question_text: How does a sharp ninety-degree right-angle warning arrow differ from a smooth curved right arrow?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.teaching_text: A squared-off turn arrow warns of a much tighter bend requiring deeper braking than a sweeping curve.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.question_text: What nearby area does a playground warning sign alert drivers to watch for?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.teaching_text: Children chasing balls near parks rarely check traffic before running toward the curb.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.question_text: What intersection layout ahead is shown by a warning sign with a black plus symbol?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.teaching_text: Cross traffic can enter from both left and right across a hidden rural or suburban crossroad.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.question_text: What roadside hazard does a Soft Shoulder warning sign alert you about?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.teaching_text: Dropping right-side tires into soft dirt can tug steering sideways or roll a car if you yank back.

sec11-card-sec11-R14.question_text: Which two types of pedestrian warning signs alert drivers to walking crossings?
sec11-card-sec11-R14.teaching_text: Advance signs prepare you to slow early before reaching the marked crosswalk sign itself.

sec11-card-sec11-R15.question_text: What do warning diamonds picturing an octagon symbol versus a traffic-light symbol announce?
sec11-card-sec11-R15.teaching_text: Advance control warnings prevent panic braking when curves, hills, or foliage hide an upcoming stop.

sec11-card-sec11-R16.question_text: What traffic pattern is indicated by a warning sign with one down arrow and one up arrow?
sec11-card-sec11-R16.teaching_text: Leaving a one-way street or divided road requires keeping right because oncoming cars share the roadway.

sec11-card-sec11-R17.question_text: What does an intersection warning sign with a short branch joining the vertical line on the right mean?
sec11-card-sec11-R17.teaching_text: Scanning that right-hand junction early spots drivers pulling out from blind driveways or side streets.

sec11-card-sec11-R18.question_text: What pavement-line rule does a No Passing Zone pennant sign enforce?
sec11-card-sec11-R18.teaching_text: Left-side pennant signs pair with solid yellow stripes so sight-blocked passing bans stay unmistakable.

sec11-card-sec11-R19.question_text: What lane change ahead does a Right Lane Ends warning sign announce?
sec11-card-sec11-R19.teaching_text: Checking mirrors and signaling left early avoids getting squeezed onto the shoulder when pavement runs out.

sec11-card-sec11-R20.question_text: What surface hazard is announced by a warning sign showing a car above curvy skid tracks?
sec11-card-sec11-R20.teaching_text: Rain lifts road oil onto smooth asphalt or bridge decks, demanding gentler steering and longer following gaps.

sec11-card-sec11-R21.question_text: What upcoming road layout does a T-shaped intersection warning sign indicate?
sec11-card-sec11-R21.teaching_text: Approaching drivers cannot continue straight and must slow to turn left or right after yielding.

sec11-card-sec11-R22.question_text: What limit does a low-clearance warning sign with top and bottom arrows state?
sec11-card-sec11-R22.teaching_text: Drivers of box trucks, vans, or roof-racked SUVs must check clearance numbers to avoid bridge strikes.

sec11-card-sec11-R23.question_text: What intersection type ahead is signaled by three chasing arrows arranged in a circle?
sec11-card-sec11-R23.teaching_text: Slowing early prepares you to yield to circulating traffic already traveling counterclockwise inside the rotary.

sec11-card-sec11-R24.question_text: What does a warning sign with two downward-angled arrows splitting both sides of an island mean?
sec11-card-sec11-R24.teaching_text: Same-direction lanes divide around a central support pier or gore while continuing toward valid routes.

sec11-card-sec11-R25.question_text: What roadside hazard does a yellow diamond picturing a leaping deer announce?
sec11-card-sec11-R25.teaching_text: Deer travel in small groups especially around dawn and dusk, so spotting one means scanning for more.

sec11-card-sec11-R26.question_text: What hazard ahead is announced by a yellow circular sign marked with an X and two Rs?
sec11-card-sec11-R26.teaching_text: Slowing, quieting cabin noise, and scanning both ways down the tracks prevents train collisions.

sec11-card-sec11-R27.question_text: How does an Added Lane warning sign differ from a Right Merge warning sign?
sec11-card-sec11-R27.teaching_text: Entering traffic gets its own new lane on an added-lane sign instead of blending directly into yours.

sec11-card-sec11-R39.question_text: Where must every approaching vehicle come to a complete halt at a Stop sign?
sec11-card-sec11-R39.teaching_text: Creeping across the white stop bar before stopping intrudes into pedestrian space and fails road tests.

sec11-card-sec11-R40.question_text: Why is slowing down not enough at a Stop sign, and what comes right after halting?
sec11-card-sec11-R40.teaching_text: A rolling slow-down is a moving violation and cuts short the pause needed to spot cross traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-R41.question_text: What does an All Way or Four Way plaque mean beneath Stop, and who goes first?
sec11-card-sec11-R41.teaching_text: Confirming every approach has halted lets the earliest arrival move through cleanly in turn.

sec11-card-sec11-R42.question_text: What actions does a Yield sign require toward vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians?
sec11-card-sec11-R42.teaching_text: Treat a Yield triangle as a potential full stop whenever cross traffic or walkers occupy your path.

sec11-card-sec11-R49.question_text: How must you respond to an advance railroad warning, and what must you never try?
sec11-card-sec11-R49.teaching_text: Large locomotives look slower than their true closing speed, turning attempts to beat a train deadly.

sec11-card-sec11-R50.question_text: What does a white X-shaped crossbuck mark, and when is a numbered plaque added below it?
sec11-card-sec11-R50.teaching_text: Seeing a multiple-track number warns you a second hidden train could arrive right behind the first.

sec11-card-sec11-R51.question_text: At least how far back from the gate or light post must you stop when railroad red lights flash?
sec11-card-sec11-R51.teaching_text: Leaving a fifteen-foot buffer keeps your front bumper clear of descending gate arms and train overhang.

sec11-card-sec11-R52.question_text: Which two conditions must both occur before you pull forward after stopping at a railroad crossing?
sec11-card-sec11-R52.teaching_text: Moving as soon as the last car clears while bells and red lamps still flash risks hitting a second train.

sec11-card-sec11-R53.question_text: If no train is visible, may you ever drive around a lowered railroad gate or past flashing lights?
sec11-card-sec11-R53.teaching_text: Curves, brush, or a passing train on track one can hide a fast oncoming locomotive.

sec11-card-sec11-R54.question_text: What two immediate steps should you take as you approach a highway or street work zone?
sec11-card-sec11-R54.teaching_text: Narrowed lanes, equipment, and sudden brake lights leave zero margin for full highway speed.

sec11-card-sec11-R55.question_text: Whose instructions must you obey in a work zone, and what happens when police conflict with signs?
sec11-card-sec11-R55.teaching_text: Live traffic controllers see real-time crew movements that fixed signs, lights, and paint cannot reflect.

sec11-card-sec11-R56.question_text: Where should your eyes stay focused while passing active machinery inside a work zone?
sec11-card-sec11-R56.teaching_text: Staring at excavators or paving crews for two seconds causes rear-end chain crashes in tight lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-R57.question_text: How do early warning or electronic boards work together with later signs inside a work zone?
sec11-card-sec11-R57.teaching_text: Reading advance boards early lets you set speed and lane position before reaching the taper.

sec11-card-sec11-R58.question_text: How do orange drums, cones, and tubular markers guide drivers through a lane closure?
sec11-card-sec11-R58.teaching_text: Channelizing tapers buffer workers from traffic and show where to blend smoothly into open lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-R59.question_text: What do work-zone barricades typically block off on a street or highway?
sec11-card-sec11-R59.teaching_text: Driving past a barricade puts your car into open trenches, wet concrete, or active work crews.

sec11-card-sec11-R60.question_text: Where do orange Detour signs lead you when a roadway or direction is closed?
sec11-card-sec11-R60.teaching_text: Staying on marked detour arrows routes you around the blockage and reconnects with your original road.

sec11-card-sec11-R61.question_text: What two pieces of lane information do portable flashing arrow boards give on multilane roads?
sec11-card-sec11-R61.teaching_text: High-mounted illuminated arrows give long-range notice to merge well before reaching the cone taper.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: What are the very first two things to do as you approach a roadway work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Shedding speed immediately gives you time to read temporary signs, cones, and flagger directions safely.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: What do short dotted white or yellow dashes mean when continuing from a solid lane line?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Tracking dotted extension dashes prevents dual-turn vehicles from drifting into each other mid-intersection.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: Except for which three intentional maneuvers must you keep your vehicle between painted lane lines?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Straddling lane stripes crowds adjacent drivers and leaves other motorists guessing which lane you claim.
sec12-card-sec12-F03.must_match_memory_hook: Stay centered except turns, exits, changes

visual_sync.text_span: Stay centered except turns, exits, changes

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: What traffic flow do white lane lines separate, and which road edge can they mark?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Seeing white between lanes confirms neighboring traffic travels your way rather than head-on.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: When may you cross a broken white line to move into an adjacent lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Dashed white paint permits lane changes only once mirrors, blind spots, and turn signals confirm a gap.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: Where do single solid white lines appear, and when is crossing one appropriate?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Solid white discourages lane weaving near hazards or shoulders unless an immediate obstacle forces avoidance.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: Is crossing double solid white lines between same-direction lanes ever allowed?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Twin solid white stripes form a legal barrier in tunnels, bridges, and high-conflict merge zones.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: What traffic streams do yellow lines divide, and which pavement edge can they mark?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Keeping yellow paint on your left side ensures you never drift into oncoming lanes or medians.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: On which side of a single broken yellow line must you travel, and when may you cross it?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Crossing left of a dashed yellow centerline borrows an oncoming lane briefly only when sightlines stay clear.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: When a solid yellow line pairs with a broken yellow line, which side may pass?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Always read the stripe closest to your tires because your sight distance differs from oncoming traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: May drivers in either direction cross two solid yellow lines to overtake another vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Twin solid yellow stripes lock down overtaking for both directions where hills, curves, or traffic block sight.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: While passing is forbidden across double solid yellow lines, what turning movement is generally allowed?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Entering driveways or side streets requires turning left across double yellow once oncoming traffic clears.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: What do large white arrows painted directly on a traffic lane communicate?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Pavement arrows reinforce overhead signs early so you do not get trapped in a turn-only lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.question_text: How does a painted stop line look different from a painted yield line on the pavement?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.teaching_text: Spotting shark-tooth white triangles versus a thick white bar clarifies whether a full stop is mandatory.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.question_text: How is a pedestrian crosswalk marked across a traffic lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.teaching_text: Brick, textured surfacing, or painted white bars all carry full legal crosswalk protection for walkers.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.question_text: Besides street intersections, at what four kinds of community spots should you expect crosswalks?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.teaching_text: Scanning midblock near bus stops, bike paths, schools, and storefronts prevents surprise pedestrian encounters.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.question_text: Where must your front bumper stop whenever a sign, signal, or crossing pedestrian requires halting?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.teaching_text: Stopping short of the painted line keeps pedestrians safe and leaves turning room for cross traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.question_text: What two traffic-control jobs does a painted or raised channelizing island perform?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.teaching_text: Channelizing islands separate conflicting turn angles and shield pedestrian refuge spaces at wide intersections.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.question_text: When, if ever, may you drive across or park on a channelizing island?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.teaching_text: Cutting across painted or curbed islands surprises merging drivers and is illegal without police direction.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.question_text: What is your duty when approaching crossing guards and school children near the street?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.teaching_text: Crossing guards hold traffic until every child reaches the opposite sidewalk safely.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.question_text: Which three visual cues warn you early that a crossing guard or children may be ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.teaching_text: Catching neon vests and handheld STOP paddles from a block away lets you brake smoothly.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: What does a large white diamond painted inside a travel lane signify?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Entering a diamond-marked lane solo or outside posted rules brings a restricted-lane citation.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.question_text: How do shared-lane markings help bicyclists on streets shared with motor vehicles?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.teaching_text: Chevrons above bike icons steer riders away from opening car doors and show right-way direction.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.question_text: What does a sharrow tell motorists to do, and is it a dedicated bicycle lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.teaching_text: Unlike a striped bike lane, a sharrow marks a full travel lane shared by cars and bikes.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.question_text: How wide is a typical bicycle lane, and how is it marked along the road?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.teaching_text: Recognizing the five-foot corridor bounded by solid white paint keeps car tires out of cyclist space.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.question_text: For what single purpose may a motor vehicle enter a bicycle lane, and what check comes first?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.teaching_text: Checking mirrors and right blind spots before crossing a bike stripe prevents right-hook collisions.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.question_text: When may a motorist use space inside a dashed advisory bicycle lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.teaching_text: Narrow streets without centerlines let passing cars edge across dashed bike stripes only when cyclists clear.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.question_text: What does bright green pavement highlight, and what must drivers do before crossing it?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.teaching_text: Green paint flags driveways, merges, and turn pockets where car paths cross straight-riding cyclists.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.question_text: Where must you avoid stopping your vehicle when waiting at a red traffic signal with green pavement?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.teaching_text: Green bike boxes ahead of stop bars let cyclists position visibly in front of queued cars.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.question_text: What public-transportation facilities are marked by red-colored pavement?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.teaching_text: Red bus lanes keep high-capacity transit coaches moving past general car congestion.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.question_text: On a multilane road in your direction, which lane is default and what three exceptions allow leaving it?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.teaching_text: Cruising needlessly in left lanes bottlenecks passing flow and triggers impatient right-side overtaking.
sec12-card-sec12-F40.must_match_memory_hook: Keep right except pass, left, block

visual_sync.text_span: Keep right except pass, left, block

sec12-card-sec12-F41.question_text: Is changing lanes while driving inside an intersection legal in Massachusetts?
sec12-card-sec12-F41.teaching_text: Turning cross-street drivers rely on through traffic holding its lane all the way across.

sec12-card-sec12-F42.question_text: When is driving in a highway breakdown lane permitted, and what is the general rule?
sec12-card-sec12-F42.teaching_text: Outside explicitly signed rush-hour corridors, breakdown shoulders belong strictly to disabled cars and emergency crews.

sec12-card-sec12-F43.question_text: What two adjustments must you make when entering a curve with an obstructed view?
sec12-card-sec12-F43.teaching_text: Keeping speed down and tucked right leaves vital margin if an oncoming vehicle drifts wide.

sec12-card-sec12-F44.question_text: For what single maneuver may an unauthorized driver briefly enter a posted restricted lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F44.teaching_text: Using a bus or HOV lane to bypass traffic ahead of your turn block earns a ticket.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.question_text: Why must you signal whenever stopping or changing your vehicle's movement?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.teaching_text: Early visual warning lets nearby pedestrians, cyclists, and trailing drivers adjust before your tires move.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.question_text: What must you use if your vehicle's electronic turn or brake signals stop working?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.teaching_text: Extending standard arm signals out the left window keeps traffic informed until burnt bulbs get fixed.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.question_text: Where must a driver extend the required left-turn hand signal when electronic blinkers fail?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.teaching_text: Drivers always signal with their left arm straight out the driver-side window where trailing traffic looks.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.question_text: Where is a driver's right-turn hand signal given, and what must road-test applicants demonstrate?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.teaching_text: Massachusetts road-test examiners check all three arm signals before pulling away from the curb.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.question_text: How does giving a slowing-or-stopping hand signal differ between motor-vehicle drivers and bicyclists?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.teaching_text: Enclosed car bodies restrict drivers to the left window while open handlebars let cyclists use either arm.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.question_text: Which five everyday driving maneuvers require activating your turn signal?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.teaching_text: Pulling away from a curb or taking an exit ramp needs signaling just like street corners.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.question_text: What should you confirm about your directional signal right after completing a lane change or turn?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.teaching_text: Driving blocks with a forgotten blinker misleads cross-street drivers into pulling out right in front.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.question_text: What exact sequence of checks and actions comes before turning, merging, or changing lanes?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.teaching_text: Mirrors miss cars tucked beside your rear quarter panel, making the shoulder head-check essential.

sec12-card-sec12-F39.question_text: Which arm may a bicyclist legally use to give directional hand signals?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.teaching_text: Pointing directly right with the right arm lets cyclists keep their left hand steady on front brakes.

sec12-card-sec12-F45.question_text: What roadway design feature defines a divided highway?
sec12-card-sec12-F45.teaching_text: Guardrails, grass medians, or concrete barriers split opposing traffic streams to prevent head-on crashes.

sec12-card-sec12-F46.question_text: How do vehicles enter and leave controlled-access expressways that lack traffic lights and intersections?
sec12-card-sec12-F46.teaching_text: Eliminating cross-street signals and driveways keeps freeway traffic flowing uninterrupted via ramps.

sec12-card-sec12-F47.question_text: When should you position your vehicle in the proper lane for entering or leaving a highway?
sec12-card-sec12-F47.teaching_text: Last-second swoops across three expressway lanes for an exit ramp trigger multi-car pileups.

sec12-card-sec12-F48.question_text: Who holds the right-of-way when you merge onto a highway from an entrance ramp?
sec12-card-sec12-F48.teaching_text: Through highway traffic never has to brake for merging cars, so ramp drivers time a safe gap.

sec12-card-sec12-F49.question_text: How should you adjust your speed while accelerating onto a highway?
sec12-card-sec12-F49.teaching_text: Merging twenty miles per hour slower than mainline traffic forces trucks and cars into emergency braking.

sec12-card-sec12-F50.question_text: What is the only safe choice if you accidentally drive past your intended highway exit?
sec12-card-sec12-F50.teaching_text: Stopping or backing up on a high-speed expressway shoulder invites catastrophic rear-end impacts.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: At least how many feet before a highway exit ramp must you start signaling?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: At sixty miles per hour, five hundred feet passes in under six seconds, giving trailing cars fair notice.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: What two precautions apply as you leave a highway onto an exit ramp?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Tightly curved exit ramps often hide queued red-light traffic while demanding sharp speed drops.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: What two vehicle requirements must be met before taking a car onto a highway?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Underpowered or poorly maintained vehicles break down or crawl dangerously below expressway flow.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: On an expressway with three or more lanes in one direction, how are right, middle, and left assigned?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Sorting traffic by speed across three lanes keeps merging ramps calm and left passing lanes open.
sec12-card-sec12-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Right slower, middle faster, left pass

visual_sync.text_span: Right slower, middle faster, left pass

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: Where within your highway lane should you track, and how should every lane change be made?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Holding the center cushion maximizes side clearance while full mirror-and-shoulder checks prevent high-speed sideswipes.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: How should you handle driving through another motorist's blind spot on the highway?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Hovering off someone's rear fender hides your car right where a quick lane change can clip you.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: Where do large trucks and buses have blind spots, and how should you position around them?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: Tailgating a trailer or pacing beside cab wheels leaves the commercial driver completely blind to your car.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: What two right-side highway situations require constant scanning as you cruise?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: Spotting entering traffic and disabled roadside vehicles early lets you move left or ease speed smoothly.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.question_text: What is the rule on weaving back and forth across highway traffic lanes?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.teaching_text: Rapid multi-lane cuts shrink safe following gaps and catch neighboring motorists in the middle of lane changes.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.question_text: What should you do when long highway miles start causing driver fatigue?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.teaching_text: Pulling off at the next exit, service plaza, or rest area beats risking a seventy-mile-per-hour microsleep.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.question_text: Where breakdown-lane travel is legally open, what must you check before crossing to an exit ramp?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.teaching_text: Commuters legally cruising inside an active breakdown lane approach fast on your right side near exits.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.question_text: How often in hours or miles should you stop and stretch during a long drive?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.teaching_text: Planned breaks restore circulation and focus before highway hypnosis dulls reaction times.

sec12-card-sec12-R13.question_text: If your car breaks down on a highway, where should you park and where should you wait?
sec12-card-sec12-R13.teaching_text: Standing in the breakdown lane exposes your body directly to distracted drivers drifting off the edge.

sec12-card-sec12-R14.question_text: How does Massachusetts traffic law define an intersection?
sec12-card-sec12-R14.teaching_text: Even unmarked T-junctions without signals count as legal intersections where turning and right-of-way rules apply.
sec12-card-sec12-R14.must_match_memory_hook: Where two or more roads meet

visual_sync.text_span: Where two or more roads meet

sec12-card-sec12-R15.question_text: What guides your exact path when an intersection provides multiple side-by-side turn lanes?
sec12-card-sec12-R15.teaching_text: Holding your assigned inner or outer arc prevents sideswiping the car turning right beside you.

sec12-card-sec12-R16.question_text: When must you wait behind the line instead of entering an intersection or crosswalk?
sec12-card-sec12-R16.teaching_text: Stopping mid-box traps cross traffic and forces pedestrians to weave between bumpers.

sec12-card-sec12-R17.question_text: What bicycle safety habit should you practice before pulling out at any intersection?
sec12-card-sec12-R17.teaching_text: Slim bicycle silhouettes hide easily behind windshield pillars during a single quick glance.

sec12-card-sec12-R18.question_text: Who has priority when you want to turn across the path of a bicyclist riding straight through?
sec12-card-sec12-R18.teaching_text: Overtaking a cyclist and hooking right across their front wheel is one of urban driving's worst crashes.

sec12-card-sec12-R19.question_text: How should every turn be approached rather than swerving at the last moment?
sec12-card-sec12-R19.teaching_text: Abrupt unannounced turns give trailing cars and curbside cyclists zero chance to brake.

sec12-card-sec12-R20.question_text: How many feet ahead must you signal a turn on surface streets versus on a highway?
sec12-card-sec12-R20.teaching_text: Higher expressway speeds cover ground five times faster, requiring five times the advance blinker distance.
sec12-card-sec12-R20.must_match_memory_hook: One hundred street, five hundred highway

visual_sync.text_span: One hundred street, five hundred highway

sec12-card-sec12-R21.question_text: Should you tap the brakes first or turn on your blinker first when preparing to turn?
sec12-card-sec12-R21.teaching_text: Flashing your turn signal before brake lights glow explains why you are slowing to the driver behind.

sec12-card-sec12-R22.question_text: Which four preparation steps come right before steering into a turn?
sec12-card-sec12-R22.teaching_text: Checking the turning-side blind spot right after slowing catches cyclists or scooters alongside your fender.

sec12-card-sec12-R23.question_text: If you need a different lane after turning onto a new street, when may you change lanes?
sec12-card-sec12-R23.teaching_text: Drifting diagonally into a second lane mid-turn cuts off opposing drivers turning into the adjacent lane.

sec12-card-sec12-R24.question_text: Which lane must you start from for a standard right turn versus a standard left turn?
sec12-card-sec12-R24.teaching_text: Turning from inner travel lanes cuts directly across cars continuing straight beside you.

sec12-card-sec12-R25.question_text: Why must you stay centered in your start and finish lanes rather than swinging wide for turns?
sec12-card-sec12-R25.teaching_text: Swinging left before a right turn tricks trailing drivers into thinking you are changing lanes left.

sec12-card-sec12-R26.question_text: What should you do if you have already started turning through an intersection into the wrong street?
sec12-card-sec12-R26.teaching_text: Freezing or jerking the steering wheel back mid-intersection causes immediate T-bone or rear-end collisions.

sec12-card-sec12-R27.question_text: Which three conditions are all mandatory before making a right turn on a red light?
sec12-card-sec12-R27.teaching_text: Missing any single piece of the stop-yield-sign check turns a legal right-on-red into a ticket.

sec12-card-sec12-R28.question_text: When is a left turn on a red signal legal in Massachusetts?
sec12-card-sec12-R28.teaching_text: Because no opposing traffic exists between two one-way streets, stopping and yielding makes the turn safe.

sec12-card-sec12-R29.question_text: What does a U-turn do, and what two conditions must hold for it to be legal?
sec12-card-sec12-R29.teaching_text: Even without a No U-Turn sign, turning across tight or busy lanes violates safe-path rules.

sec12-card-sec12-R30.question_text: From which lane must a U-turn begin, and how much clearance is needed?
sec12-card-sec12-R30.teaching_text: Starting a U-turn from a right curb lane sweeps across same-direction traffic moving up beside you.

sec12-card-sec12-R31.question_text: How many feet of clear visibility in both directions are required to make a legal U-turn?
sec12-card-sec12-R31.teaching_text: Hillcrests and curves hide fast-closing traffic while your car sits broadside across the road.

sec12-card-sec12-R32.question_text: On two-way streets, what is a shared middle lane strictly reserved for, and what is forbidden?
sec12-card-sec12-R32.teaching_text: Both directions enter that middle pocket to turn left, so using it for passing risks head-on crashes.

sec12-card-sec12-R33.question_text: Under what street, traffic, visibility, and legal conditions should you consider a three-point turn?
sec12-card-sec12-R33.teaching_text: Because a three-point turn blocks both lanes perpendicular to traffic, use it only when no alternative exists.

sec12-card-sec12-R34.question_text: Before starting a three-point turn from the right curb, what checks and traffic gap are required?
sec12-card-sec12-R34.teaching_text: Waiting for a full twenty-to-thirty-second window ensures nobody crests a block away mid-turn.

sec12-card-sec12-R35.question_text: How do you steer and where do you stop during step one of a three-point turn?
sec12-card-sec12-R35.teaching_text: Halting two feet short of the opposite curb leaves room to crank the wheels right without bumping.

sec12-card-sec12-R36.question_text: Which way do you turn the wheel and look during the backing phase of a three-point turn?
sec12-card-sec12-R36.teaching_text: Turning physically to look out the rear window over your right shoulder outperforms mirrors alone.

sec12-card-sec12-R37.question_text: Where must you stop backing during the second leg of a three-point turn?
sec12-card-sec12-R37.teaching_text: Stopping before your rear tires strike the curb prevents rolling onto the sidewalk where pedestrians walk.

sec12-card-sec12-R38.question_text: Which checks, signal, and gear step finish a three-point turn cleanly?
sec12-card-sec12-R38.teaching_text: Forgetting to shift out of Reverse before pressing the gas backs your car straight over the curb.

sec12-card-sec12-R39.question_text: How do you position, check, and steer when backing straight along a curb?
sec12-card-sec12-R39.teaching_text: Creeping smoothly while looking over your right shoulder keeps the car straight alongside the curb.

sec12-card-sec12-R40.question_text: How does the manual frame right-of-way when another driver ignores traffic rules?
sec12-card-sec12-R40.teaching_text: Insisting on legal priority against a careless driver wins an argument only inside a tow yard.

sec12-card-sec12-R41.question_text: Who has priority if your traffic signal turns green while a pedestrian is still in the crosswalk?
sec12-card-sec12-R41.teaching_text: A fresh green light never lets you crowd or honk at someone finishing their crossing.

sec12-card-sec12-R42.question_text: Who holds right-of-way when a driver turns across a sidewalk, driveway, or alley?
sec12-card-sec12-R42.teaching_text: Every driveway apron and alley entrance crosses pedestrian space where walkers always come first.

sec12-card-sec12-R43.question_text: What must you do and avoid doing when a blind pedestrian crosses the street?
sec12-card-sec12-R43.teaching_text: Blind travelers rely on traffic sound cues, so honking startles them and hand waves go unseen.

sec12-card-sec12-R44.question_text: How should you approach an intersection with no signs or lights, and which side gets priority?
sec12-card-sec12-R44.teaching_text: Without stop signs or signals, yielding to cars on your right resolves tie-breakers predictably.

sec12-card-sec12-R45.question_text: Even when you are on the right at an uncontrolled corner, what must you verify on your left?
sec12-card-sec12-R45.teaching_text: Never bet your doors on another motorist noticing an unmarked neighborhood intersection.

sec12-card-sec12-R46.question_text: At an all-way stop, who goes first, and what breaks a simultaneous-arrival tie?
sec12-card-sec12-R46.teaching_text: Arrival order sets the queue, and yielding to the driver on your right settles ties cleanly.

sec12-card-sec12-R47.question_text: What visual habit helps drivers clarify intentions and prevent crashes at an all-way stop?
sec12-card-sec12-R47.teaching_text: Confirming the other driver actually sees you avoids awkward double-starts into the middle.

sec12-card-sec12-R48.question_text: Which three groups must a driver yield to before making any left turn?
sec12-card-sec12-R48.teaching_text: Focusing only on oncoming headlights often blinds left-turners to pedestrians and cyclists in the crosswalk.

sec12-card-sec12-R49.question_text: What must you do before entering a paved through street from a driveway, private road, or dirt road?
sec12-card-sec12-R49.teaching_text: Paved public roadways and their sidewalks always hold priority over private driveways and unpaved lanes.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.question_text: How much space and speed should you use beside an animal or horse-drawn vehicle going your way?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.teaching_text: Crowding or rushing past a horse or buggy can spook the animal right into your lane.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.question_text: What sound restriction applies whenever you drive near an animal?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.teaching_text: Sudden horn blasts or revving engines startle horses and livestock into dangerous unpredictable bolting.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.question_text: What must you do immediately if an animal you are passing looks frightened?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.teaching_text: Continuing to creep past a panicked animal only escalates the risk for rider and driver alike.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.question_text: How must you respond if an animal's rider or cart driver signals you to stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.teaching_text: Riders feel tension in the reins before you see it, so obey their stop hand immediately.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.question_text: Which animals fall under the Massachusetts animal-passing law, and what seasonal ride requires extra caution?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.teaching_text: Farm cattle, working draft teams, and open passenger hayrides all demand extra patience on rural roads.

sec14-card-sec14-F42.question_text: What does Massachusetts law say about driving on a wager or drag racing?
sec14-card-sec14-F42.teaching_text: Racing or betting behind the wheel turns public streets into felony-level crash zones with severe license loss.

sec14-card-sec14-F43.question_text: What does Massachusetts prohibit regarding throwing objects or dumping trash and glass from vehicles?
sec14-card-sec14-F43.teaching_text: Flying debris shatters windshields and punctured tires hazard every driver, cyclist, and landowner nearby.

sec14-card-sec14-F44.question_text: What fire-related items are illegal to toss near a forest or open field?
sec14-card-sec14-F44.teaching_text: One glowing cigarette butt in dry roadside grass can ignite a fast-moving brush or forest wildfire.

sec14-card-sec14-F45.question_text: Is it legal in Massachusetts to bypass or disable the effect of your vehicle's muffler system?
sec14-card-sec14-F45.teaching_text: Cutouts and straight-pipe deletes break state equipment law and fail annual vehicle inspections.

sec14-card-sec14-F46.question_text: Where should you take used motor oil, transmission fluid, and other hazardous car fluids?
sec14-card-sec14-F46.teaching_text: Pouring automotive fluids in trash or storm drains poisons groundwater, whereas retail sellers recycle them properly.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.question_text: What basic safety rule governs every stopped or parked vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.teaching_text: Even where signs allow stopping, leaving your car jutting into blind curves or lanes creates danger.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.question_text: At least how many feet of unobstructed roadway must remain open for passing traffic when you park?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.teaching_text: Fire engines and passing cars cannot squeeze past safely if parked vehicles pinch the road narrower.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.question_text: What five steps must you take before walking away from an unattended vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.teaching_text: Shutting down, setting the parking brake, locking the ignition, pulling the key, and locking doors prevents rollaways and theft.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.question_text: What three steps must you follow before pulling away from a curb into traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.teaching_text: Cars already moving in the travel lane hold right of way over parked drivers pulling out.
