sec14-card-sec14-F10.question_text: Unless angled parking is permitted, how close to the curb must you park in business or residential districts?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.teaching_text: Leaving tires more than a foot off the curb narrows the travel lane and risks mirror strikes.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.question_text: What two things should you verify when choosing a parallel-parking space?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.teaching_text: Forcing your car into a tight hydrant zone wastes time and fails a road test fast.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.question_text: How far beside the front parked car and aligned with what landmarks do you start parallel parking?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.teaching_text: Starting two or three feet out with rear bumpers or front seats even sets clean backing geometry.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.question_text: Before reversing into a parallel-parking space, what check must you make?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.teaching_text: Pedestrians and cyclists can step near the curb right as your front end swings toward traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.question_text: Where should you look while actively reversing into a parallel-parking space?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.teaching_text: Examiners deduct points when you stare only at mirrors or cameras instead of turning to look back.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.question_text: At what clearance point during parallel parking do you reverse your steering direction?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.teaching_text: Turning the wheel the opposite way too early clips the front car's bumper; too late hits the curb.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.question_text: How do you finish positioning your car once you have backed far enough into a parallel space?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.teaching_text: Pulling centered leaves both neighboring drivers room to maneuver out without tapping your bumpers.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.question_text: How must you set the brake and transmission when parking on any hill?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.teaching_text: Pairing the parking brake with Park or an engaged manual gear provides backup if a cable slips.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.question_text: Which way do you turn your front wheels when parking uphill or downhill without a curb?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.teaching_text: Pointing tires toward the shoulder sends a rolling car off the pavement rather than into traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.question_text: Which direction do you point your front wheels when parked uphill next to a curb?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.teaching_text: Turning away from the curb lets the back of your front tire catch the curb if gravity pulls.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.question_text: Which direction do you point your front wheels when parked downhill next to a curb?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.teaching_text: Pointing inward wedges the front tire straight against the curb face if the car creeps forward.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.question_text: How must a vehicle sit relative to painted parking-space lines?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.teaching_text: Straddling a painted line steals an adjacent stall and earns an easy municipal parking ticket.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.question_text: Which three posted curb-restriction signs forbid leaving your car parked?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.teaching_text: All three curb signs bar leaving a parked vehicle, with No Stopping banning even brief pauses.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.question_text: Which three working or cycling curb zones are off-limits for general parking?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.teaching_text: Blocking a bike lane forces cyclists into fast traffic, while taxi and loading zones serve active pickups.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.question_text: What dollar penalty applies to parking in a posted bus stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.teaching_text: Forcing a transit bus to load riders in the travel lane triggers a hundred-dollar fine.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.question_text: When is parking prohibited inside a posted street-cleaning zone?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.teaching_text: Checking exact day-and-hour plaques saves you from tickets and tow trucks on street-sweeping days.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.question_text: Within how many feet of an intersection is parking prohibited?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.teaching_text: Cars parked right on corners blind turning drivers and hide pedestrians stepping off the curb.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.question_text: Which three pedestrian or property access points must never be blocked by a parked car?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.teaching_text: Blocking curb cuts traps wheelchair users, and blocking crosswalks or driveways hazards walkers and homeowners.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.question_text: What authorization is required for disabled parking spaces, and what is the listed first-offense fine?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.teaching_text: Even quick errands without valid disability plates or a placard carry a steep three-hundred-dollar first ticket.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.question_text: May a driver displaying a valid disability placard park in the crosshatched stripes beside an accessible stall?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.teaching_text: Wheelchair lifts and ramps deploy into that striped zone, so nobody may ever park on it.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.question_text: Within how many feet of a fire hydrant or fire lane is parking prohibited in Massachusetts?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.teaching_text: Memorize ten feet for Massachusetts hydrants and twenty feet for intersections so test numbers never blur.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.question_text: Which four raised pedestrian or divider surfaces must never be used for parking?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.teaching_text: Mounting curbs, sidewalks, islands, or medians blocks foot travel and damages roadside infrastructure.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.question_text: What happens to street parking permissions during a roadway or weather emergency?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.teaching_text: Snowplows and emergency rigs need curb-to-curb clearance whenever storm or roadway bans go live.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.question_text: Is parking on the left side of a two-way street facing oncoming traffic allowed?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.teaching_text: Pulling across oncoming lanes to park nose-first forces a blind wrong-way merge when leaving.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.question_text: When is non-emergency parking permitted along a state or interstate highway?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.teaching_text: High-speed shoulders exist for breakdowns rather than phone calls, naps, or casual stops.

sec14-card-sec14-F35.question_text: What fine range applies to unauthorized parking along the Massachusetts Turnpike?
sec14-card-sec14-F35.teaching_text: Stopping unnecessarily along the Turnpike invites a fifteen-to-hundred-dollar citation on top of high-speed danger.

sec14-card-sec14-F36.question_text: Where outside town centers is using the roadway itself as a parking spot prohibited?
sec14-card-sec14-F36.teaching_text: Drivers rounding unlit country roads outside thickly settled districts never expect parked cars in live lanes.
sec14-card-sec14-F36.must_match_memory_hook: No roadway parking in rural areas

visual_sync.text_span: No roadway parking in rural areas

sec14-card-sec14-F37.question_text: What does Massachusetts law say about double parking alongside cars already parked at the curb?
sec14-card-sec14-F37.teaching_text: Stopping in the travel lane beside parked cars traps curb vehicles and chokes street flow.

sec14-card-sec14-F38.question_text: May you park on a public street to carry out routine nonemergency vehicle repairs?
sec14-card-sec14-F38.teaching_text: Save oil changes and nonemergency wrenching for private driveways or garages away from moving traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F39.question_text: Who sets most parking-ticket amounts, and what RMV consequence follows unpaid parking tickets?
sec14-card-sec14-F39.teaching_text: Ignoring town parking tickets eventually freezes your driver license or registration renewal at the RMV.

sec14-card-sec14-F40.question_text: What two meter mistakes can earn you a parking citation?
sec14-card-sec14-F40.teaching_text: Both unpaid meters and staying past the posted maximum limit trigger enforcement tickets.

sec14-card-sec14-F41.question_text: What two credentials allow parking on a street marked for resident permits only?
sec14-card-sec14-F41.teaching_text: Without a valid neighborhood sticker or authorized visitor pass displayed, guests get ticketed quickly.

sec14-card-sec14-F47.question_text: How should pedestrians use marked crosswalks and push-button walk signals?
sec14-card-sec14-F47.teaching_text: Pressing the pedestrian button and waiting for the walk phase aligns foot crossings with protected signal timing.

sec14-card-sec14-F48.question_text: What curb stop and three-step look pattern should pedestrians use, even at a one-way street?
sec14-card-sec14-F48.teaching_text: Bicycles, backing cars, or wrong-way drivers can still approach from the unexpected side of one-way streets.

sec14-card-sec14-F49.question_text: Where should a pedestrian pause and check when emerging from between parked vehicles?
sec14-card-sec14-F49.teaching_text: Tall SUVs hide walkers from approaching drivers until you pause at the outer sightline edge.

sec14-card-sec14-F50.question_text: Where must a pedestrian walk when no sidewalk is available along a road?
sec14-card-sec14-F50.teaching_text: Facing approaching headlights lets you see drifting cars first and step clear in time.

sec14-card-sec14-F51.question_text: On which three high-speed highway types is walking along or across strictly forbidden?
sec14-card-sec14-F51.teaching_text: High-speed limited-access highways give drivers zero expectation of pedestrians on shoulders or lanes.

sec14-card-sec14-F52.question_text: What clothing choices help drivers spot pedestrians, especially after dark?
sec14-card-sec14-F52.teaching_text: Dark hoodies blend into wet asphalt at night, whereas retroreflective trim bounces headlight beams right back.

sec14-card-sec14-F53.question_text: May bicyclists use the full travel lane even when a bike lane exists, and where are bikes barred?
sec14-card-sec14-F53.teaching_text: Debris, car doors, or left turns often justify taking the full lane outside signed limited-access highways.
sec14-card-sec14-F53.must_match_memory_hook: Full lane allowed except posted expressways

visual_sync.text_span: Full lane allowed except posted expressways

sec14-card-sec14-R01.question_text: In what direction must bicyclists ride, and how must they treat red lights and stop signs?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.teaching_text: Bicycles follow vehicle direction and intersection stop controls unless dedicated markings direct otherwise.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.question_text: On which side may a bicyclist legally overtake a motor vehicle in the same lane?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.teaching_text: Drivers must check right mirrors before turning because Massachusetts explicitly permits cyclists to pass on the right.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.question_text: Which hand may a Massachusetts cyclist use to signal, and when may a signal be skipped?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.teaching_text: Rough pavement, braking, or tight turns let riders keep both hands on the bars for stability.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.question_text: Where may a bicyclist legally ride on a sidewalk in Massachusetts?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.teaching_text: Downtown storefront zones bar sidewalk riding, and local town bylaws can restrict additional streets.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.question_text: What yielding and sound rules apply to cyclists passing pedestrians on sidewalks or shared paths?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.teaching_text: A friendly bell or voice warning alerts walkers, whereas whistles and sirens are barred on bikes.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.question_text: How many cyclists may ride side by side, and what rule applies on multilane same-direction roads?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.teaching_text: Riding three wide is illegal, and pairs must stay within a single lane without needlessly blocking passes.
sec14-card-sec14-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Max two abreast inside one lane

visual_sync.text_span: Max two abreast inside one lane

sec14-card-sec14-R07.question_text: How should bicyclists manage spacing from other riders and speed near busy crosswalks?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.teaching_text: Leaving room between wheels and easing speed near busy crossings prevents chain-reaction bike spills.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.question_text: What seating equipment must every bicycle rider and passenger use?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.teaching_text: Perching a friend on handlebars or rear pegs throws off steering balance and breaks state law.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.question_text: Which young children require an upright harnessed baby bike seat with spoke protection?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.teaching_text: Toddlers one through four or up to forty pounds need harness support plus guards keeping feet out of spokes.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.question_text: What physical fit requirement lets a passenger ride on a tandem bicycle seat?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.teaching_text: A rider too short to grip the bars and plant feet on pedals cannot stabilize a tandem.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.question_text: At what young age is a child completely barred from being carried on a bicycle?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.teaching_text: Infants younger than twelve months lack the neck strength to handle road vibration or helmet weight.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.question_text: Under what age must bicycle riders and passengers wear a secured approved helmet, and what is the exception?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.teaching_text: Riders under sixteen need a buckled CPSC-approved helmet unless riding inside a head-protecting enclosed trailer.

sec14-card-sec14-R13.question_text: What condition governs parking a bicycle on a road or sidewalk?
sec14-card-sec14-R13.teaching_text: Laying a bike across curb ramps or narrow sidewalks trips visually impaired walkers and strollers.

sec14-card-sec14-R14.question_text: May a bicycle be pulled by another vehicle, and what is the only thing a bicycle may tow?
sec14-card-sec14-R14.teaching_text: Grabbing onto a moving car causes violent high-speed falls, and bikes may pull only proper trailers.

sec14-card-sec14-R15.question_text: What hand and cargo rule must every bicyclist follow while riding?
sec14-card-sec14-R15.teaching_text: Riding no-handed with bulky bags leaves you helpless when a pothole or car door appears.

sec14-card-sec14-R16.question_text: Within how many feet must bicycle brakes be able to stop from fifteen miles per hour?
sec14-card-sec14-R16.teaching_text: Pair fifteen miles per hour with thirty stopping feet so equipment questions never catch you guessing.

sec14-card-sec14-R17.question_text: Half an hour past sunset until half an hour before sunrise, what bike lights are required?
sec14-card-sec14-R17.teaching_text: Watch the distance difference, with front white visible five hundred feet and rear red six hundred.

sec14-card-sec14-R18.question_text: What side and pedal reflector visibility is required on a bicycle during nighttime hours?
sec14-card-sec14-R18.teaching_text: Moving ankle or pedal reflectors catch cross-street headlights from six hundred feet in every direction.

sec14-card-sec14-R19.question_text: What height and design limits apply to bicycle handlebars and front forks?
sec14-card-sec14-R19.teaching_text: Sky-high ape-hanger bars above shoulder height and stretched custom forks ruin emergency steering leverage.

sec14-card-sec14-R20.question_text: When must a bicyclist report a crash to local police, and what dollar threshold triggers it?
sec14-card-sec14-R20.teaching_text: Notice the bicycle threshold is over one hundred dollars, far lower than the thousand-dollar motor-car threshold.

sec14-card-sec14-R21.question_text: How should a cyclist ride in lanes and adjust speed when legally sharing a sidewalk?
sec14-card-sec14-R21.teaching_text: Holding a steady line helps drivers pass, while dropping to walking pace protects sidewalk pedestrians.

sec14-card-sec14-R22.question_text: How should bicyclists treat cell phones and texting while riding?
sec14-card-sec14-R22.teaching_text: Looking down at a screen on two wheels steals both steering stability and intersection awareness.

sec14-card-sec14-R23.question_text: At least how far from parked cars should a bicyclist ride to clear opening doors?
sec14-card-sec14-R23.teaching_text: A flung-open car door spans roughly three feet, knocking close riders into moving traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-R24.question_text: On which side should you pass other bicycles, and how should you queue at red lights?
sec14-card-sec14-R24.teaching_text: Shoaling ahead of stopped cyclists at an intersection forces awkward re-passing once the light turns green.

sec14-card-sec14-R25.question_text: How should bicyclists approach intersections rather than racing past turning drivers?
sec14-card-sec14-R25.teaching_text: Locking eyes with turning drivers and anticipating sudden hooks beats trying to outrun a bumper.

sec14-card-sec14-R26.question_text: What three rules keep bicyclists safe around tractor-trailers and heavy trucks?
sec14-card-sec14-R26.teaching_text: Passing a moving tractor-trailer on the right puts a cyclist squarely inside a lethal wide-turn blind zone.
sec14-card-sec14-R26.must_match_memory_hook: Give room, blind spots, never right

visual_sync.text_span: Give room, blind spots, never right

sec14-card-sec14-R27.question_text: How should a bicyclist handle passing a transit bus on the right versus on the left?
sec14-card-sec14-R27.teaching_text: Curbside doors and pull-ins trap riders on the right, and buses quickly signal back left into traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-R28.question_text: What headphone or earbud rule applies to bicyclists on the road?
sec14-card-sec14-R28.teaching_text: Blocking both ears muffles approaching sirens, horns, and tire noise behind you.

sec14-card-sec14-R29.question_text: After overtaking a bicyclist, when may a motorist move back toward the right?
sec14-card-sec14-R29.teaching_text: Drifting right too early clips the rider's front wheel or forces them into the curb.

sec14-card-sec14-R30.question_text: What must a driver do before turning right after passing a bicyclist?
sec14-card-sec14-R30.teaching_text: Passing a cyclist just to slam on the brakes and hook right across their wheel causes severe crashes.

sec14-card-sec14-R31.question_text: What must a driver do in a narrow lane behind a bike, and what minimum passing gap applies?
sec14-card-sec14-R31.teaching_text: Massachusetts requires at least four clear feet when overtaking a cyclist, borrowing an adjacent lane if needed.

sec14-card-sec14-R32.question_text: When must a left-turning driver yield to an oncoming bicyclist?
sec14-card-sec14-R32.teaching_text: Treat oncoming bikes like oncoming cars whenever they are inside the intersection or close enough for danger.

sec14-card-sec14-R33.question_text: Does a cyclist's legal position to the right of motor traffic excuse a driver who hits them?
sec14-card-sec14-R33.teaching_text: Since law allows cyclists on the right, drivers carry full responsibility to check before squeezing or turning.

sec14-card-sec14-R34.question_text: Up to how much can a driver or passenger be fined for opening a vehicle door into a cyclist?
sec14-card-sec14-R34.teaching_text: Both drivers and back-seat passengers face up to one hundred dollars for swinging a door into a rider.

sec14-card-sec14-R35.question_text: What simple check must every occupant make before opening a vehicle door?
sec14-card-sec14-R35.teaching_text: A two-second glance backward catches fast-moving bikes and scooters before your door swings into their lane.

sec14-card-sec14-R44.question_text: How does a separated bicycle lane divide traffic, and what color markings may cross intersections?
sec14-card-sec14-R44.teaching_text: Posts, curbs, or parked cars separate riders mid-block while green paint highlights intersection conflict zones.

sec14-card-sec14-R45.question_text: Where must pedestrians walk when a separated bicycle lane runs alongside a sidewalk?
sec14-card-sec14-R45.teaching_text: Stepping into a protected bike lane surprises silent riders who have barriers on both sides.

sec14-card-sec14-R46.question_text: What stop and yield duties apply to drivers turning right across a protected bicycle lane?
sec14-card-sec14-R46.teaching_text: Parked buffer cars can screen bikes until the corner, so stop at the line and yield first.

sec14-card-sec14-R47.question_text: Where must you look before turning across any bicycle lane?
sec14-card-sec14-R47.teaching_text: Side mirrors miss close riders, so look beside and over your shoulder before crossing bike paint.

sec14-card-sec14-R48.question_text: What three rules apply to bicyclists riding through a protected-lane intersection?
sec14-card-sec14-R48.teaching_text: Protected barriers never excuse riding wrong-way, ignoring turning bumpers, or cutting off crosswalk pedestrians.
sec14-card-sec14-R48.must_match_memory_hook: Right direction, watch turns, yield walkers

visual_sync.text_span: Right direction, watch turns, yield walkers

sec14-card-sec14-R49.question_text: What three visual or judgment traps must motorists guard against around bicycles?
sec14-card-sec14-R49.teaching_text: Parked vans hide approaching bikes, and riders often cruise much faster than drivers casually assume.
sec14-card-sec14-R49.must_match_memory_hook: Hidden riders, fast speed, wide space

visual_sync.text_span: Hidden riders, fast speed, wide space

sec14-card-sec14-R36.question_text: What mirror checks and hand choice make up the Dutch Reach when opening a car door?
sec14-card-sec14-R36.teaching_text: Checking inside and side mirrors then reaching across with your right hand prevents sudden dooring crashes.
sec14-card-sec14-R36.must_match_memory_hook: Both mirrors, open with far hand

visual_sync.text_span: Both mirrors, open with far hand

sec14-card-sec14-R37.question_text: What two safety benefits come from opening your car door with the hand farther from it?
sec14-card-sec14-R37.teaching_text: Reaching across naturally pivots your shoulders toward approaching cyclists and keeps the door from flying wide.

sec14-card-sec14-R38.question_text: Does riding inside a painted bicycle lane remove the need to stay three feet from parked cars?
sec14-card-sec14-R38.teaching_text: Curbside bike lanes often run beside parked bumpers, where swinging doors still reach three feet out.
sec14-card-sec14-R38.must_match_memory_hook: Keep three feet even in lanes

visual_sync.text_span: Keep three feet even in lanes

sec14-card-sec14-R39.question_text: What is a bicycle box, where does it sit, and how does it help riders at red lights?
sec14-card-sec14-R39.teaching_text: Sitting ahead of stopped bumpers at red lights lets cyclists line up visibly for turns.

sec14-card-sec14-R40.question_text: Where must motorists stop at a red light that has an empty green bicycle box?
sec14-card-sec14-R40.teaching_text: Rolling onto green bike-box paint is illegal even when zero cyclists are currently waiting.

sec14-card-sec14-R41.question_text: How should a bicyclist use a bicycle box to set up a left turn at a red light?
sec14-card-sec14-R41.teaching_text: Sliding to the left side of the green box places left-turning riders visibly ahead of straight traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-R42.question_text: Where and how should cyclists wait inside a bicycle box when going straight or turning right?
sec14-card-sec14-R42.teaching_text: Waiting staggered on the right keeps the left side open for left-turning cyclists and speeds launch.

sec14-card-sec14-R43.question_text: What two green-light crossings make up a two-stage bicycle left turn?
sec14-card-sec14-R43.teaching_text: Two-stage turns let cyclists avoid weaving across fast multi-lane traffic by crossing straight twice.
sec14-card-sec14-R43.must_match_memory_hook: Cross straight to cross-road box, wait

visual_sync.text_span: Cross straight to cross-road box, wait

sec14-card-sec14-R50.question_text: Who is at fault in the manual's Left Cross bicycle crash scenario, and what must drivers watch for?
sec14-card-sec14-R50.teaching_text: Turning left across oncoming lanes blindsides riders emerging from behind buildings or larger vehicles.

sec14-card-sec14-R51.question_text: Who is at fault in the manual's Right Hook bicycle crash scenario, and what mistake causes it?
sec14-card-sec14-R51.teaching_text: Assuming a cyclist is pedaling slowly tricks drivers into cutting right across a fast-moving front wheel.

sec14-card-sec14-R52.question_text: Who is at fault in a Drive Out bicycle crash, and how can cyclists make themselves more visible?
sec14-card-sec14-R52.teaching_text: Pulling out from driveways or side streets misses curb-hugging bikes, so riding farther left boosts sightlines.

sec14-card-sec14-R53.question_text: Who is at fault in a Sideswipe bicycle crash, and what passing error must drivers avoid?
sec14-card-sec14-R53.teaching_text: Squeezing past inside a tight lane leaves cyclists zero room to dodge potholes or wind gusts.
sec14-card-sec14-R53.must_match_memory_hook: Motorist fault, give full passing room

visual_sync.text_span: Motorist fault, give full passing room
